title: fix(caching): cache empty active-teams result to avoid repeated SELECT
author: robbie-c

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Well-targeted caching fix: introduces a separate populated-marker Redis key to avoid repeated ClickHouse queries when the active-teams set is empty. Logic is correct, atomic (pipeline), and thoroughly tested with parameterized cases for both the marker and TTL behavior.

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: The graphite-app inline comment about stale zset data is fully addressed in this diff — when ClickHouse returns empty, the code now atomically deletes the zset and sets the populated marker in a pipeline. A dedicated test validates this scenario. No remaining showstoppers.

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: The stale-zset concern raised in the inline comment is fully addressed by the atomic pipeline that deletes the zset and sets the populated marker together when ClickHouse returns empty. Logic is correct across both `is_team_active` and `active_teams`, and the new tests thoroughly cover the empty-result, stale-data, and TTL scenarios.

commits.message:
fix(caching): cache empty active-teams result to avoid repeated SELECT

Every signal-fired sync_insight_caching_state.delay() task eventually
reaches is_team_active(team_id), which on a cold redis populates the
recently-accessed-teams zset by running a SELECT against ClickHouse's
events table. When the SELECT returned nothing (a common case: any team
without events in the last 3 days), the existing code returned without
writing to redis, so the next signal firing on the same or another
inactive team re-ran the same SELECT.

In tests this manifested as 12 identical SELECTs per trends test that
calls _create_events (because Organization.bootstrap creates a default
dashboard whose 8 insight tiles each fire two signals). Those queries
shifted snapshot positions and triggered spurious tests-posthog[bot]
snapshot rewrites on unrelated PRs. In production it's pointless
ClickHouse load on every fresh insight-caching-state sync for a quiet
team.

Fix by adding a companion `..._POPULATED` marker key, written on every
populate (including the empty case). is_team_active and active_teams
now check the marker before re-querying. The marker key is independent
of the zset so we don't have to leak a sentinel team into iteration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: robbie-c

commits.message:
fix(caching): pipeline populate writes and trim comments

Pipeline the zset writes and the populated marker so they commit in one
round trip, eliminating the partial-write window where one could land
without the other. Also trim the comments down to one-liners and drop
the test docstrings per repo convention.

reviews.body: ## Pull request overview Fixes Bedrock routing in the LLM gateway’s Anthropic messages path by ensuring LiteLLM can correctly detect the Bedrock provider for regional inference profile IDs (e.g. `us.anthropic.*`), preventing pre-flight 400s that bypass AWS entirely. **Changes:** - Prefix Bedrock model IDs with `bedrock/` before calling `litellm.anthropic_messages` in the Bedrock path. - Keep the unprefixed Bedrock model ID for internal `model` labeling (metrics/log context) and for `strip_server_side_tools` logging to avoid dashboard cardinality changes. - Update/add regression tests to assert LiteLLM receives the prefixed model for mapped Anthropic names and Bedrock inference profile IDs. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | services/llm-gateway/src/llm_gateway/api/anthropic.py | Prefixes Bedrock model IDs with `bedrock/` for LiteLLM routing while preserving unprefixed IDs for internal labeling. | | services/llm-gateway/tests/test_bedrock.py | Updates an existing assertion and adds a parametrized regression test ensuring the `bedrock/` prefix is passed to LiteLLM. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. commits.message:
fix(llma): prefix bedrock model id with bedrock/ for litellm

The bedrock fallback path passed the raw bedrock model id (e.g.
"us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7-v1") to litellm. litellm only pattern-matches
"claude-*" as native Anthropic and can't infer the provider from a regional
inference profile id, so every call 400s with "LLM Provider NOT provided"
before leaving the gateway. Prefix the model with "bedrock/" so litellm
routes to the bedrock provider as intended.

title: fix(web-vitals): ship web-vitals-with-attribution.js bundle to frontend/dist/
author: alex-kozh

commits.message:
fix(web-vitals): ship web-vitals-with-attribution.js bundle to frontend/dist/

posthog-js builds and publishes both `web-vitals.js` and
`web-vitals-with-attribution.js` in its npm `dist/`. PostHog (this repo)
only copies `web-vitals.js` into `frontend/dist/`, so the attribution
bundle is missing from the PostHog CDN.

When `posthog-js` is configured with `web_vitals_attribution: true`
(or the equivalent `capture_performance: { web_vitals_attribution: true }`),
the SDK loads `/static/web-vitals-with-attribution.js?v=<version>`
instead of `/static/web-vitals.js`. On self-hosted PostHog the request
falls through to the SPA catch-all and returns `200 + text/html`; the
browser refuses to execute it as JavaScript and silently drops all
web-vitals callbacks. Same behavior on PostHog Cloud
(`us-assets.i.posthog.com/static/web-vitals-with-attribution.js`
returns `302 /login`).

Add the file to both copy paths used by the build:

- `frontend/bin/copy-posthog-js` — used by the main webpack/CI build.
- `frontend/plugins/vite-posthog-js-plugin.ts` — used by the Storybook
  Vite build, which copies a static allowlist.

`web-vitals-with-attribution.js` is shipped by every recent posthog-js
release (`unpkg.com/posthog-js@latest/dist/web-vitals-with-attribution.js`
returns 200 text/javascript).
commits.author: Aleksandr Kozhevnikov

chore(data-warehouse): disable temporal deadlock detector in data-imports tests

Tests in `posthog/temporal/tests/data_imports/` use `UnsandboxedWorkflowRunner()` so
mocks can run inside the workflow loop, but Temporal's 2s deadlock detector remains
on. Slow MagicMock attribute creation, aiobotocore/aiohttp teardown crossing the
workflow loop, and GC/weakref cleanup can each push a workflow tick over the 2s
ceiling, producing rotating CI flakes (e.g. test_chargebee_customer,
test_customer_io_sender_identities, test_zendesk_sla_policies, test_zendesk_groups).

Setting `debug_mode=True` on the Worker turns off both the sandbox and the deadlock
detector, matching the existing pattern in
`posthog/temporal/tests/test_subscriptions_workflows.py`.

A follow-up should move `get_data_import_finished_metric(...).add(1)` out of the
workflow body and into the `update_external_data_job_model` activity, but that's

title: perf(frontend): defer authenticated shell to lazy chunk
author: pauldambra

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: An unresolved bot comment flags a genuine behavioral change: AI_ONLY_MODE is now only evaluated inside AuthenticatedShell (authenticated users only), whereas it previously applied regardless of auth state. All 13 reviews are from the author's own automated systems with zero independent human sign-off on this behavioral change.

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: The implementation quality is high and all bot-raised concerns were addressed, but this is a core frontend architecture change (lazy-splitting the authenticated shell, new ChunkLoadErrorBoundary, moving kea logic mount points) with zero human review — every one of the 23 review threads is from bots or the PR author's own automation. A human teammate should sign off before merging.

commits.message:
perf(frontend): defer authenticated shell to lazy chunk

Unauthenticated pages (/login, /signup, /oauth/authorize, etc.) parse
and execute the full App tree on first paint - Navigation, Max,
GlobalModals, GlobalShortcuts, command palette, post-onboarding modal,
impersonation notice, and several auth-only kea logics. None of that
renders until user !== null.

Move the user-gated tree into a new AuthenticatedShell component
loaded via React.lazy. The unauthenticated path returns just the
scene element + toast container.

Also:
- defer preWarmDecompression() in index.tsx behind requestIdleCallback
- catch chunk-load failures on the deferred import
- idle-prefetch the AuthenticatedShell chunk once user is known
- wrap Suspense in a ChunkLoadErrorBoundary that reloads once on
  stale-deploy chunk-hash drift, with a 20s localStorage guard
  against reload loops, mirroring sceneLogic's pattern
- use WrappingLoadingSkeleton (#58118) as the Suspense fallback
- eagerly import AuthenticatedShell in storybook's withKea decorator
  so module-level side effects from its eager-imported children
  remain present in the storybook bundle (production unaffected,
  the React.lazy boundary still applies)

Build effects:
- App entry chunk: 245 KB -> 58 KB
- Eager sibling chunks: 45 -> 20

fix(frontend): guard localStorage access in ChunkLoadErrorBoundary

In Safari private-browsing mode, localStorage.setItem throws
QuotaExceededError - which would skip window.location.reload() and
leave the user blank-screened with no recovery path. Wrap both the
read and the write in try/catch so a storage failure degrades
gracefully and we still reload.

title: fix(llma): tag runs list shows empty when data exists
author: andrewm4894

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: The change is a legitimate bug fix with correct escaping logic, but it alters HogQL query construction (switching from parameterized to escaped string interpolation) in a security-adjacent area, and the author is not on the owning team (@PostHog/team-llm-analytics). Needs a sign-off from that team before merge.

commits.message:
fix(llma): tag runs list shows empty when data exists

The runs query combined a `{tagger_id}` placeholder from the `values`
dict with a `{filters}` placeholder. `parse_select` eagerly resolves
all placeholders against `values` before `find_placeholders` runs, so
`{filters}` errors out as missing and the whole query fails. The
runs loader catches the error and silently returns an empty list.

Inline the tagger_id with HogQL string escaping (defense in depth —
it's a UUID from the URL path), matching the `escapeHogqlString`
pattern already used in `traceMessagesLazyLoaderLogic.ts`.

title: fix(approvals): allow role-based approvers to approve change requests
author: gustavohstrassburger

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body:
## Pull request overview Fixes role-based approvers being unable to approve change requests due to UUID-vs-string mismatches when comparing role IDs from `policy_snapshot`/`approver_config` against `RoleMembership.role_id` query results. **Changes:** - Coerce role IDs to strings on both sides of role intersection checks in approvals permissioning and policy evaluation. - Add API and policy-engine tests covering role-based approver authorization and org-boundary behavior. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | posthog/approvals/permissions.py | Normalizes role IDs to strings before intersecting with policy snapshot role IDs. | | posthog/approvals/policies.py | Normalizes role IDs to strings in `_actor_is_approver` to correctly detect approvers via roles. | | posthog/approvals/serializers.py | Normalizes role IDs to strings when computing `can_approve`, with clarifying comment on JSON round-tripping. | | posthog/approvals/tests/test_approvals_api.py | Adds API-level tests ensuring `can_approve` and `approve/` succeed for users in approver roles. | | posthog/approvals/tests/test_policy_engine.py | Adds unit tests for `_actor_is_approver` role matching and org isolation. |
--- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

commits.message:
fix(approvals): allow role-based approvers to approve change requests

Role IDs are stored as strings in policy_snapshot/approver_config (JSON has no UUID type)
but RoleMembership.role_id comes back as uuid.UUID. The set intersection therefore always
missed, hiding the Approve/Deny buttons for role-only approvers and rejecting their POSTs.

feat(insights): dagster backfill for personsOnEventsMode modifier

Adds a Dagster job that persists each team's resolved `personsOnEventsMode`
into `team.modifiers["personsOnEventsMode"]`, eliminating the per-pod
flag-eval variance that fragments query cache_keys across web pods.

Resolution uses `posthoganalytics.get_flags_decision`, which POSTs the team
context to the FF `/flags/` endpoint without consulting the local SDK cache.
Robust against the regional hypercache mis-pointing that motivated the
investigation (the EU worker SDK's HyperCacheFlagProvider points at a
customer project rather than the company project; server-side eval bypasses
that entirely).

Fallback when both PoE flags are False/None is `PERSON_ID_OVERRIDE_PROPERTIES_ON_EVENTS`
(v2), not `JOINED` — flag 8523 has been at 100% rollout for orgs created
after 2024-06-14 so v2 is the canonical modern default.

Idempotent (skips teams whose modifier is already set). `dry_run` op config
logs what would be written without touching the DB. Inherits team_ids /
batch_size / rollout_percentage from the standard `get_all_team_ids_op`.

No production code path changes in this PR — separate follow-up will rip
out `team.person_on_events_mode_flag_based_default` and remove the FF eval
from the cache_key path.

round-trips can always land on their callback scene and run their effects,
even when project onboarding is incomplete.

commits.message:
feat(mcp): render lifecycle insights as stacked bars in the UI app

The MCP `query-results.html` app currently routes lifecycle results through
`TrendsVisualizer`, which falls back to a line graph. The lifecycle UI in
PostHog is a stacked bar chart with `dormant` extending below zero (the
backend already returns dormant counts negated). This adds a dedicated
`LifecycleVisualizer` that:

- Stacks `new` / `returning` / `resurrecting` upward from zero
- Extends `dormant` downward (data already comes in signed)
- Uses the conventional bucket colors from `--color-lifecycle-*`
- Renders a zero-crossing y-axis with ticks on both sides

`Component.tsx` detects lifecycle results before the trends check (lifecycle
items also pass `isTrendsResult`) and falls back to `query.kind === 'LifecycleQuery'`.

commits.message:
fix(mcp): apply toggledLifecycles + drop letterboxed SVG height

Address greptile review on #58004:

- `lifecycleFilter.toggledLifecycles` is a client-side filter in the main
  app — the backend always returns all four buckets and the UI hides the
  toggled-off ones. Mirror that here so a saved insight with
  `toggledLifecycles: ['new', 'returning']` doesn't show resurrecting and
  dormant in the MCP visualizer. Filter applies to bounds, bars, and legend.
- Drop the explicit `height: 420px` on the SVG. The viewBox is 600x320 and
  the explicit height was producing letterboxed empty bands above/below the
  chart. With just `width: 100%`, the SVG scales to its viewBox aspect
  ratio (no distortion, fully responsive).

commits.message:
fix(mcp): include query in non-actors wrapper response payload

The non-actors path in `query-wrapper-factory.ts` was returning only
`{ results, _posthogUrl }` to the UI app — the `query` field was never
propagated. As a result, `LifecycleVisualizer` (and `TrendsVisualizer`)
received `query: undefined`, so query-level filters like
`lifecycleFilter.toggledLifecycles` and `trendsFilter.display` silently
did nothing.

Without the query, the toggled-lifecycles fix from cd1a6a0 was a no-op:
all four buckets always rendered regardless of the filter. With the
query threaded through, the visualizer now correctly hides toggled-off
buckets in bounds, bars, and legend.

perf(ci): update Rust test shard weights from 2-week CI data

- Recalibrate package weights based on actual avg job durations from
  the last 2 weeks (thousands of runs). Key changes:
  - personhog-replica: 49 → 140 (85s integration test was underweighted)
  - personhog-leader: 30 → 115 (1m31s compile was underweighted)
  - k8s-awareness: 60 → 107 (80s integration test)
  - property-defs-rs: 93 → 136 (87s integration test)
  - feature-flags: 241 → 181 (was overweighted)
  - kafka-assigner: 150 → 84 (was overweighted)
  - embedding-worker: 98 → 25 (was heavily overweighted)

- Replace hardcoded TARGET_SHARDS=8 with TARGET_MINUTES=10.
  Shard count is now computed dynamically: ceil(total_weight / 600).
  This means adding new packages won't silently blow past the time
  budget — it will just add more shards automatically.

- With current weights (total 2325s), this produces 4 shards at ~580s
  each, well within the 10-min target per shard.

feat(lemon-table): add bulkSelection prop

Abstracts the bulk-selection pattern (checkbox column + toolbar) into
LemonTable itself via a new `bulkSelection` config. Consumers provide a
`renderActions` render-prop that receives selection context
(`selectedKeys`, `selectedRecords`, `selectedCount`, `clearSelection`,
`setSelectedKeys`) and decides what bulk actions to render. The leading
checkbox column and the bar above the table only appear when the prop is
set, and the bar only shows when something is selected.

Covers: shift-click range select, indeterminate/all-on-page header
checkbox, per-row gating with disabled reasons, and an optional
imperative `handleRef` for callers that need to push selection in from
outside the render slot (e.g. "select all matching across pages").

Migrates the three existing consumers — feature flags, dashboards, and
saved insights — onto the new API. Replaces `BulkActionToolbar` /
`SelectionCheckbox` / `BulkUpdateTagsPopover` / `listSelectionLogic` with
a self-contained `BulkUpdateTagsButton` component that takes
`selectedIds` as a prop. Trims `flagSelectionLogic` to just the bulk
delete + select-all-matching loaders and the result modal state.

Adds 10 unit tests for the selection hook and two storybook variants
(nothing selected, two pre-selected).

title: fix(hogql): resolve person.distinct_id filter under person-on-events
author: thmsobrmlr

commits.message:
fix(hogql): resolve person.distinct_id filter under person-on-events

The special case for `{type: "person", key: "distinct_id"}` filters routed
through `events.person.pdi` to reach the pdi lazy join. Under person-on-events
mode, `events.person` is rebound to the `poe` virtual table, which has no
`pdi` field, so the resolver raised "Field not found: pdi".

Filters of this shape land in team `test_account_filters` and break every
insight runner that applies them when person-on-events is enabled. Route
event-scope lookups straight to the `events.distinct_id` column (no join
needed) and keep `persons.pdi.distinct_id` for person-scope queries.

test(cdp): pin clock for slack cooldown boundary tests

Boundary tests previously read the real wallclock via `dayjs()` and
absorbed up to 5s of CI drift via `SECONDS ± 5` margins — fragile under
slow runners. Switch to `jest.useFakeTimers` with `Date`-only faking so
`dayjs()` returns a fixed `FIXED_NOW`; keep timers real so
`kea-test-utils`' `toFinishAllListeners()` still runs. The fixed clock
lets the boundaries tighten to ±1s.

describe-scoped closure dependency, and remove the tautological

three boundary tests already exercise the constant meaningfully.

feat(cdp): show explicit countdown on slack channel refresh cooldown

`earliestRefresh.from(now)` rendered "a few seconds" for the entire 30s

click to unlock. Replace with `Math.ceil(earliestRefresh.diff(now) /
1000)` so the disabled-reason reads "in 30 seconds" → "in 1 second" and
ticks every second. `ceil` avoids both "in 29 seconds" right after
click (with floor) and "in 0 seconds" while the button is still
disabled.

Tighten the picker's `usePeriodicRerender` from 10s → 1s so the
countdown text actually updates each second instead of jumping in 10s

title: fix(phai): return 403 insufficient_scope on MCP init when OAuth token lacks user:read
author: skoob13

commits.message:
fix(phai): return 403 insufficient_scope when MCP OAuth token lacks a scope needed by init()

OAuth-issued bearer tokens (DCR or CIMD, prefix `pha_`) on the JSON-RPC `initialize`
request returned HTTP 500 / `Internal server error` instead of a structured 403
`insufficient_scope` challenge when the token was missing a scope that MCP `init()`
needs (e.g. `user:read` for `_fetchUser`). Personal API keys (`phx_`) worked because
they are issued with the full scope preset, masking the bug.

Root cause: `_fetchUser` wraps the typed `PostHogPermissionError` with `wrapError`
and throws inside the durable object. The Cloudflare DO RPC boundary serializer
preserves only `name`, `message`, and `stack`; `Error.cause` and the custom
subclass prototype are stripped. The worker-side `findPostHogPermissionError`
walks `cause` looking for an `instanceof` match, finds nothing, and the request
falls through to the generic 500 branch — so MCP-SDK clients never receive the
RFC 6750 §3.1 challenge their `auth()` recovery path needs to prompt re-consent.

Fix: extend `findPostHogPermissionError` with a message-shape fallback that
reconstructs a `PostHogPermissionError` from the literal `Missing PostHog API
scope: 'X'` produced by the constructor — the one piece of information that
survives the boundary. `formatPermissionErrorMessage` now also handles the
empty `url`/`method` case the recovered error carries, so the body stays
readable. Adds a worker-level boundary test plus three unit tests pinning the
fallback contract.
commits.author: skoob13

title: fix(capture): update v1 Retry-After handling for spec parity
author: eli-r-ph

commits.message:
fix(capture v1): emit Retry-After: 1 on retryable error responses

Per the v1 RFC retry handling section, all retryable error responses
should carry a Retry-After header. Today only 429 emits one (with the
fixed value "60"). This expands header emission to cover 408, 500, 503,
504 as well, and switches the value to a flat 1 second on every
retryable response. SDKs are expected to layer their own jittered
exponential backoff on top of the Retry-After floor.

402 (BillingLimitExceeded) is intentionally non-retryable per RFC and
continues to omit the header.

chore(flags): drop has_encrypted_payloads from cached flag responses

title: fix(data deletion): discover materialized columns by comment alone
author: orian

commits.message:
fix(data deletion): discover materialized columns by comment alone

The discover-mat-cols query filtered by `default_kind = 'DEFAULT'` on the
distributed `events` table, but `materialize()` only attaches the DEFAULT
expression to `sharded_events` and only attaches the
`column_materializer::` comment to `events` — so the two facts never
appear on the same `system.columns` row in production. The query
returned zero rows, leaving the clean-temp mutation without any
`mat_<prop>` resets.

Drop the `default_kind` predicate; the comment is a sufficient
identifier (PostHog-specific, with `elements_chain::*` already excluded).

Update the test helper to mirror production (DEFAULT only on
sharded_events, comment only on events) so this class of bug is now
caught by `test_full_job_property_removal_clears_materialized_columns`.

reviews.author: fercgomes
reviews.body: Tested it locally, all good :pinched_fingers:

commits.message:
feat(oauth): show "Redirecting…" screen after authorize

When users click Authorize for native OAuth clients (Cursor, Claude Code, and
similar MCP clients using loopback redirect URIs), the backend POST to
/oauth/authorize/ returns quickly but the browser then sits navigating to
http://localhost:<port>/callback?code=… while the client's local listener
takes its time to respond — and sometimes never does. The original screen
stayed visible the whole time with the Authorize button stuck in a loading
state, so it looked like PostHog was hung.

This swaps the screen to a dedicated "Redirecting to {appName}…" view as
soon as the authorize POST resolves: a spinner, an inline "Click here" link
in case the automatic redirect doesn't fire, and a note that it's safe to
close the window if the client already finished. The same flow handles
native protocol clients (vscode://, cursor://, etc.) which still transition
to the success screen after the existing 100ms delay.

feat(data-table): add absolute/relative time toggle to column header menu

Adds a "Show absolute time" / "Show relative time" toggle to the
DataTable column header menu for date-time columns on events- and
actors-style sources (Activity scene, person profile Events tab,
persons/groups lists).

The user can now flip the timestamp/created_at/last_seen/last_seen_at
columns between "20 hours ago" and the absolute date+time that's
already shown in the existing hover popover, without resorting to a
custom SQL expression column.

Implementation reuses the existing TZLabel timestampStyle prop and
adds a single boolean (showAbsoluteTime) to DataTableNodeViewProps,
threaded through to the cell renderer. The toggle persists in-memory
on the query state for v1; saving to the backend ColumnConfiguration
model is a deliberate follow-up.

Suppress the actors "last hour" pill in absolute mode so it does not
override TZLabel's formatted children.

commits.message:
feat: upgrade openapi spec to 3.1.0

Switch drf-spectacular OAS_VERSION from 3.0.3 to 3.1.0.

OpenAPI 3.1 is based on JSON Schema 2020-12, making Pydantic v2's
native output directly compatible — no conversion needed for nullable
anyOf, const literals, or $ref siblings. The schema fix-up hook is
simplified to only the cleanup that still applies in 3.1: collapsing
single-entry allOf wrappers, stripping vestigial numeric bounds from
ref-only combinator schemas, and normalising empty additionalProperties.

The lint hook's $ref sibling check is removed (3.1 allows siblings) and
is_effectively_nullable is updated to recognise the 3.1 type-array form
("type": ["X", "null"]) in addition to the oneOf/anyOf/NullEnum forms.

https://claude.ai/code/session_016LG9guVedmCaEtnXrubL6a
commits.author: claude

commits.message: Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master' into claude/upgrade-openapi-3.1-6tuGG
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat: collapse 3.1 nullability shapes into idiomatic ts/zod

Two postprocessing fixes for the 3.1 spec output:

- Collapse `oneOf: [{}, {"type": "null"}]` to `{}` in the schema postprocessing
  hook. drf-spectacular's `append_meta` emits this shape for nullable
  JSONFields in 3.1 mode (the equivalent of 3.0's bare `nullable: true`).
  An empty schema already matches any value including null, so the
  combinator is structural noise — and Orval would otherwise translate
  it to `zod.union([zod.unknown(), zod.null()])` instead of
  `zod.unknown()`. Affects 225 fields across the spec.

- Inline `$ref: NullEnum` to `{"type": "null"}` in the preprocessing
  layer. drf-spectacular emits `NullEnum` as a named component for every
  nullable enum, which Orval mirrors as a `NullEnumApi = null` type
  alias and then references in unions like `Status | NullEnumApi | null`.
  The type alias and the trailing `| null` are both redundant once you
  inline. Extends the existing SCHEMAS_TO_INLINE map (also used for
  TimezoneEnum) so each entry carries its substitute schema instead of
  hardcoding `{type: "string"}`.

Net effect: ~5k lines deleted across the regenerated frontend/MCP
clients, with cleaner unions like `Role | "" | null` and zod schemas
like `union([X, zod.null()]).optional()` instead of the verbose
`.union([X, zod.literal(null)]).nullish()` equivalent.

commits.message:
fix(devex): normalise leftover nullable: true to 3.1 form

drf-spectacular's `append_meta` converts `nullable: true` to the 3.1
type-array form for schemas it builds from DRF fields, but it doesn't
run external schemas through that path. Two sources slip through and
end up emitting invalid 3.1 syntax:

- DRF's `get_paginated_response_schema()` hard-codes `nullable: true`
  on the paginator's `next`/`previous` URLs.
- Hand-written `@extend_schema_field` annotations across the codebase
  still use the 3.0 spelling.

Vacuum's `oas3-schema` rule fires on every occurrence (300+ findings).
Add a normalisation pass to the existing schema cleanup hook that
mirrors `append_meta`'s conversion logic. Future leaks get fixed
automatically; manual annotations don't need to be migrated one by one.

Cleaner upstream fixes were considered and rejected: bumping DRF
doesn't help (3.17.1 still hard-codes the flag), drf-spectacular has
no setting to override paginator handling, and subclassing the
default paginator wouldn't catch the manual-annotation case.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(devex): bump orval to 8.9.1 + strip null from path params

Two CI-blocking issues from the 3.1 upgrade, fixed together:

orval 8.0.3 → 8.9.1
-------------------
8.0.3 was the third patch of orval's brand-new openapi 3.1 support and
mishandled `anyOf: [{type: array, items: ...}, {type: null}]`, emitting
`undefinedItem[]` as the array element type. fixed in 8.2.0 (#2886).

bumping to 8.9.1 also resolves a `| null | null` dedup bug (107 cases
collapsed to `| null`) and aligns with how orval handles nullable type
arrays now. main behavioral change: orval 8.9.1 respects the spec's
`requestBody.required` field — drf-spectacular doesn't emit
`required: true` for ~185 POST/PUT endpoints (all-readonly required
fields, or no required fields) and 191 PATCH endpoints (forced
partial=true). these now become optional in generated clients,
matching what the spec actually says.

we accept the change rather than papering over it: PATCH bodies are
genuinely optional per REST semantics, trigger-style POSTs (refresh,
cancel, snapshot) genuinely take no body, and the remaining cases are
spec-quality drift better addressed per-endpoint as fields gain
explicit `required=True`. about 90 frontend files import generated
clients today, so the surface area is small.

path parameter nullability
--------------------------
drf-spectacular propagates the underlying model field's `null=True`
into path-param schemas, which 3.1 surfaces as `type: ["X", "null"]`
and produces `insightId: number | null` in clients. callers could
build `/insights/null/sharing/` urls. add a postprocessing helper that
strips the null branch from any path-param schema (28 cases) — path
segments are never legitimately null.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(devex): import tests from submodules to avoid orval barrel

orval 8.9.1's package.json declares a "development" export condition
pointing to ./src/index.ts, which isn't shipped in the published
package — only ./dist/index.mjs is. Vitest's resolver picks up the
"development" condition by default, so any test that loads `orval` at
import time fails with `Failed to resolve entry for package "orval"`.

The tests don't actually exercise orval — they only test schema,
preprocess, and exclusions helpers. They were going through index.mjs
(barrel), which re-exports `runOrvalParallel` and that pulls orval in.
Switch tests to import directly from `../src/<module>.mjs` so the
barrel (and orval with it) never gets loaded.

Cleaner than overriding vitest's resolve conditions, and means tests
keep working through any future orval packaging churn.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(devex): hide deprecated symbol_sets endpoints + null assert in test

Frontend typecheck caught real downstream consequences of the optional
requestBody change:

- error_tracking symbol_sets ViewSet exposes create/update/partial_update
  via ModelViewSet, but its serializer is entirely read-only — there are
  no fields a client could set. orval 8.9.1 generates functions with a
  declared body param that never gets used (empty FormData), tripping

commits.message:
fix(data-table): sort by aliased SQL expression columns

Sorting a DataTable column with a multi-word alias (e.g.
formatDateTime(...) as "Absolute Time") failed with
"Unable to resolve field: Absolute" because the resolved alias name was
written straight into ORDER BY, where HogQL tokenized it on whitespace.

Look up the underlying SELECT expression by alias and ORDER BY that
expression instead — events ORDER BY does not resolve SELECT aliases by
name. Also extend extractAsAlias to recognize double-quoted aliases (per
HogQL grammar) and fix isDescOrderBy detection that only matched
" DESC" while the click handler actually emits "\n DESC".

Task-Id: 70811a05-ff37-434d-90ba-8ccba153415e

commits.message:
fix(data-table): normalize hogQl when preserving sort across column edit

Address a regression Copilot flagged on the column-edit handler:
when the user replaces a sorted column via the TaxonomicPopover, the
preserved orderBy value used the new hogQl verbatim with " DESC" appended.

If the new expression has a trailing "-- comment" the appended DESC was
swallowed by the comment, and if it had an "AS <alias>" suffix the
ORDER BY parser hit the same alias-resolution failure this PR fixes.

Strip the AS clause via removeAsAlias and switch to "\n DESC" so the
DESC token survives any trailing line comment.

Also restructure the orderByForSelectKey tests to use it.each, matching
the parameterised style used by the rest of the file (greptile nit).

fix(shared-views): isSharedView reads window.POSTHOG_EXPORTED_DATA

The new playwright network-leak assertion (commit 8d58198) caught a real bug
that was masking the entire shared-views skipping fix:

trackFileSystemLogView is called inside a leaf component's useEffect. React
fires child effects before parent ones, so the BindLogic wrapping <Exporter>
hasn't mounted exporterViewLogic yet by the time the gate runs. isSharedView()
asked kea, kea said "not mounted" -> returned false -> POST fired anyway.

worked because their loaders run async (by the time the API call lands the
logic is mounted), but useFileSystemLogView fires synchronously inside the
useEffect, so it leaked.

sets that global before React boots, so the check is synchronous and immune
to mount ordering. Falls back to the kea check for non-exporter contexts
(Storybook, jest) where the global isn't injected.

title: feat(property-values): rebuild text index with lowercase preprocessor
author: andyzzhao

commits.message:
feat(property-values): rebuild text index with lowercase preprocessor

Adds preprocessor = lower(property_value) to property_values'
idx_property_value text index so case-insensitive autocomplete queries
can engage it. The previous index was case-sensitive ngrams, which the
production ILIKE-based query path bypasses entirely.

Migration steps: drop the existing index, add the new one with the
preprocessor, materialize so existing parts pick up the new definition.
On prod the storage table is currently empty (consumer was broken until
the previous fix shipped, and pipelines are paused), so materialize is
fast. On dev with ~5M rows it takes a short while but does not block
inserts or queries.

The new index engages for hasAnyTokens(property_value, ['term']) and
plain LIKE '%lowercase_term%'. ILIKE itself still does not engage the
index because the optimizer does not recognize the equivalence with the
preprocessor. The autocomplete API will need a separate change to
either pre-lowercase user input and use LIKE, or switch to hasAnyTokens.

fix(tasks): make activity tests survive cross-thread asyncify

Tests for asyncified activities relied on `sync_to_async` running on the
calling thread (thread_sensitive=True), so the activity could see data
created inside the test's pytest-django transaction. With
thread_sensitive=False the activity runs on a worker thread with its own
connection that sits outside that transaction, and lookups raise
`TaskNotFoundError` even though the row was created in setup.

actually committed and visible across threads. Also extract the inner
`connections.all().close()` loop into `_close_initialized_connections`
and repoint the unit tests there — the previous patch target
(`close_old_connections`) was removed when we switched to

title: fix(signals): Consume `UserIntegration` on par with `Integration` for sandboxes
author: sortafreel

reviews.author: sortafreel
reviews.body:
# ReviewHog Report ## Refactoring **Files:** `posthog/models/github_integration_base.py`, `posthog/models/integration.py` **Issues:** 2 issues
What were the main changes
- Moves shared GitHub token access, authenticated API GET, retry/rate-limit handling, and async cache listing helpers from the team-bound GitHubIntegration implementation into GitHubIntegrationBase. - Keeps team Integration behavior available while making the same helpers usable by UserGitHubIntegration. - This is the foundational refactor that later chunks depend on for user-level GitHub integration support.
Full analysis
This chunk centralizes shared installation-authenticated GitHub behavior in `GitHubIntegrationBase` so the same API helpers can be used by both the existing team-scoped `GitHubIntegration` wrapper and the newer user-scoped `UserGitHubIntegration` wrapper. The refactor removes duplicate implementation from `posthog/models/integration.py` while preserving the team-specific refresh hooks in `GitHubIntegration`, such as clearing integration errors, incrementing OAuth refresh metrics, and reloading plugin workers after a successful token refresh. Implementation-wise, `posthog/models/github_integration_base.py` now imports `database_sync_to_async` and owns `get_access_token`, secondary rate-limit detection, retry-after parsing, `_gh_api_get`, and `list_all_cached_repositories_async`. `_gh_api_get` validates GitHub API paths, builds the `https://api.github.com` URL, performs authenticated GETs through the instrumented `_github_api_get`, refreshes expired tokens, retries once for network failures, 401s, and transient 502/503/504 responses, and converts rate limits, non-2xx responses, non-JSON bodies, or unexpected payload shapes into `GitHubIntegrationError` with structured fields for callers. Architecturally, this makes `GitHubIntegrationBase` the shared contract for repository listing and low-level GitHub API access. That matters for downstream integration points such as `GitHubRepositoryFullCache`, signals repository selection, and task repository resolution, where code can work against a `GitHubIntegrationBase` without caring whether credentials came from a team `Integration` row or a user `UserIntegration` row. The trade-off is that the base class now assumes its `integration` object exposes common fields like `id`, `config`, `sensitive_config`, `repository_cache`, `repository_cache_updated_at`, and `repository_cache_entries`, which is satisfied by both current model types and enables later chunks to add user-level GitHub support without duplicating GitHub API behavior.
## Data model **Files:** `posthog/models/integration_repository_cache.py`, `posthog/migrations/1146_integrationrepositorycacheentry_user_integration.py` **Issues:** 4 issues
What were the main changes
- Extends IntegrationRepositoryCacheEntry so cache rows can belong to either a team Integration or a UserIntegration, enforced by an XOR check constraint. - Replaces the old unique_together with conditional unique constraints for integration/full_name and user_integration/team/full_name. - Updates GitHubRepositoryFullCache to accept GitHubIntegrationBase, require a team_id for user integrations, and scope reads, writes, and orphan eviction by team.
Full analysis
This chunk updates the GitHub repository heavy-cache data model so it can store cache rows for both legacy team-scoped GitHub integrations and the newer user-scoped GitHub integrations used by PostHog Code or Signals flows. `IntegrationRepositoryCacheEntry` now has two nullable ownership foreign keys, `integration` and `user_integration`, while keeping `team` denormalized so HogQL and application reads can still scope rows directly by team. The new migration makes the existing `integration` FK nullable, adds `user_integration`, replaces `unique_together` with conditional unique constraints, and adds an XOR check constraint so every row belongs to exactly one integration owner type.
## Business logic **Files:** `products/signals/backend/report_generation/select_repo.py`, `products/signals/backend/temporal/agentic/__init__.py`, `products/signals/backend/temporal/agentic/select_repository.py` **Issues:** 4 issues
What were the main changes
- Adds GitHub source resolution for Signals that prefers a team GitHub integration and falls back to a GitHub UserIntegration from a user with team access. - Updates repository selection to use the shared GitHub integration interface and hydrate/read the repository cache with the current team scope. - Changes sandbox user selection so user-level GitHub integrations can drive agentic repository discovery, while cleanly returning a no-repo result when no GitHub source exists.
Full analysis
This chunk makes Signals repository selection work against a unified GitHub integration abstraction instead of assuming every team has a team-scoped `Integration`. `products/signals/backend/report_generation/select_repo.py` now resolves a single GitHub source through `resolve_team_github_integration(team_id)`, preferring the first team-level GitHub integration and falling back to the first GitHub `UserIntegration` owned by an active user with access to the team. The implementation keeps the previous two-stage repository selection architecture: first resolve/list/cache/filter repositories deterministically, then invoke the sandbox agent only when multiple eligible candidates remain. `GitHubRepositoryFullCache(github, team_id=team_id)` is now created with an explicit team scope, which is important because user-scoped GitHub integrations are not inherently tied to one team and their repository-cache rows are keyed by `user_integration`, `team`, and `full_name`. commits.message:
chore(devex): add semgrep rule blocking manual api.* calls in product frontends

Manual api.<verb>(...) calls in products/*/frontend bypass the generated
client (Orval-emitted from the OpenAPI spec) and the typed schemas that
come with it. New code should use the generated functions; existing call
sites are tagged with `// nosemgrep: prefer-codegen-api` so CI stays green
and adoption can happen incrementally — `rg "nosemgrep: prefer-codegen-api"`
is the live worklist.

The rule message points agents at the `adopting-generated-api-types` skill
for the migration workflow and humans at `hogli product:maturity --codegen`
for per-call-site suggestions.

Runs in a dedicated semgrep-products-frontend job rather than expanding the
existing semgrep-js scan to products/ — the broader JS/security packs would
surface a long tail of un-triaged findings on product code that's outside
the scope of this rule.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(semgrep): anchor prefer-codegen-api include path to repo root

Silences the Semgrepignore v2 deprecation warning. The pattern was meant
to match products/ at the repo root, so the leading slash makes that
explicit instead of relying on the soon-to-change unanchored interpretation.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(semgrep): catch nested generics, narrow products job to single rule

Two reviewer concerns:

1. Generic-type fallback regex `<[^>]*>` stops at the first `>`, so
   `api.get<PaginatedResponse<Foo>>(...)` slipped through. Bound the type
   args by `(` instead so nested generics still match. Confirmed against
   real instances in frontend/ that the pattern would otherwise miss.

2. The semgrep-products-frontend job loaded all of `.semgrep/rules/`,
   meaning a future no-direct-fuse-instantiation or require-iframe-sandbox
   violation in product code would surface under a job named after our
   rule. Pin the config to prefer-codegen-api.yaml — when more
   product-specific rules land, extend the list explicitly.

title: fix(hog-charts): clip y-axis at 0 when only an overlay dips negative
author: sampennington

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Self-contained internal charting library refactor — all old property names are confined to the `hog-charts` directory, all 15 affected files are covered by the diff, and no external consumers use the renamed API. Logic inversions and the new overlay-aware scale behavior are correctly implemented and well-tested.

commits.message:
fix(hog-charts): clip y-axis at 0 when only an overlay dips negative

A backward-extrapolated trend line whose projection drops slightly below 0
was dragging the y-axis baseline well below zero — d3.nice() applied to a
slightly-negative min produces a disproportionately large negative tick
(e.g. domain [-1, 14500] expands to [-5000, 20000]).

Auxiliary overlays (trend lines, moving averages, CI bands) are now tagged
via a top-level Series.overlay flag and excluded from the y-axis baseline
calculation when the primary data is non-negative. They still contribute
to the max so an upward overlay still expands the axis.

Also renames the visibility flags for clarity:
- visibility.fromTooltip: true → visibility.tooltip: false
- visibility.fromValueLabels: true → visibility.valueLabel: false
- visibility.fromStack: true → top-level Series.overlay: true

commits.message:
fix(hog-charts): clip line chart data drawing to the plot area

Without a canvas clip, an overlay series with values outside the y-domain
(e.g. a trendline projecting below 0 after the axis baseline got clipped to
0) bled into the x-axis label gutter beneath the chart.

width past their center pixel. Pad the clip by 8px on top/bottom to fit

reviews.body: No showstoppers. All reviewer concerns were addressed in the current diff, changes are frontend-only UX improvements within a single product area, and the author is on the owning team.

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): rename "Layout shift" chip to "Subtle change"

The SSIM-tier classifier catches any perceptual change where few pixels
differ — text edits, color tweaks, font rendering shifts — not just
spatial layout rearrangements. "Layout shift" was misleading for these
cases and made users question the classification on obvious text-only
diffs.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): show pixel diff % on structural changes, rename to "Perceptible change"

Previously the structural tier hid the pixel diff percentage and showed
raw SSIM (0.949) — confusing because it points the opposite direction
from pixel diff % and the scales aren't comparable.

Now structural snapshots show the real pixel diff % alongside a
"Perceptible change" label. The low % is truthful and the label explains
why it's flagged despite the small number. Both tiers use the same
metric so the overview can average across them.

Also converts the SSIM value in pixel-tier tooltips from raw score to
dissimilarity percentage to match the "higher = more changed" direction.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): always show pixel diff % on structural chips

The display floor doesn't apply here — even 0.0% is meaningful context
next to "Perceptible change" since it reinforces how few pixels actually
differ. Legacy rows with NULL diff_percentage still show label-only.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): increase filmstrip tile size and sidebar width by 20%

Filmstrip tiles: 104×72 → 125×86, label area 108 → 130.
Sidebar: w-52 (208px) → 250px.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat(visual-review): separate quarantine banners for light and dark variants

The snapshot history page already shows light/dark side by side, but
quarantine status only reflected the identifier from the URL. Now both
theme variants get independent banners with their own status and
unquarantine action, rendered in a two-column grid matching the timeline
layout. Non-themed identifiers still get a single banner.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): refresh sibling quarantine state after quarantine action

The quarantineIdentifier listener only reloaded the primary entry,
leaving the sibling column stale after quarantining with "Also
quarantine sibling" enabled.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): clamp SSIM and show <0.1% for sub-floor diffs

Clamp SSIM to [0,1] before converting to dissimilarity % to avoid
negative values from floating point edge cases. Show "<0.1%" instead of
"0.0%" for very small structural diffs so the chip doesn't read as
"no change."

commits.message:
feat(flags): require remote configuration for encrypted payloads

Encrypted payloads are only valid on remote configuration flags.
This constraint is enforced at both the model and serializer levels:
- Model.clean() validates at the database layer
- Serializer validates during API requests (create/update)

Tests verify that:
- Creating a flag with encrypted payloads but is_remote_configuration=False fails
- Creating a flag with both encrypted payloads and is_remote_configuration=True succeeds
- Updates similarly enforce this constraint
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(flags): backfill flags violating encrypted-payload invariant

Clears has_encrypted_payloads on existing flags where
is_remote_configuration is false. Required before the validation added
in the parent commit lands, otherwise edits to those rows would be
rejected. All affected rows have empty payloads, so the flip is
lossless.
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(flags): fix encrypted payloads on template switch and partial update

When switching a remote config flag to a different template, the frontend
now clears has_encrypted_payloads and filters.payloads so the flag stays
consistent. The backend update serializer is also made defensive: a PATCH
that omits filters.payloads preserves the existing encrypted value instead
of crashing with KeyError.

Includes parameterized tests covering filters omitted, payloads omitted,
missing true key, and redacted placeholder scenarios.
commits.author: haacked

commits.message: test(backend): update query snapshots
commits.author: tests-posthog[bot]

commits.message:
fix(flags): tighten encrypted-payload invariant per copilot review

- Resolve `has_encrypted_payloads` against the instance in update() so a
  partial PATCH that omits the boolean still encrypts a fresh plaintext
  payload instead of writing it as plaintext on an "encrypted" row.
- Strip leftover ciphertext when a PATCH downgrades the flag, regardless
  of whether the client also sent filters. Without this the bit flips to
  false but `filters.payloads.true` retains the prior ciphertext, which
  redaction then exposes as a normal payload.
- Partition the backfill migration so only rows with empty
  `filters.payloads.true` get flipped; rows with non-empty payloads are
  logged for manual review instead of silently exposing ciphertext.
  No-op against PostHog Cloud (verified all violating rows are empty);
  defensive for self-hosted installs.
- Document on FeatureFlag.clean() that Django does not invoke it from
  save(); the API path is gated by the serializer validator.

Adds tests covering the partial-downgrade clear and the
boolean-omitted-but-payload-supplied encryption path.
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(flags): align empty-string handling across encrypt/preserve/downgrade

The encrypted-stay-encrypted branch checked `is None`, while the new
downgrade branch used truthiness. An empty string in `payloads.true`
slipped past the first check and fell through to the encryption path.

The public API can't actually land `""` here (validate_filters rejects
it as invalid JSON upstream), but direct serializer callers could, so
align both paths on the same predicate.
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(tasks): include tasks task queue in liveness interceptor

The tasks worker exposes a /healthz liveness probe (port 8011) backed by
LivenessTracker. Timestamps are only updated by LivenessInterceptor, but
the tasks task queue was not in LivenessInterceptor.task_queue, so the
interceptor was filtered out for that worker. The tracker stayed at
process-start time and the probe began returning 503 after 30 minutes
of idle, killing the container mid-flight every ~30 minutes and causing
downstream activity timeouts and "workflow not found" heartbeats.

commits.message:
chore(flags): add redis-cli and awscli to rust-jumphost image

Add a runtime-jumphost Docker build stage that layers redis-tools and awscli
on top of the shared runtime stage. The flags-cache-warmer image opts into
this variant via `target:` in rust-images.yml, giving operators shell access
to inspect Redis and S3 cache state from a claimed jumphost pod.

Other Rust services continue building the smaller runtime stage (default
behavior when target is unset). No impact on build times or image sizes for
non-jumphost services.
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(flags): keep default rust Dockerfile target as the minimal runtime stage

Without a trailing no-op stage, `runtime-jumphost` was the last stage in
the file, so any build that omits `--target` (canary-flags-enable.yml,
ad-hoc `docker build`, the empty default in `_rust-build-images.yml`)
would silently produce the heavier jumphost image. Adding
`FROM runtime AS default` keeps the implicit final target equivalent to
`runtime`; the jumphost image is still produced when explicitly opted
into via `target: runtime-jumphost` in `.github/rust-images.yml`.

docs(skills): fold polar-source lessons into implementing-warehouse-sources

Eight items surfaced while implementing the Polar source that the
existing skill didn't cover. Adding them inline so future authors don't
hit the same traps:

- Don't import or instantiate Batcher in the source layer; the pipeline
  framework batches yielded items at the same thresholds.
- Use urllib.parse.urlencode for URL building instead of
  requests.Request().prepare() with an unreachable f-string fallback.

  timestamp filter; client-side cursor with full fetch is misleading
  for users on row-based billing.
- Honor inputs.incremental_field; INCREMENTAL_FIELDS per-endpoint is
  the menu of options, not the runtime default.
- Per-endpoint sort enums vary; verify each list endpoint with curl
  before hardcoding (Polar's subscriptions rejects sorting=created_at).
- Specify ?sorting= explicitly when destination row order matters; API
  defaults differ across endpoints on the same provider.
- Distinguish 401 (invalid token) from 403 (valid token, scope
  missing) at source-create; accept 403 so users can grant scopes per
  endpoint instead of all-or-nothing. Re-raise 403 for per-schema
  validation through the incremental_fields action.
- Document required token scopes in the caption so users don't grant
  the full set defensively.

chore(tasks): bump sandbox TTL to 6h and inactivity timeout to 2h

Now that the process_task workflow uses user-to-server tokens, runs are
less impacted by token expiries — bump the bounds back up:

- Sandbox TTL: 2h → 6h (max lifetime from boot to close)
- Workflow inactivity timeout: 5m → 2h

chore(tasks): cap sandbox TTL at 15 min during tests

The 6-hour production sandbox TTL is appropriate for real agent runs but
acts as a long safety-net leak in CI: if an integration test that creates
a real Modal sandbox crashes before its cleanup, the orphaned sandbox
stays alive for 6 hours and burns Modal capacity. Tests now use a 15-min
default TTL via settings.TEST so any orphan auto-destroys quickly.

commits.message:
fix(tasks): bound follow-up HTTP timeout below activity start-to-close

The send_followup_to_sandbox activity used SANDBOX_TTL_SECONDS as its
HTTP timeout, but the activity itself has a 35-minute start_to_close
timeout in the workflow. Once the sandbox TTL goes to 6h, a hung
requests.post would keep a worker thread blocked for hours after
Temporal has already abandoned the activity, starving the worker pool.

Decouple the two: introduce FOLLOWUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30 min,
bounded under the 35-min activity timeout so a stuck delivery can't
outlive its activity.

commits.message:
fix(property-values): correct kafka named collection and add dev tables

Two fixes to migration 0244's property_values setup.

1. Named collection mismatch on US/EU. 0244 created kafka_property_values
on AUX with the default named collection (msk_cluster), but the WarpStream
pipeline events_json_to_property_values_ws produces clickhouse_property_values
to the warpstream-ingestion VC and the topic does not exist on MSK. The
Kafka engine table currently consumes from a cluster that has no data;
it's only invisible because the pipeline is paused. Drop and recreate
kafka_property_values + property_values_mv on AUX with the corrected
named collection (warpstream_ingestion). Storage table is untouched
(it's empty since the consumer never read anything).

2. Missing tables on DEV. 0244 targets NodeRole.AUX, but dev has no
nodes labeled hostClusterRole=aux (the `aux` cluster name aliases the
4 main posthog hosts which are labeled `data`). The AUX-targeted
operations no-op silently on dev. Create storage, Kafka engine, and MV
on DATA nodes on dev — dev's `aux` cluster aliases to those same hosts
so the existing Distributed proxy resolves correctly.

commits.message:
feat(usage-reports): publish billing usage to s3 + single sqs pointer

Replace the per-org SQS fan-out in `send_all_org_usage_reports` with a
Temporal workflow that gathers ~55 metric queries serially (each its own
retriable activity), persists every intermediate to S3, then aggregates
into gzipped JSONL chunks of 10k orgs. Billing receives a single SQS
pointer per run (on a new `usage_reports_v2` queue) and reads chunks
from S3 instead of consuming 50k+ messages.

Layout follows the standard Temporal module pattern: types / queries /
aggregator / activities / workflow, with storage helpers (including an
async streamed gzipped-JSONL writer) in their own file. Snapshot
queries that ignore the period are quarantined with `kind="snapshot"`
and a disclaimer in the registry. Schedule is cloud-only and runs at
04:45 UTC, an hour after the existing Celery beat, to give ClickHouse
breathing room while both flows run side by side.

Cleanup of intermediate per-query files is intentionally not yet wired
up so the artifacts stick around in S3 for debugging during validation.

refactor(usage-reports): split snapshot vs period query signatures

`QuerySpec.fn` is now a union of `PeriodFn = (begin, end) -> Any` and
`SnapshotFn = () -> Any`. The activity branches dispatch on

that were previously wrapped in `lambda _b, _e: fn()` now reference
the underlying function directly.

Two new registry tests guard the contract: period specs must take
exactly two required args, snapshot specs must take zero. This means
"fix this snapshot to honor the period" becomes a typed migration
(change `kind` and the signature shifts under it) rather than an
easy-to-miss search.

first time the worker registers the schedule, killing the cloud daily

commits.message:
perf(usage-reports): batch jsonl bytes before handing to gzip stream

`JsonlGzipWriter.write` previously called `self._gz.write` twice per
line (once for the JSON payload, once for the newline). With 10k orgs
per chunk that's 20k gzip method calls — small, but the per-call
overhead adds up while the activity is sync-running on the event loop
under `Heartbeater`.

Buffer encoded JSONL bytes in a local `bytearray` and flush to the gzip
stream in 256 KiB batches. `_finalize` drains whatever's still pending,
so the on-the-wire output is byte-identical (the existing roundtrip
tests pin this).

commits.message:
chore(devex): make playwright e2e opt-in to cut ci cost

Playwright e2e is one of the most expensive workflows. Empirically the
failures are mostly flakes rather than real bugs and most regressions
are caught earlier (ci-backend, jest, typecheck, storybook VR) or fix
forward from master. Pay less for it.

- Drop runner depot-ubuntu-latest-16 to -8. Observed ~18% avg / 30%
  peak memory on 16-core runs; #46853 already noted the workload
  isn't resource constrained. The 16-core was a flake-fix experiment
  from #40314 that was never revisited.
- Path filter goes narrow: only playwright/** and the workflow file
  trigger automatically. Other code paths (frontend, posthog, deps,
  compose) post a suggest-label comment nudging the author to add the
  run-playwright label if they want a sweep. Runner only spins up on
  real signal or explicit opt-in. Master push always runs.
- Restore the postgres schema from the same Actions cache ci-backend
  produces (keyed on merge-base), skipping the ~3 min Django migrate
  step on most PRs. Cache miss falls back to a full migrate.

Refactor: rename hogli db:restore-test-db to db:restore-schema-fresh
with a TARGET_DB env var (defaults to test_posthog, so existing
callers in ci-backend / ci-dagster keep working).

Pre-merge: the run-playwright label needs to be created in repo
settings.

reviews.body: Well-crafted prompt injection defense with correct sanitization ordering (invisible Unicode stripped before tag regex, iterative loop handles arbitrary nesting, U+2028/U+2029 collapsed by explicit regex). Two human approvals, all review comments resolved, comprehensive test coverage. No data model, API contract, or infrastructure changes.

commits.message:
fix(subscriptions): sanitise user text in AI summary prompts

The AI subscription summary already protected the user-provided
`summary_prompt_guide` from prompt injection (tag stripping +
`<user_context>` wrapping + meta-prompt). The data being summarised
did not get the same treatment. Insight names, descriptions, series
labels, funnel step names, retention cohort labels, subscription
titles, and HogQL row values all flowed into the LLM prompt
unescaped. A user could embed `</user_context>` to close the guide
tag, `<system>` to fake a system turn, or `\n### Header` to mimic
the section structure used to delimit per-insight data. They could
also smuggle text via zero-width / RTL Unicode chars, or via NEL
(U+0085) which some tokenizers treat as a line separator.

Introduce `sanitize_user_text(value, max_len)` in a new module that
strips control chars and dangerous Unicode (zero-width, RTL/LTR
overrides, BOM, NEL) FIRST, then runs two tag-strip passes (so
unicode-stripped fragments forming a new tag get caught), collapses
newlines and whitespace runs, and truncates per-field. Apply at the
LLM-prompt-build boundary.

Wrap each previous/current data section in `<insight_data>` tags
and the subscription title in `<subscription_title>` tags. Update
both fallback system prompts to call out every wrapper.

Replace the parallel `_sanitize_prompt_guide` (tag-only, weaker)
with a single call to `sanitize_user_text` with a dedicated
`PROMPT_GUIDE_MAX_LEN`, so all user-controlled prompt input shares
one hardened helper.

commits.message:
fix(subscriptions): loop tag-strip until stable to defeat nested escaping

Two passes catches `<<sys>tem>` (where the outer-`<` plus the
post-strip `tem>` form a new tag), but a determined attacker can
nest deeper: `<<<sys>tem>tem>` needs three passes, depth-N needs N.
Replace the fixed two-pass with a `while previous != cleaned`
loop so the strip runs until the regex finds nothing to remove,
making the defence depth-independent.

commits.message:
fix(subscriptions): close three remaining sanitiser bypasses from security audit

Security audit (Piccirello via /security-audit on PR #57625) flagged
three real bypasses in `sanitize_user_text`. All three are now closed:

1. Unclosed structural-tag prefix. `_TAG_RE` requires a closing `>`, so

   slipped through. Add `_LLM_MARKER_RE` matching the known marker
   names with optional `>`, so an unterminated prefix still gets
   stripped.

2. Whitespace between `<` and tag name. `<\tsystem>` was preserved
   because `\t` doesn't satisfy `[a-zA-Z_]`. The new `_LLM_MARKER_RE`
   uses `</?\s*<marker>` so any whitespace between the angle and the
   marker name is consumed.

3. Invisibles outside `Cf`/`Cc`. Combining marks (`\u034f`), Hangul
   fillers (`\u115f`, `\u1160`, `\u3164`), variation selectors
   (`\ufe00-\ufe0f`, Mongolian `\u180b-\u180d`, supplement
   `\ue0100-\ue01ef`) are categories `Mn` / `Lo` and were not stripped.
   Replace the regex-based unicode strip with a character-by-character
   pass that drops `Cc`/`Cf` plus an explicit set of these
   default-ignorable code points.

Three new parametrised test classes exercise every bypass — every
known LLM marker tag in unclosed form, the whitespace-prefix variants,
and ten extended invisible code points.

fix(subscriptions): collapse U+2028/U+2029 line separators

The previous `_DANGEROUS_UNICODE_RE` covered range \u2028-\u202f, which
included LINE SEPARATOR (Zl) and PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR (Zp). When the
unicode strip moved to a Cc/Cf category check those two slipped through
because they're Zl/Zp. The other characters in that old range (Cf RTL/
LTR overrides) are still caught by the category strip.

Add U+2028 and U+2029 to `_NEWLINE_RE` so they collapse to a space the
same way `\n` and `\r` do — same defence against `\n### Fake header`
injection, just for the Unicode line terminators.
