commits.message:
feat(visual-review): split pixel diff and ssim, add change kind and clusters

The two-tier classifier was overloading `diff_percentage`: pixel diff %
when the pixel tier triggered, SSIM dissimilarity % when the SSIM tier
triggered. Same column, different meanings — humans reading the run scene
saw "1.5% diff" on snapshots that were below the pixel threshold and
couldn't tell which signal it represented.

Going forward `diff_percentage` always means pixel diff %, with three new
companion fields:

- `ssim_score` (0.0–1.0, 1.0 = identical) — populated for every diffed
  snapshot regardless of which tier classified it.
- `change_kind` — categorical: `pixel`, `structural`, `viewport_mismatch`.
  The kind is the source of truth for rendering; numbers are details.
- `diff_metadata` — JSONB column governed by the `DiffMetadata` Pydantic
  model (writes via `.model_dump()`, reads via `.model_validate()`).
  Holds `cluster_summary` for spatial clustering output, room for future
  pipeline-derived fields (e.g. engine version stamp) without schema
  migrations. Kept separate from the existing `metadata` column so user-
  provided ingestion context doesn't collide with system-computed output.

`viewport_mismatch` is a new signal lifted from the new pixelhog API.
Different baseline/current dimensions used to silently produce a giant
inflated diff % dominated by padded pixels; now the classifier flags it
as its own kind and downstream callers can render it separately.

Cluster summary uses pixelhog's tuned defaults (`min_pixels=16`,
`min_side=4`, `dilation=4`, `max_clusters=20`) to produce region-level
bboxes a UI can render directly. Skipped for size mismatches and zero-diff
cases where clusters reduce to noise.

Backfill migration repairs existing rows by the `diff_pixel_count = 0`
discriminator the old SSIM tier left behind:

- Pixel-tier rows: just stamp `change_kind = 'pixel'`.
- SSIM-tier rows: derive `ssim_score = 1 - diff_percentage/100`,
  null out `diff_percentage` (we don't have the true pixel diff for
  these), set `change_kind = 'structural'`.
- `diff_metadata` defaults to `{}` for legacy rows; populated only when
  the new pipeline runs.

Also switches `diff.py` from the legacy `pixelhog.compare()` to the new
`Comparison` object — single decode pass shared across diff, ssim, diff
image, thumbnail, and clusters; also exposes the size-mismatch flag.

Pure-function `classify_compare_result()` extracted from `_diff_snapshot`
so unit tests can drive every classification path without touching the DB.

Note: requires pixelhog 1.2.0. uv.lock bump pending the pixelhog release;
this branch is CI-red until that lands. Serializers and frontend are not
updated here — `diff_percentage` becomes nullable for legacy structural
rows, which follow-up PRs will surface as the categorical chip.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat(visual-review): expose ssim_score, change_kind, cluster_summary on snapshot DTO

Snapshot contract gains the new diff classification fields. Cluster
summary uses a friendlier wire shape (`x/y/width/height/pixel_count`)
than the compact storage shape (`bbox: [x,y,w,h], px`); the translation
lives in `_to_cluster_summary`, which routes the raw `diff_metadata`
JSON through the Pydantic validator before mapping to the public DTO.

This keeps the storage layer free to evolve (add keys to `diff_metadata`
without breaking the wire) while the API stays explicit and verbose for
frontend consumers.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
chore(visual-review): regenerate openapi types for cluster summary fields

Auto-generated from the contract additions in the previous commit. Adds
DiffClusterApi, ClusterSummaryApi, and the new SnapshotApi fields
(ssim_score, change_kind, cluster_summary) to both the frontend
generated client and the MCP api types.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat(visual-review): categorical change badge using change_kind

Replaces the old "X% diff" chip that showed pixel-diff percentage on
pixel-tier rows and SSIM dissimilarity percentage on SSIM-tier rows
without telling the user which signal it was. New `SnapshotChangeBadge`
maps `change_kind` to distinct chips:

- `pixel`         -> percentage chip with pulse icon (current behavior,
                     restored to truthful pixel diff %)
- `structural`    -> "Layout shift" — number deliberately hidden because
                     the pixel diff is below the classifier threshold and
                     reading it as a diff fights the user's mental model
- `viewport_mismatch` -> "Viewport mismatch" warning chip — surfaces what
                     used to be silently buried in inflated diff numbers

Tooltips carry the SSIM score and (where available) the cluster count so
users who want the underlying numbers can find them.

Wired into:
- run scene snapshot list (per-row chip alongside the thumbnail)
- snapshot diff viewer (summary header)
- snapshot history scene (per-history-row chip)

`SnapshotHistoryEntry` contract gains `change_kind` and `ssim_score` so
the history view can render the same categorical chip per row;
`cluster_summary` deliberately omitted there since bbox overlays don't
apply to a list view.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat(visual-review): bbox overlays on diff viewer using cluster_summary

VisualImageDiffViewer gains a `diffOverlayBoxes` prop that draws
SVG rectangles over the diff image when in `diff` comparison mode.
SVG uses a viewBox in natural image coords plus
`preserveAspectRatio="none"` so bbox positions stay accurate even when
the browser scales the diff image down to fit the panel.

SnapshotDiffViewer feeds the prop from `snapshot.cluster_summary.items`.
Truncated cluster lists (top-N by pixel count) render the top N as bboxes
and the FE relies on `total` for the categorical "Layout shift" label
in the chip when the diff is highly scattered.

`vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` keeps the outline thickness constant
regardless of zoom, so bboxes stay legible on tiny thumbnails and full-
page screenshots alike.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
refactor(visual-review): treat size mismatch as metadata, not a kind

`viewport_mismatch` was an exclusive ChangeKind, which short-circuited
the classifier and skipped clusters whenever baseline and current had
different dimensions. That conflated two orthogonal things — a snapshot
can have a different viewport AND a real content change.

Pixelhog 1.2.0 already pads the smaller image to the largest dims and
runs pixelmatch / SSIM / clusters over the padded buffers, so we always
have meaningful metrics. The only thing that changes when sizes differ
is that one cluster will cover the new content area, which is the right
answer.

- Drop VIEWPORT_MISMATCH from ChangeKind (kinds are now pixel / structural)
- Compute clusters even when sizes differ
- Add size_mismatch flag to DiffMetadata (Pydantic-governed JSONB)
- Surface it on Snapshot + SnapshotHistoryEntry contracts
- SnapshotChangeBadge renders a separate "Size changed" chip that
  composes with the kind chip
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): align bbox overlay with the diff image

Bboxes are returned by pixelhog in the diff image's natural pixel
space — which equals current/baseline when sizes match and the
*padded* size when they don't. The SVG viewBox was using
current_artifact dims, so on size-mismatch runs the overlay drifted
out of alignment with the visible diff image.

Pass diff_artifact.width/height as separate `diffOverlay{Width,Height}`
props, fall back to the image dims for callers that never had a
mismatch. Also drop the inline-image baseline gap by setting `block`
on the img and `leading-none` on the wrapper, otherwise the SVG
hugs a few pixels lower than the image's actual bottom edge.

Bumps the stroke to a constant 2px (was scaled with image width)
plus a translucent fill so the boxes read against either the diff
heatmap or — once we extend to other modes — the original screenshot.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat(visual-review): add collapsible cluster overview + numbered overlay

Click into a snapshot diff and the change clusters now have somewhere
to live. A LemonCollapse panel above the comparison shows one row per
region — position, size, pixel count, share-of-image — and each row is
mapped to a numbered chip on the image overlay. Hovering a row
emphasizes its bbox and dims the others.

Bbox overlays also render in `blend` mode now, not just `diff`, so
users can see where the changes are without leaving the
baseline-vs-current visual. Skipped when sizes mismatched and the
bbox coord space (padded) doesn't match the underlying image — would
be misleading to draw boxes that point at nothing.

Layout follows the design mockup; the cluster row content is
deliberately lighter (no per-cluster review actions) — those still
live in the existing top-right action bar so this panel stays
informational.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat(visual-review): cluster panel into sidebar, bidirectional hover, toggle

Cluster overview moved into the existing right sidebar (below the
diff minimap) and made always-visible — no LemonCollapse, since the
sidebar already gives it a natural home and the panel is more useful
when it's just there. Compact rows for the 208px sidebar width: orange
numbered chip + position/size/pixel count.

Hover now syncs both directions:
  - row hover → bbox + chip emphasized in the image
  - bbox/chip hover → row emphasized in the panel
Switched the overlay color to the same warm orange the mockup uses,
so panel rows and image chips read as one visual system.

Overlay now also renders on the side-by-side "After" panel (skipped
when sizes mismatched and the bbox coord space wouldn't align), so
the overlay is available in every comparison mode that's meaningful.

Added a small "Clusters" toggle next to the diff % tag in the viewer
toolbar — lets users dismiss the overlay to read the underlying image
clearly without losing the sidebar panel.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): bump cluster dilation 4 -> 8

A list-shift diff (timeline of items shifted vertically) exploded
into 69 clusters at dilation=4 — every text row stayed its own
cluster because the ~13-16px gap between rows was too wide for
4-pixel dilation to bridge. Bumping to 8 closes ~16px gaps and
collapses adjacent text rows + row separators into a single
regional cluster, which is the answer humans actually want when
they say "the list shifted".

Verified across the demo set: small precise diffs (2-cluster
button add/remove) hold their resolution, structural shifts that
were fragmented into per-line clusters now collapse to one
regional cluster, and full inversions stay 1 cluster as expected.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat(visual-review): cap visible clusters at 5, hide when one cluster dominates

Three UX guardrails on the cluster overview:

1. Cap visible clusters at top 5 by pixel count. The backend stores
   up to CLUSTER_MAX (currently 20) for completeness, but more than
   ~5 numbered chips on an image start to crowd each other and the
   sidebar runs out of vertical real estate. Total count stays in
   the panel header so the trim is explicit ("top 5 of 21").

2. Hide the cluster overview entirely when a single cluster covers
   most of the image (>=80% diff). Full inversions or wholesale
   changes show as "1 region · 99%" — drawing a giant box around
   the entire image just shouts the diff% tag at you. Skip it.

3. Render bbox overlays in split mode too (second copy inside the
   clipped After half so boxes stay visible regardless of split
   position). Previously only diff / blend / side-by-side-after
   carried the overlay; now every comparison mode does.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): post-merge aligned cluster bboxes

Pixelhog's CCL still produces one cluster per visually distinct row
in a list-shift diff even with dilation=8 — the dilation closes 16px
gaps but rows that share an x-extent and stack vertically end up as
N separate but heavily overlapping bboxes. From the user's POV that's
"the list shifted", which is one regional change, not seven.

Add a wrapper-side post-merge pass that combines bboxes if they're
already overlapping, or aligned on one axis (>=50% overlap on that
axis) and within ~60px on the other. Catches both the same-column
list-row case and the same-row button-strip case without merging
unrelated regions on opposite sides of the screen.

Verified across the demo set: session-timeline collapses 21 -> 1
regional cluster, exception-card stays at 1, tags-popover small
button changes merge to 1, full inversions stay at 1.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): tone down per-snapshot change chips

The pulse icon reads as "average drift over time" — it makes sense in
the snapshots overview where we surface aggregated drift, but on a
single snapshot it overstates a one-off measurement. Worse, in the
filmstrip we were rendering it twice per card (kind chip + size-changed
chip), which crowded the thumbnail and pushed the identifier text out
of view.

- Drop IconPulse from SnapshotChangeBadge (keeps it in SnapshotCard /
  VisualReviewSnapshotOverviewScene where it belongs).
- Compact mode (size="small") now uses non-pill corners, smaller
  padding, and shortens "Layout shift" to "Shift".
- Size-mismatch chip becomes icon-only on the filmstrip; the verbose
  "Size changed" text still shows on the sidebar.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
refactor(visual-review): adopt native cluster merging from pixelhog 1.2.0

Pixelhog landed the aligned-bbox merge feature we proposed (merge_gap +
merge_overlap on Comparison.clusters). Drop our Python post-process
mirror — same algorithm, runs in Rust, behaves identically against the
demo set.

A subtle semantic shift: pixelhog's `total_clusters` reports the
pre-merge raw count and `truncated` flips when items.length < total
(i.e. merging happened). Our previous Python pass overwrote total to
the post-merge length and forced truncated=False, throwing that signal
away. Now we keep it — the panel header reads "top 1 of 21" when 21
raw clusters merged into 1 regional cluster, which is more honest than
hiding the pre-merge size.

Update the dominant-cluster guard to use `items.length === 1` instead
of `total === 1`. Same intent ("a single cluster covers most of the
image"), but post-merge — `total` can be 21 even when pixelhog merged
everything into one region.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): adopt pixelhog 1.2 truncated semantics

Pixelhog rebuilt with the fix from open-question #1: `truncated` now
fires only when max_clusters dropped clusters pre-merge. Merging by
itself no longer flips it. `total_clusters` still reports the
pre-merge raw count, but it's now meaningful as "we collapsed N raw
into M regional", not as "you're seeing M of N".

Cluster panel header reflects the new shape:
  - "1 region"                         (no merging, no cap)
  - "1 region · merged from 21 raw"    (merging, no cap)
  - "5 regions · cap reached"          (cap kicked in pre-merge)
  - both compose when both apply

Drop the FE-level VISIBLE_CLUSTER_CAP slice — it conflated FE trimming
with the new cap-reached signal, and pixelhog's native merge keeps
post-merge counts in single digits in 97 % of real diffs anyway.
The dominant-cluster guard (hide overlay when 1 cluster covers >=80 %
of the image) is unchanged.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat(visual-review): manage quarantine from snapshot history view

Two missing things from the per-identifier page:

  - couldn't tell whether the identifier was currently quarantined,
    by whom, why, or until when
  - couldn't unquarantine without bouncing back to a run scene

Both surface the same backend pieces that already exist; just
weren't wired in. History scene now loads the active quarantine
entry on mount, renders a banner showing reason / created_by /
expiry / unquarantine button when active, or a quarantine trigger
when not.

Pulled the quarantine modal + theme-sibling helper out of
SnapshotDiffViewer into a shared `QuarantineAction` component so
both views drive identical UX.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): use LemonBanner action slot for unquarantine

The hand-rolled flex layout fought LemonBanner's internal flex —
the icon, title, and button ended up stacked instead of laid out
on one row. LemonBanner exposes an `action` prop that handles the
"button on the right at md+, full-width below at narrower widths"
pattern correctly; use that instead and let the banner own the
layout.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
chore(visual-review): bump pixelhog to 1.2.0 from PyPI, drop SSIM wrapper

Pixelhog 1.2.0 dropped the standalone paired-image API (compare,
diff, diff_count, ssim, *_rgba variants) in favor of the Comparison
object — the API discussion we had with them landed.

Migrate the one remaining caller (`backend/ssim.py`) over to
`Comparison(a, b).ssim()`, which makes the wrapper a one-liner
that adds nothing. Drop the file outright. Drop the TestComputeSSIM
unit tests too — they were smoke-testing pixelhog's SSIM contract
(identical -> 1.0, very different -> low, etc.) and pixelhog
already covers those in its own suite. The two-tier classification
tests still exercise SSIM via `compare_images`.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): address bot review feedback

Five fixes from the Copilot / Greptile / Codex passes on the PR:

1. Empty UI shells when SnapshotChangeBadge returns null. The
   filmstrip, history-row separator, and diff-viewer "Change" row
   each gated on conditions broader than the badge's actual render
   predicate, so sub-display-floor (`diff_percentage > 0` but below
   PCT_DISPLAY_FLOOR=0.05) snapshots with no `change_kind` rendered
   blank chip areas / dangling separator dots / empty value rows.
   Export `hasSnapshotChangeBadge` from the badge module and gate
   on it everywhere.

2. Image -> panel hover sync was silently broken on the After half
   of split mode. The second `BboxOverlay` instance inside the
   clipped split-After overlay was missing `onHover`, so hovering
   bboxes there did nothing. Forward `onOverlayHover` to that
   instance too.

3. `sortedChangedSnapshots` ordering broke for structural snapshots
   after the backfill nulled their `diff_percentage`. The selector
   used `s.diff_percentage ?? 0`, which sank structural rows to the
   bottom of run review. Fall back to `(1 - ssim_score) * 100` so
   structural shifts surface alongside pixel diffs by perceptual
   severity.

4. `get_snapshot_history` was running the full Pydantic
   `DiffMetadata.model_validate` plus cluster reconstruction per
   row just to extract one boolean (the `cluster_summary` is
   intentionally omitted from the history-entry contract).
   Read `size_mismatch` directly from the dict.

5. `_make_compare_result` test factory wasn't passing the new
   `size_mismatch` and `cluster_summary` fields that landed on
   `CompareResult` — typecheck error in `test_thumbnails.py`.
   Pass the no-op defaults explicitly.

Plus parametrize the three solid-color classification tests in
`TestTwoTierClassification` (obvious_pixel_change / identical /
subtle_noise) — they all share the `_classify(a, b) == expected`
shape and consolidate cleanly per the codebase convention.

title: fix(scenes): persist inactive-tab URL updates onto the right fields
author: georgemunyoro

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body: ## Pull request overview This PR fixes a race in internal scene tabs where URL-sync actions emitted by an *inactive* tab’s logic were not being persisted into that tab’s stored URL state, causing user edits (e.g. in the SQL editor) to be lost when switching tabs quickly. **Changes:** - For inactive tabs, compute the intended URL from the action’s own `actionToUrl` handler (instead of reading `router.values.location`, which reflects the active tab). - Persist the resulting URL into the correct `SceneTab` fields (`pathname`, `search`, `hash`) rather than writing a non-existent `url` property. --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

reviews.author: mariusandra
reviews.body: Looks good to me! 👍

commits.message:
fix(scenes): persist inactive-tab URL updates onto the right fields

When an inactive scene tab's logic fires a URL-changing action (e.g.
syncUrlWithQuery resolving after setQueryInput's 500ms breakpoint, post
tab-switch), tabAwareActionToUrl was reading router.values.location —
the active tab's URL — and writing it to a non-existent `url` field on
SceneTab, so the inactive tab's stored pathname/search/hash never got
the update. In the SQL editor this looked like edits silently vanishing
when you switched tabs within 500ms of typing.

Use the action's own URL builder for the inactive logic, run combineUrl
on it, and write pathname/search/hash for real.

title: perf(cdp): split observeResults reads to redis reader pool
author: meikelmosby

reviews.author: dmarchuk
reviews.body: LGTM 👍 Just pointed out one caveat which I think should be ok in this case

commits.message:
perf(cdp): split observeResults reads to redis reader pool using mget

The observeResults pipeline previously sent 3 commands per function to
the writer: get(state), get(lock), checkRateLimitV2. The state and lock
reads don't depend on the token bucket write, so split them out to the
reader pool.

Uses mget to batch all state keys and lock keys into 2 commands instead
of 2N individual gets, further reducing round-trip overhead. The reads
and writes run in parallel via Promise.all so there's no added latency.
Includes fallback to writer if the reader fails, and early return when
there are no function costs to process.
commits.author: meikelmosby

All six top-level reviews came from bots (greptile, codex) or the PR author (posthog[bot]) replying to those bots — no human has signed off on the final shape of the change. reviews.body: in theory looks good, lets see how it does in prod

commits.message:
fix(slack-app): include block/attachment text from thread root in agent context

When a Slack thread is started by a PostHog alert (subscriptions, log
alerts, hog-function destinations), the substantive content lives in
`blocks` while the top-level `text` field is often empty or a thin
fallback. _collect_thread_messages only read msg["text"], so the agent
saw effectively no alert content when a user followed up with a
@PostHog mention in that thread.

Walk the block-kit tree (and attachments) to flatten any informational
text when the top-level `text` is empty, and use bot_profile.name /
username as the author label for bot-authored messages so the agent
gets a sensible "PostHog: ..." line instead of "Unknown: ".

Block flattening is wrapped in try/except per-message — a malformed
block on one message can't drop the rest of the thread.

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body: ## Pull request overview This PR fixes a performance regression in Dagster CI by preventing an unscoped `git fetch --deepen=...` from using the default wildcard refspec (which fetches every branch) during merge-base computation for the schema cache key. **Changes:** - Increase the `changes` job checkout depth to `fetch-depth: 1000` and add `filter: blob:none` to ensure `HEAD^2` is available for merge-base computation. - Replace the unscoped `git fetch --deepen=200` with an explicit, scoped fetch of only the PR base ref, using `--no-tags` and `--filter=blob:none`, matching the established `ci-backend` pattern. --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. commits.message:
fix(ci): scope dagster merge-base fetch to base ref

Previous version called `git fetch --deepen=200` with no refspec, which
fell back to `remote.origin.fetch` (`+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`)
and pulled every branch in the repo. The dagster `changes` job ran past
its 5m timeout doing this on PR runs.

Match ci-backend's turbo-discover pattern instead: bump checkout to
fetch-depth=1000 with `filter: blob:none` so HEAD^2 is reachable, and
fetch only the base ref (no-tags, blob-filtered) for merge-base.

feat(insights): wrap trending in paginated envelope, expose activity tools

Two follow-ups after live-testing the trending MCP tool:

1. Switch the trending response to {count, next, previous, results} so
   the MCP codegen's per-item enrichment template runs over the array
   correctly (it was treating the flat array as a single object and

   Required scope added so personal API keys / OAuth tokens work.

2. Enable insights-activity-retrieve and insights-all-activity-retrieve

commits.message:
chore(insights): trim activity payloads in MCP tools

Live testing showed each activity entry includes the full before/after
JSON of the changed field — even when only one nested key changed. For
the query field that means hundreds of lines of noise per entry, which
swamps an agent reading "what was worked on recently".

Use the YAML response.exclude config (with list: true so per-item
filtering applies) to drop:
- detail.changes.*.before / .after (the bulky bit)
- detail.trigger / detail.type (almost always null)

Agent still sees who did what, when, and which fields changed —
enough to decide whether to drill deeper. For full state of an insight
after a change, agents call insight-get; for a single insight's full
history, insights-activity-retrieve still gives field-level changes.
commits.author: andrewm4894

commits.message:
fix(insights): surface last_modified_by on trending insight serializer

Greptile correctly flagged that the YAML response.include listed
last_modified_by for insights-trending-retrieve, but the underlying
TrendingInsightSerializer extends InsightBasicSerializer (which only
has the timestamp, not the user FK) — so the field was silently
absent.

Adds last_modified_by as a UserBasicSerializer field on the trending
serializer with help_text, and adds select_related on the queryset to
avoid an N+1 (matching how the basic insights list builds its query).

Genuinely useful info for agents ranking trending insights — surfaces
who is currently iterating alongside the view-count signal.

title: fix(ingestion-consumer): set metadata.broker.list to match Node config
author: jose-sequeira

commits.message:
fix(ingestion-consumer): set metadata.broker.list to match Node config

bootstrap.servers and metadata.broker.list are aliases in librdkafka, but
rdkafka-rs stores them in a HashMap with non-deterministic iteration order.
Setting bootstrap.servers from KAFKA_HOSTS while overriding metadata.broker.list
from KAFKA_CONSUMER_METADATA_BROKER_LIST left the consumer landing on either
cluster at random. Using the same key (matching Node consumer.ts) means the
override overwrites in place, so HashMap ordering can no longer matter.
commits.author: jose-sequeira

fix(feature-flags): block disallowed cohort operators from Recent picker

Feature flag release conditions intentionally hide the operator dropdown
for cohort filters because only `in` is supported. The Recent tab in the
TaxonomicFilter, however, replays whatever property filter the user
previously selected anywhere in PostHog (including a `not_in` cohort
from Insights), bypassing that restriction and silently shrinking flag

  filter with a non-`in` operator to `in` instead of applying it
  verbatim.
- `infiniteListLogic.contextFilteredRecentItems` hides those entries
  from the Recent list so the disallowed option never surfaces.

title: fix(notebooks): make SQL chart adapt to notebook node height
author: a-lider

commits.message:
fix(notebooks): make SQL chart output fluid in notebook nodes

The SQL chart output in notebook nodes was rendering at a fixed
~60vh because the chart kept resolving `presetChartHeight=true`
even though the host container has explicit height. Stretching
the node didn't grow the chart, and shrinking it clipped the chart.

Add an explicit `fitOutputToContainer` prop on SQLEditor / OutputPane
that forces the visualization to fill its container. NotebookSQLEditorOutput
passes it so the chart adapts to whatever height the notebook node
is set to (default or user-resized). Other consumers (the SQL editor
scene) are unchanged.
commits.author: claude

commits.message:
refactor(notebooks): use existing `embedded` prop to disable 60vh preset

Replace the new `fitOutputToContainer` prop chain with an override
based on the existing `embedded` prop / sql editor's `isEmbeddedMode`.

The semantics already line up: `embedded=true` means the chart sits
inside a host that owns layout — notebook node, output pane in
embedded mode — so the chart should fill its container instead of
falling back to 60vh of the viewport.

Two surgical overrides — one in DataVisualization's
InternalDataTableVisualization (covers `<Query>` path used by saved
insights), one in OutputPane's InternalDataTableVisualization (covers
SQL editor path) — and the prop chain through SQLEditor / OutputPane /
NotebookSQLEditor goes away.
commits.author: a-lider

commits.message:
fix(notebooks): SQL chart now resizes both ways with the node

The SQL LineGraph used `useResizeObserver` to feed observed container
height back as inline `style={{ height: `${px}px` }}` on its inner
div. That created a feedback loop:

- shrink: the inline pixel height held the inner at its old size, the
  outer flex-col couldn't shrink past it, ResizeObserver never fired,
  state never updated, chart got clipped by the notebook node's
  overflow-hidden.
- grow: the inline value was smaller than what the parent now allowed,
  flex-grow expanded past it, ResizeObserver fired — worked.

The insights LineGraph (used by Trends) doesn't do any of this — it
puts the canvas inside a single flex container and lets Chart.js handle
resizing via its built-in ResizeObserver
(responsive: true, maintainAspectRatio: false). Both directions work.

Match that shape: drop useResizeObserver and the inline height
forwarding, render the canvas directly inside one flex container.
commits.author: a-lider

commits.message:
fix(notebooks): SQL chart adapts to node height like Trends does

Wrap the embedded path in InsightCard__viz so SQL DataVisualization charts
follow the same layout pattern as InsightViz/Trends. Mirrors InsightViz.tsx's
embedded branch — InsightCard__viz provides display: flex; flex-direction:
column; flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto, which is the chain that lets
the canvas shrink with its host container instead of getting stuck at its
previous render size.

Apply the same wrap inside OutputPane's InternalDataTableVisualization so
inline SQL queries in notebooks behave the same way.

Drop the LineGraph wrapper's flex-col layout (the canvas-as-flex-item caused
min-height: auto to clamp to canvas content size, blocking shrink). Match the
insights LineGraph: plain block wrapper, grow + h-full, canvas as a regular
block child sized by Chart.js responsive mode.

Center the SavedInsight loading state so the LoadingBar sits in the middle
of the node instead of pinned to the top during metadata fetch.
commits.author: a-lider

commits.message:
refactor(notebooks): simplify — drop redundant presetChartHeight override

The `embedded ? false : presetChartHeight` override was needed before
the InsightCard__viz wrap landed: back then the chart sat directly inside
a non-flex parent, so h-[60vh] was a hard fixed height that didn't adapt.

With the InsightCard__viz wrap (display: flex; flex-direction: column;
flex: 1; min-height: 0), the chart wrapper becomes a flex item whose
h-[60vh] is now just a flex-basis. flex-grow:1 lets it expand past 60vh,
flex-shrink:1 + min-height:0 (from overflow-hidden) lets it shrink below.
The wrapper adapts to the parent regardless of presetChartHeight.

Drop the override in both DataVisualization.tsx and OutputPane.tsx.
commits.author: a-lider

title: fix(data-deletion): drop table qualifier on materialized columns in HogQL predicates
author: orian

commits.message:
fix(data-deletion): drop table qualifier on materialized columns in HogQL predicates

The Dagster `data_deletion_request_event_removal` job was failing on
lightweight DELETE when a HogQL predicate referenced a property backed
by a materialized column:

    DB::Exception: Missing columns: 'sharded_events.mat_$current_url'
    while processing: '_CAST(if((team_id = …) AND … AND
    like(sharded_events.`mat_$current_url`, '%…')))

The column exists on every replica — `clusterAllReplicas(system.columns)`
confirmed it. The actual cause is a ClickHouse quirk: lightweight DELETE
rewrites the predicate into an `_CAST(if(<predicate>, …))` mutation, and
the mutation expression analyzer does not resolve table-qualified column
references the way SELECT does. Unqualified columns (`team_id`,
`timestamp`) work; `sharded_events.mat_$current_url` is treated as a
column literally named that, hence "Missing columns".

The HogQL printer already drops the table prefix for regular fields when
`within_non_hogql_query=True` (base.py visit_field_type, "Do not prepend
table name in non-hogql context"). The materialized-column path was
inconsistent — it always emitted `<table>.mat_<prop>`. This change makes
the mat-column and dmat-column paths honor the same convention: in
non-HogQL contexts, pass `table=None` to PrintableMaterializedColumn so
the column is emitted unqualified, matching the legacy
events__pdi__person path that already does this.

Cleanup: 272a571e7d0 (3 hours ago) introduced a `target_data_table` flag
to switch the qualifier between `events.` and `sharded_events.`. With
the printer no longer emitting any qualifier in non-HogQL contexts, that
plumbing is dead weight and is removed:

- `compile_hogql_predicate(obj)` — no more `target_data_table` parameter
- `_event_removal_where(obj)` (dag) — parameter dropped
- `_build_event_filter` / `_build_property_filter` (admin) — parameter dropped
- `_fetch_stats` — collapsed dual `(events_filter, sharded_filter)` to a
  single `(extra_filter, params)` since both queries now take the same
  predicate

Tests renamed and snapshots regenerated to assert that no table prefix
appears in the compiled SQL.
commits.author: orian

author: gustavohstrassburger

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR aims to fix realtime cohort tiering by stopping realtime calculations from mutating the backfill timestamp and by sharing percentile boundaries through Redis-backed quantile caching. It fits into the Temporal messaging workflow that partitions realtime cohorts into percentile-based schedules. **Changes:** - Removes the incorrect `last_backfill_person_properties_at` update from realtime cohort metric writes. - Switches percentile-threshold calculation to use a Redis-backed quantiles cache with retry/lock logic. - Adds unit/integration tests for threshold math, cache behavior, and concurrent access. **Review outcome:** I found blocking issues in the new Redis locking/caching logic, so this is not ready as-is. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `posthog/temporal/messaging/test/test_threshold_calculation_math.py` | Adds math-focused tests for percentile boundary alignment with cached quantiles. | | `posthog/temporal/messaging/test/test_realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow.py` | Updates existing workflow threshold tests to mock cache-based quantile lookup. | | `posthog/temporal/messaging/test/test_quantiles_storage.py` | Adds unit tests for Redis keying, cache reads/writes, and mocked race handling. | | `posthog/temporal/messaging/test/test_quantiles_integration.py` | Adds Redis-backed concurrency and cache-expiration integration tests. | | `posthog/temporal/messaging/realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow.py` | Stops realtime cohort updates from touching the backfill timestamp. | | `posthog/temporal/messaging/realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow_coordinator.py` | Changes percentile threshold calculation to use cached quantiles instead of direct local computation. | | `posthog/temporal/messaging/quantiles_storage.py` | Introduces Redis cache/lock helpers for quantile reuse across workflows. |

reviews.author: dmarticus
reviews.body:
Did a pass focused on what greptile/Copilot didn't catch (or only partially addressed). Latest commit looks like it landed the lock-acquisition guard and the fail-closed retry path — nice. A few things still worth addressing before merge: ## P1 — blocking **1. Redis is now a hard dependency for the realtime cohort workflow — undocumented operational regression.** End-to-end: when Redis is unavailable, `get_quantiles` catches and returns `None`, `store_quantiles` catches and returns `False`, `_calculate_and_cache_quantiles` retries 3× and returns `None` (the explicit "fail closed" comment at `quantiles_storage.py:269-272`), `calculate_percentile_thresholds` returns `None`, and every percentile schedule (p50/p80/p90/p95/p99) skips execution. Before this PR there was a local fallback. The "consistency over availability" trade-off is defensible but it's nowhere in the PR description, has no metric/alert, and isn't covered by tests. A Redis blip that used to be invisible now silently halts the realtime cohort tier. At minimum, raise the log level to `error` on Redis-driven cache miss and emit a metric so on-call notices. **2. The headline timestamp fix has zero test coverage.** The PR title says "threshold overlaps **and timestamp bugs**", but `_batch_update_cohort_metrics` in `realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow.py:228` has no test. Removing the `last_backfill_person_properties_at` write is the primary stated bug fix and there's no regression guard. Easy to undo accidentally. ## P2 — important **3. `get_or_calculate_quantiles` (line 207) is dead "legacy" wrapper in a brand-new file.** It only exists because the tests call it. Update the tests to call `get_cached_quantiles_or_calculate` directly and delete the wrapper — there's no real legacy caller in master, and leaving it makes future cleanup awkward. **4. Lazy import in coordinator violates AGENTS.md** (greptile only flagged `statistics`). `realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow_coordinator.py:175` has `from posthog.temporal.messaging.quantiles_storage import get_cached_quantiles_or_calculate` inside `get_thresholds()`. AGENTS.md is explicit about module-level imports. Tests will still patch correctly via `patch("posthog.temporal.messaging.quantiles_storage.get_cached_quantiles_or_calculate")` because that patches the source module, not the import binding. **5. Distributed lock has the textbook TTL-expiry safety hole.** `store_quantiles` writes constant `"locked"` (line 78) and unconditionally `redis_client.delete(lock_key)` on exit. If the 5-minute LOCK_TTL expires under our feet (GC pause, slow thread, slow Redis), another worker can acquire with a fresh lock and we'd then delete *their* lock on cleanup. Standard fix: unique token per acquirer (`uuid4().hex`) plus Lua compare-and-delete on release. In practice `statistics.quantiles` is fast so this is rare, but it's trivial to make correct. ## P3 — minor **6. Copilot's hour-boundary concern still appears unaddressed.** A p0-p50 run at 12:59 and a p50-p80 run at 13:03 use different hour buckets and can produce overlapping ranges again — the exact bug this PR fixes. Either read current+previous bucket, or extend the bucket window with grace. **7. `time.sleep` partially addressed, not fully.** Worst case is now ~600ms (3 × 200ms + jitter) blocking inside the `database_sync_to_async` pool, which is also doing Redis I/O. Better would be moving retry/backoff to the async caller (`calculate_percentile_thresholds`) with `asyncio.sleep`, leaving the sync wrapper to do one fast attempt. **8. Stale strings:** - `quantiles_storage.py:26` — comment says `quantiles:2024-01-15:14`, prefix is actually `duration_quantiles:`. - `test_quantiles_storage.py:146` — test docstring says "2-hour bucket format", buckets are hourly. **9. `time.sleep(1.1)` in `test_cache_expiration_behavior`** — flaky on slow CI. Mock `DEFAULT_TTL` and the time check rather than wall-clocking. **10. `max_retries` is misnamed** — it's total attempts (including the first), not retries. **11. `@database_sync_to_async` now wraps Redis I/O.** Pushing Redis retries with `time.sleep` into the Django sync pool changes its workload mix; cleaner to do the Redis interaction outside the wrapper. ## Suggested feedback before merge - log/metric on Redis-driven cache miss so we can see when the new fail-closed path triggers - regression test for the timestamp fix - drop the dead `get_or_calculate_quantiles` wrapper - module-level imports The rest you can do after if you want, but IMO why not do it all ya know? ---
Copy this feedback into an agent to address it ``` Address the following review feedback on this branch. Items are ranked; please do all P1 and P2 items, plus #6 from P3. Feel free to push back if any of these are wrong. Files involved: - posthog/temporal/messaging/quantiles_storage.py - posthog/temporal/messaging/realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow.py - posthog/temporal/messaging/realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow_coordinator.py - posthog/temporal/messaging/test/test_quantiles_storage.py - posthog/temporal/messaging/test/test_quantiles_integration.py - posthog/temporal/messaging/test/test_realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow.py - posthog/temporal/messaging/test/test_threshold_calculation_math.py P1: 1. The PR makes Redis a hard dependency for the realtime cohort workflow — when Redis is unavailable, all percentile schedules now silently skip instead of falling back. This is intentional ("fail closed for consistency") but undocumented and unmonitored. Add: - Raise the log level to `LOGGER.error` (not warning) in `_calculate_and_cache_quantiles` when we're returning None after exhausting retries with no cached value. - Emit a Temporal metric (use the existing `temporalio.workflow.metric_meter()` pattern in this directory) counting "quantiles_unavailable" so on-call can see it. - Update the PR description to state the consistency-over-availability trade-off explicitly. 2. The PR title claims a timestamp bug fix but `_batch_update_cohort_metrics` in posthog/temporal/messaging/realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow.py has no test. Add a regression test in test_realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow.py that: - Calls `_batch_update_cohort_metrics` with a couple of cohorts. - Asserts `last_backfill_person_properties_at` is NOT updated. - Asserts `last_realtime_cohort_calculation_at` IS updated. - Asserts `last_calculation_duration_ms` updates respect the DURATION_UPDATE_RELATIVE_THRESHOLD. P2: 3. Delete `get_or_calculate_quantiles` in quantiles_storage.py (the "legacy" wrapper). It only exists for tests in this brand-new module. Update test_quantiles_storage.py and test_quantiles_integration.py to call `get_cached_quantiles_or_calculate` directly. 4. Move the lazy import in realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow_coordinator.py:175 (`from posthog.temporal.messaging.quantiles_storage import get_cached_quantiles_or_calculate`) and the `import statistics` lazy import in quantiles_storage.py to module-top. AGENTS.md requires module-level imports. Tests use `patch("posthog.temporal.messaging.quantiles_storage.get_cached_quantiles_or_calculate")` which patches the source module, so test mocks still work after the move. 5. Fix the distributed lock to handle TTL expiry safely. Currently `store_quantiles` writes constant `"locked"` and unconditionally deletes the key. Instead: - Write a unique token (e.g., `uuid4().hex`) when acquiring. - On release, use a Lua script (`EVAL`) for atomic compare-and-delete: only delete if the value still equals the token we wrote. - If you don't want a Lua script, accept the risk and add a comment documenting it; but the Lua script is the standard fix and the redis client supports it. P3: 6. Address the hour-boundary issue: schedules running near :59/:00 currently use different hour buckets and can reintroduce overlapping thresholds. Pick one approach: - On cache miss, also check the previous-hour bucket and use it if present and recent. - OR: round bucket boundaries to a coarser unit (e.g., 30-minute buckets shifted so adjacent schedule runs land in the same bucket). The first approach is simpler and lower-risk. After your changes: - Run the test files listed above and make sure they pass. - Run `ruff check . --fix` and `ruff format .` on the touched files. - Don't push automatically — leave changes local for review. ```

reviews.author: dmarticus
reviews.body:
Re-reviewed since my last pass — looks good, all my P1/P2 items and the priority P3 (hour-boundary) are addressed. Bonus call-out: pulling `max_value` into `CachedQuantiles` actually fixes a hole I missed — p100 was still coming from the current worker's `max(durations_list)` while p1–p99 came from cache, so the top tier could drift. Nice catch.

Approving. A few non-blocking notes for follow-up (or now if convenient):

1. **Function-body imports in the new tests** (`test_realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow.py:1472, 1546, 1586`). AGENTS.md requires module-level imports — please move these up. Easy cleanup.

2. **The `quantiles_unavailable` counter may silently no-op in prod.** `temporalio.activity.metric_meter()` is invoked inside a `database_sync_to_async` wrapper, which runs on a sync thread pool. Activity contextvars don't reliably propagate to those threads, and the `except RuntimeError: pass` will swallow the failure. If you're going to alert on this metric, worth either capturing the meter on the async side and passing it in, or emitting from `calculate_percentile_thresholds` *after* `get_thresholds()` returns `None`. Verify it actually fires before wiring an alert to it.

3. **Counter built inline** — convention in `realtime_cohort_calculation_workflow.py:97-115` factors these into helpers. Makes alert wiring easier to grep for.

4. **`TestBatchUpdateCohortMetrics` boilerplate** — the three tests rebuild org+team and differ only in cohort setup + expectations. Per AGENTS.md ("prefer parameterized tests"), these read more clearly as a `@pytest.mark.parametrize` with a shared fixture.

5. **First-calculation assertion is loose** — `cohort.last_realtime_cohort_calculation_at != initial_realtime_time` works because `None != datetime` is True; `is not None` expresses intent better.

Still unaddressed from my prior pass (also non-blocking):
- PR description doesn't note the consistency-over-availability tradeoff.
- Stale comment at `quantiles_storage.py:28` (says `quantiles:...`, prefix is `duration_quantiles:`).
- `time.sleep(1.1)` in `test_cache_expiration_behavior` — flake risk on slow CI.
- Retry `time.sleep` still runs inside `database_sync_to_async` pool (~600ms worst case).

title: chore(ci): key schema cache restore on merge-base sha
author: webjunkie

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body: ## Pull request overview This PR makes schema-cache restores in CI deterministic by keying restores to the PR branch’s merge-base with the base branch instead of restoring the newest `master` cache. In the backend/dagster test pipelines, that reduces the chance of applying a schema snapshot from a newer master commit that the branch has not actually incorporated yet. **Changes:** - Added `schema_cache_key` job outputs in backend and dagster discovery jobs. - Computed a merge-base-derived cache key on pull requests and propagated it to downstream test jobs. - Removed broad `restore-keys` fallback so cache misses safely fall back to full migrations. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `.github/workflows/ci-backend.yml` | Computes and exports a merge-base schema cache key, then uses it for backend test job cache restores. | | `.github/workflows/ci-dagster.yml` | Computes and exports the same style of merge-base schema cache key for dagster shards and uses it for schema restore. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

reviews.author: rnegron
reviews.body: ohh good catch

commits.message:
chore(ci): key schema cache restore on merge-base sha

Previously the restore used `restore-keys: posthog-schema-master-` which
always matched the newest master cache regardless of where the PR branch
diverged. A stale branch could get a schema from a master commit ahead of
its branch point, causing migration conflicts when the branch's own
migrations tried to alter tables or columns already changed by master.

Compute `git merge-base HEAD^2 origin/<base>` once in `turbo-discover`
(ci-backend) and `changes` (ci-dagster), output it as `schema_cache_key`,
and use it as the exact restore key in all consumer jobs (turbo-tests,
django, dagster shards). No `restore-keys` fallback — a cache miss falls
through to a full migrate, which is already the safe baseline.

Branches more than ~1000 commits behind master (backend) or ~200 commits
(dagster) also fall through to full migrate gracefully.

fix(members): don't poll updates or me-first while a search is active

Two bugs surfaced by qa-swarm now that members is server-filtered:

1. loadMemberUpdates polls for updated_after the latest known member
   and merges results into `members`. With server-side search active,
   `members` holds the filtered set, so any concurrent poll would

   results — visibly broken UX. Skip the poll while a search is set.

   match score. With client-side Fuse the user only saw themselves at

   they always do, even when searching for someone else. Only put me

The change moves analytics metadata queries onto the authentication request path, directly touching user serialization during auth flows — this needs a human reviewer to sign off.

commits.message:
perf(user): move identify property update from request path to frontend

UserSerializer.to_representation called user_identify.identify_task.delay()
on every render. The Celery task itself is fire-and-forget, but the
.delay() broker write is synchronous and was spiking to 570ms+ in
production traces (FtYCla, 81ms in PaViiG, etc.). Volume = every
authenticated render = every page navigation.

The property bundle is data the frontend already has access to via
UserSerializer. Move the responsibility:

- Backend exposes user.analytics_metadata: a SerializerMethodField that
  returns User.get_analytics_metadata() (org/project counts, current
  membership level, social providers, etc.). Only computed when the
  serialized user is the requesting user, so staff retrievals don't
  seed analytics for someone else.
- Frontend (userLogic.loadUserSuccess) hands the bundle to
  posthog.people.set alongside the existing email/realm. posthog-js
  already debounces these for us.
- Drop the .delay() call from to_representation entirely.

Same correctness model as today (fire on every render), but the broker
write happens client-side via the SDK's own batching instead of on the
Django request path.

feat(workflows): surface workflow variables in All/Suggestions tab

The All/Suggestions tab is always prepended to the workflow scene's
taxonomic filter via TaxonomicPropertyFilter, and is the default landing
tab when the category-dropdown flag is on. With no items contributed by
the WorkflowVariables group it lands users on an empty-feeling tab that

  All/Suggestions list.

commits.message:
fix(taxonomic-filter): keep popover open when clicking category dropdown trigger pill

The `click-outside-block` class on the LemonMenu lands on the dropdown
overlay (the menu items), not on the trigger button. When the trigger
pill is clicked from inside a parent popover (e.g. reopening a saved
property filter in a workflow conditional branch), the native mouseup
target is the trigger button, which has no `click-outside-block`
ancestor. The parent FilterRow Popover treats the click as outside and
closes, which means the user can't change the active category once the
filter has been saved.

Add `click-outside-block` to the trigger LemonButton so the click is
covered by the `useOutsideClickHandler` exception and the parent
popover stays open.

Adds a Playwright regression test that reopens a saved $browser=Chrome
filter on a conditional branch and asserts the popover stays open and
the category menu opens after clicking the trigger pill.

title: perf(preflight): pre-warm timezone offsets cache at app startup
author: pauldambra

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Low-risk performance tweak: pre-warms an already-cached utility function at app startup, safely guarded against test/static-collection environments and swallowing any exception without crashing startup.

commits.message:
perf(preflight): pre-warm timezone offsets cache at app startup

#57418 made get_available_timezones_with_offsets hourly-cached, but the
cache is per-process via @lru_cache. With many pods and modest home-view
traffic per pod, every fresh pod still pays the ~580ms pytz walk on its
first preflight call.

Production traces from 2026-05-04 09:14-09:53 UTC show four separate
home-view requests landing on four freshly-started pods (started at
08:37, 09:13, 09:29, 09:43 UTC), each paying 490-637ms in
preflight.available_timezones - the lru_cache is only saving the second
call onwards on each pod, but with many pods we don't get a second call
on most of them within an hour.

Pre-warm by calling get_available_timezones_with_offsets() from
PostHogConfig.ready() so every new pod populates its cache before
serving traffic. Skip during TEST and STATIC_COLLECTION (Dockerfile
build step has no Redis/etc.) and swallow exceptions so a pre-warm
failure cannot block app startup.

The "Tolerated drift" tile was inflated by AUTO_THRESHOLD rows — those
are auto-minted by the diff pipeline as a tolerated-hash cache for
sub-threshold pixel jitter, not deliberate "we accept this drift"
decisions. Scope all four tolerate aggregates (per-entry 30d/90d +
totals recent/frequent) to reason__in=[HUMAN, AGENT] so the count
reflects intent rather than rendering noise.

Card meta row redesigned around the data hierarchy:

- Corner badge reserved for severity (quarantine only). Tolerate count
  was sitting in the corner as a red `~N` glyph, which read as "alert"
  but represented activity, not severity.
- Drift % is now visible on the card via IconPulse — previously sorted
  by but never displayed, so the toolbar's "Sorted by drift avg"
  indicator pointed at nothing. Tints warning when ≥ 1%.
- Tolerate count moves into the meta row with IconFlag, alongside the
  baseline-change count. All three are zero-hidden, so clean cards
  stay clean.

Sort axis collapsed to drift-desc for every preset (was alpha for
"All" / drift for the problem slices). One axis means the toolbar
indicator stays honest as the user toggles presets.

Stat-row description and the inline `frequent` chip get explicit
human/agent wording + a tooltip explaining the ≥3-in-90d threshold.

Backend test added for AUTO_THRESHOLD exclusion. Local test infra (CH
zookeeper) is broken — CI will validate.

commits.message:
feat(mcp): accept object form for *_override params on all insight/dashboard tools

Follow-up to #57257. Two related changes:

1. Carries forward the union schema + normalizeOverride helper for the
   hand-written insight-query tool — the original commit was lost during
   the squash-merge of the parent PR.

2. Extends generate-tools.ts so any auto-generated tool with *_override
   query params (insight-get, dashboard-get, dashboard-insights-run, and
   future stream-tiles-retrieve) emits a .extend({...}) clause that
   accepts either a JSON string or a plain object, preserving the OpenAPI
   description via .describe(). The runtime client.request() helper
   already JSON.stringify-s object query params, so no handler changes
   are needed for the auto-generated path.

LLM agents reading insight/dashboard responses see variables and filters
as objects; requiring JSON.stringify before sending was friction that
frequently broke (escaping, double-encoding). Backward-compatible —
pre-encoded JSON strings still parse via the union.
commits.author: vdekrijger

commits.message:
refactor(mcp): drive object-form widening from x-accepts-stringified-json

Replaces the suffix-based detection with an explicit OpenAPI extension set
by the Django factories in posthog/api/openapi_parameters.py. The MCP
codegen reads `x-accepts-stringified-json` instead of pattern-matching
parameter names — the contract lives where the parameter is defined.

Also:
- Updates the description on both factories from "JSON object to
  override..." to "Object (or pre-encoded JSON string) to override..." so
  LLM agents reading auto-generated tool descriptions see the same hint
  the hand-written insight-query already gave.
- Skips the auto-union when a YAML param_overrides entry already covers
  the field (Zod's last-write-wins would otherwise silently clobber the
  more specific config).
- Adds 5 generate-tools unit tests for the extension-driven widening
  (including the param_overrides collision guard and exclude_params
  interaction) and 5 queryHandler unit tests covering the string +
  object override paths through normalizeOverride.
commits.author: vdekrijger

docs(mcp): clarify intent of two override-handling code paths

- generate-tools.ts: comment why the queryParamNames.includes guard exists
  in the stringified-json filter (it's the post-include/exclude filter, so
  YAML-excluded params don't get widened).
- query.ts: note that normalizeOverride is transitional — once
  insights().get() migrates onto the generic request() helper at
  services/mcp/src/api/client.ts:141-145 the helper can be deleted.

commits.message:
fix(surveys): unbreak class-body list[...] annotations after adding list() override

Adding `def list()` to SurveyViewSet shadowed Python's built-in `list`
inside the class namespace, breaking pre-existing `list[str]` and
`list[tuple[...]]` annotations on `_get_partial_responses_filter` and
`_process_survey_results`. At class-body evaluation, those `list[...]`
expressions resolved to the new method, raising:

at module import time, taking down 81 CI checks.

Switches the two affected annotations to `typing.List[...]` so they
reference the type via the typing module instead of the shadowed
built-in. Insight.py and dashboard.py don't hit this because their
viewsets don't have `list[...]` annotations in the class body.

title: perf(preflight): cache timezone offsets per-hour
author: pauldambra

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Clean, low-risk perf refactor: caching moves to a private helper keyed by hour components, the public wrapper is now decorator-free (fixing the stacked lru_cache the bot flagged in an older commit), and a clear test verifies same-hour deduplication and cross-hour recomputation.

commits.message:
perf(preflight): cache timezone offsets per-hour to avoid pytz walk per request

template.preflight has been spiking to 500-580ms in production traces.
Per-step instrumentation (#57404) localized the cost to
preflight.available_timezones — get_available_timezones_with_offsets
walks all ~600 entries in pytz.common_timezones on every preflight
load, computing the UTC offset for each.

Cache by hour. The set of timezones doesn't change at runtime, and
offsets only change at DST transitions (twice a year per timezone),
so an hourly bucket keeps the result correct within an hour of the
DST flip. lru_cache(maxsize=2) keeps memory bounded to the current
plus previous hour.

Existing test (test_available_timezones) still passes.

commits.message:
fix(preflight): drop stacked redundant lru_cache decorator

The original get_available_timezones_with_offsets had @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
on its def. When I extracted the bucketed inner function I left the original
decorator above the new @lru_cache(maxsize=2), so the function ended up
with two stacked lru_cache wrappers — the inner maxsize=1 retains 1 entry,
the outer maxsize=2 retains 2, so the inner cache evicts more aggressively
than needed and the layering reads as a leftover.

Bumping only via transaction.on_commit broke any test that mutates a

title: fix(replay): drop event-less sessions in summarization sweep
author: TueHaulund

commits.message:
fix(replay): drop event-less sessions in summarization sweep

The sweep finds candidates from session_replay_events and only filters by
summaries_exist before fanning out a summarize-session per session.
Recording-only sessions (replay snapshots but no analytics events) never
get a summary row written, so they're re-discovered every tick and the
workflow short-circuits at the no-events guard. In a recent 6h prod-us
window: 68k summarize-session workflows across 1.1k unique session IDs.

Add a HogQL pre-filter against the events table to drop sessions that
won't survive the workflow's no-events guard. Lift the workflow's
events_to_ignore literal into a shared SESSION_SUMMARY_EVENT_BLOCKLIST
constant so both call sites apply the same exclusion list. Widen the
events timestamp predicate beyond the sweep's lookback to cover sessions
whose events fired before the candidate window opened. Use a tighter
60s CH budget for the pre-filter so two sequential CH queries fit
inside FIND_ACTIVITY_TIMEOUT.

author: TueHaulund

reviews.author: fasyy612
reviews.body: Just a few nit comments but they are non-blocking, LGTM!

commits.message:
refactor(replay): drive gemini cleanup sweep from redis tracking

The previous Gemini cleanup sweep listed every file in the Gemini account
each cycle and inferred ownership from a `display_name` prefix. Two issues:

- Gemini's `files.list` returns HTTP 500 when paginating deep, which took
  down the whole sweep before any orphan got reclaimed.
- Files lingered on Gemini through consolidation, storage, tagging, and
  emission — none of which need them. The 20 GB account-wide cap limits
  in-flight summaries.

Switch the sweep to explicit per-upload tracking in Redis and release the
file as soon as analysis is done. Plus a related fix to the summarization
reconciler workflow, which was reporting success even when 100% of its
fan-out activities failed.

- Track every Gemini upload in Redis: per-file key (48h TTL) plus a
  sorted-set index keyed on `uploaded_at` so the sweep can fetch the
  oldest N entries via `ZRANGE LIMIT` — bounded server-side regardless of
  backlog. Tracking is written immediately after the file gets a name,
  before waiting for ACTIVE, so a polling timeout still leaves the file
  visible to the sweep.
- Sweep classifies via Temporal `describe`: terminal/`NOT_FOUND` →
  reclaim; `RUNNING` → skip (covers retries naturally). Bounded at 1500
  files per cycle, oldest-first.
- Atomic upload+track in a2: if Redis SET fails after a successful
  upload, the file is deleted inline and the activity raises so Temporal
  retries — no silent leaks. Missing-name guard is wrapped in the same
  try-block to avoid orphaning files when Gemini returns no name.
- Treat Gemini 404 as success during sweep delete: a previous untrack
  failure may have left an orphan key whose Gemini file is already gone
  — drop the key instead of looping until the 48h TTL.
- Schedule cadence: 30 min → 5 min. 4h age threshold → 60s
  race-condition guard.
- Summary workflow releases the file right after
  `analyze_video_segment_activity` finishes; `finally` guard handles
  failure paths.
- Renumbered `video_based/` files: a7_cleanup → a5_cleanup,
  a5_consolidate → a6_consolidate, a6a..d → a7a..d.
- Reconciler: fail the workflow when every fan-out activity (upsert +
  delete) failed. Partial failures still log and return as before.

commits.message:
perf(team): debounce calculate_product_activation enqueue per team

TeamSerializer.get_product_intents calls
`calculate_product_activation.delay(team_id, only_calc_if_days_since_last_checked=1)`
on every authenticated page load via get_context_for_template. The Celery
task itself short-circuits when it's been less than a day since the last
check - so the work is correctly skipped - but the .delay() round-trip to
the broker still happens on every render. Thousands of enqueues per
minute that the worker no-ops.

Add `enqueue_product_activation_calc_debounced(team_id)` that uses
`cache.add(..., timeout=24h)` (atomic SETNX EX) to debounce the enqueue
itself. Matches the task's own `only_calc_if_days_since_last_checked=1`
threshold, so we never miss a window the task would actually act on.

Returns True when the task was enqueued, False when debounced - useful
for assertions in tests, and matches the existing return contract of
`cache.add`.

Both `TeamSerializer.get_product_intents` and
`ProjectBackwardCompatSerializer.get_product_intents` now call this
helper.

commits.message:
perf(team): cache live_events_token JWT for 24h

TeamSerializer.get_live_events_token is part of get_context_for_template
and runs on every authenticated page load. The JWT itself is valid for
7 days but the previous code re-signed it on every render - HMAC + secret
read on the hot home-view path, ~200us per call but called constantly.

Extract a `get_or_mint_live_events_token(team, user_id)` helper that
caches the signed token for 24h. Cache key includes every claim that
would change the token (team_id, user_id, api_token, organization_id),
so api-token rotation or org moves automatically force a fresh mint. A
24h cache TTL on a 7-day token guarantees at least 6 days of remaining
validity for any cached value returned.

ProjectSerializer mints the same token via near-identical code; switch
it to use the same helper so both call sites share the cache.

4 unit tests cover: claim contents, second-call cache hit (no encode_jwt
called), per-user cache key isolation, api_token rotation invalidation.

fix: address qa-swarm convergent findings on cache-key contract

QA Swarm review surfaced two convergent issues plus a coverage gap; this
commit addresses all three:

1. SECRET_KEY rotation hazard (paul + qa-team + xp).
   Embed a 16-char SHA256 fingerprint of `settings.SECRET_KEY` in the
   cache key. On rotation the namespace partitions automatically -
   cached tokens signed with the old key become unreachable rather than
   served until TTL. No manual flush required.

2. Cache-key primitive obsession (qa-team + xp).
   Same change: hashing the secret + extracting the key construction
   into `_live_events_token_cache_key()` formalises the contract. The
   `:` separator collision risk for future api-token formats is moot
   now that the secret-derived prefix is in front, but extracting the
   key builder gives us one place to upgrade if needed.

3. user_id=None test coverage gap (paul + xp).
   Anonymous is the most common hot path. Parameterise the existing
   tests across (authenticated, anonymous) and add a dedicated test
   for SECRET_KEY rotation invalidation.

Also collapsed the four "mutation invalidates cache" tests into one
parameterised test per AGENTS.md preference for parameterised cases of
the same shape.

commits.message:
fix(llma): hash non-uuid trace ids in llm-gateway callback

Anthropic's `metadata.user_id` is co-opted by Claude Code as a trace
identifier and can arrive as a serialized JSON blob. The PostHog
callback in the LLM gateway forwarded it as `$ai_trace_id` verbatim,
producing trace records that could not be opened in LLM analytics
because `/llm-observability/traces/<id>` requires a URL-safe
identifier.

Normalize the value at capture time: pass through anything already
shaped like a UUID, and hash everything else into a deterministic UUID5
under a fixed namespace so the same JSON input keeps mapping to the
same trace id.

commits.message:
fix(taxonomic-filter): stop closed and empty result events from over-firing

The new dashboard's headline numbers — ~67% picker abandonment, 82% of
search users hitting a dead-end — looked too high to be real user
behaviour. Two analytics bugs were inflating both:

1) `taxonomic filter closed` was firing on every kea logic
   mount/unmount. The TaxonomicFilter logic mounts in many contexts
   where the picker isn't visibly opened (popover content rendered
   before the popover opens, side panels tied to scene lifecycle, route
   transitions...) so every involuntary mount fired a close with
   hadSelection=false. Top sessions had 100+ closes — clearly not user
   behaviour. Gate the capture on a new `cache.hadInteraction` flag set
   by real user-driven actions: keyboard nav (moveUp/moveDown,
   tabLeft/tabRight, setActiveTab), search input typing/clearing
   (markUserInteraction wired into _onChange — distinguishes from the
   controlled-prop useEffect path that calls setSearchQuery directly),
   and the existing hadSelection.

2) `taxonomic filter empty result` was firing per list, not per search.
   Every tab runs the search in parallel — typing 'email' commonly
   fires 4-8 empty events from background tabs the user can't see, so
   the dead-end metric counted phantom dead-ends. Gate on the existing
   `isActiveTab` selector so empties only fire from the visible tab.

Adds parameterised tests for both gates: closed event only fires after
typing or selection (not on bare mount/unmount), empty result only
fires for the active tab and not for background tabs.

commits.message:
chore(proxy): extract cloudflare client into posthog/proxy/

Move posthog/temporal/proxy_service/cloudflare.py to posthog/proxy/
to host non-Temporal-specific reverse proxy code. The Cloudflare
client is consumed by upcoming sync code paths (diagnose endpoint)
in addition to the existing Temporal workflows, and the import path

commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
feat(proxy): add reverse proxy diagnostics module

Adds a synchronous diagnose() function that runs six checks against a
ProxyRecord and returns a structured DiagnosticReport: DNS CNAME alignment,
Cloudflare custom hostname state, CAA records walked up the customer's DNS
tree, HTTP-01 challenge reachability, live event probe, and certificate
expiry. Each check produces a CheckResult with a vendor-neutral
PostHog-flavored message and (where applicable) a Remediation block listing
exact DNS records the customer should add.

The check pipeline honors skip rules: when SSL is already active we don't
re-walk CAA or probe the challenge URL; when the live event passes we treat
the proxy as healthy regardless of upstream warnings. The ReportSummary
exposes the most actionable issue and a one-line next_action.

Also relocates this work from posthog/proxy/ to products/proxy/backend/ to
follow the products/ convention. The Cloudflare client picks up new fields
on CustomHostnameSSL (http_url, http_body, certificate_authority,
validation_records) needed by the CAA and HTTP-01 checks; existing call
sites in the Temporal monitor/create/delete activities are unaffected.

The new endpoint, MCP tool, and frontend land in subsequent commits.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
refactor(proxy): relocate diagnostics into platform_features product

The reverse proxy is part of the existing platform_features product, so
diagnostics, messages, and the Cloudflare client belong as a peer subdomain
to org_intelligence/ — not in a standalone products/proxy/ directory.

Moves files into products/platform_features/backend/proxy/ and renames the
test files to test_proxy_cloudflare.py / test_proxy_diagnostics.py to slot
into the central tests/ directory matching the convention. Import sites
in the Temporal workflows updated accordingly. No behavior change.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
feat(proxy): add diagnose endpoint to ProxyRecordViewset

POST /api/organizations/{org_id}/proxy_records/{id}/diagnose/

Wires the on-demand diagnostic pipeline behind a typed DRF action.
Response is a structured DiagnosticReport (summary + per-check
results) so the frontend and MCP can render it without parsing
free text. Inherits OrganizationAdminWritePermissions from the
viewset; non-admins get 403, unknown ids get 404.

Adds five response serializers (DiagnosticReportSerializer and
its nested types) with help_text on every field and explicit
choice lists, so the generated frontend types and downstream MCP
schemas come through fully typed. Regenerated services/mcp/src/api/
generated.ts surfaces operation_id proxy_records_diagnose_create
ready for the MCP yaml entry in the next commit.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
feat(proxy): expose proxy-diagnose as MCP tool

Adds a proxy-diagnose entry to services/mcp/definitions/proxy-records.yaml
referencing operation proxy_records_diagnose_create. The codegen produces
the handler, Zod schema, and combined tool registry — total enabled MCP
operations goes from 289 to 290.

Scoped organization:write to match the underlying viewset's admin
permission requirement (the OAuth scope must align with what the endpoint
actually accepts; otherwise read-only tokens hit 403 at runtime). Marked
readOnly:true since the endpoint inspects state without mutating, and
idempotent:false because each call performs live network probes.

Now an AI agent can call proxy-diagnose alongside proxy-get and explain
to a user exactly why their reverse proxy is stuck — including the exact
DNS records they need to add for CAA-blocked validations.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
fix(proxy): backfill ProxyRecord.message on create-time errors

Previously, when CreateManagedProxyWorkflow caught an ActivityError or
generic Exception it set status=ERRORING but left message=NULL, forcing
debugging through Temporal UI even when the underlying cause was obvious.
This was particularly painful for stuck Cloudflare validations
(e.g. 'wait_for_cloudflare_certificate: Certificate not yet ready,
status: pending_validation') where the activity exception already carries
a clear summary that just wasn't being persisted.

Adds two small helpers — _describe_activity_failure and
_describe_workflow_failure — that produce a short, truncated string
(<=800 chars to stay within the 1024 column) from the captured exception,
and threads them into the two ERRORING update sites. Monitor workflow
already does this for its check failures via errors[]/warnings[]; this
brings the create workflow to parity.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
feat(proxy): in-app diagnose button and report panel

Adds a Diagnose entry to the per-record action menu in the Reverse
proxy settings page. Clicking calls the new diagnose endpoint and
renders the structured report inline above the table:

- Summary banner colored by overall status with the next-action
  sentence
- Per-check row with status icon, check name, and customer-facing
  detail
- For checks that produced a Remediation, a code snippet showing
  the exact DNS records to add (e.g. CAA records for the most
  common stuck-validation case)
- Dismissable per-record so multiple proxies can be diagnosed in
  parallel

The kea logic gains diagnose / diagnoseSuccess / diagnoseFailure /
clearDiagnosticReport actions, a per-id diagnosticReports map, and
a diagnoseLoadingIds list to guard the menu while a request is in
flight.

Note: this scene's API calls still use the lib/api shim and
handwritten ProxyRecord types — migrating to generated API types
(adopting-generated-api-types skill) is a separate cleanup since
the proxy_records endpoints aren't currently included in
frontend/src/generated/core/.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
refactor(proxy): render diagnostics inside the row's tab section

Drops the standalone DiagnosticReportPanel banner above the table and
moves the report into a second 'Diagnosis' tab inside the existing
expandable row, alongside the CNAME tab. The Diagnosis tab is only
present when there's a report for that record.

Clicking Diagnose now also auto-expands the row and switches the active
tab to Diagnosis (via a listener on diagnoseSuccess), so the user sees
the result in context without an extra click. Manual expand/collapse and
tab switching are tracked in kea state (expandedRecordIds and
recordActiveTabs reducers) so the row's selection survives re-renders
and is cleared along with the report.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
fix(proxy): render diagnostic detail strings as markdown

Customer-facing diagnostic strings use backtick-delimited inline code
(domain names, DNS values) so they need LemonMarkdown rendering.
Without it the literal backticks leaked into the UI.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
fix(proxy): drop summary banner and inline DNS values from prose

The diagnostic report's top summary banner duplicated information
already shown in the per-check rows and was prone to producing
unreadable strings when interpolated values had trailing dots
(e.g. CNAME targets shown as 'foo..' from sentence period after FQDN).

The CNAME check messages now also drop the target_cname value from
prose entirely. The same value is already rendered in the
CodeSnippet block under the remediation summary, so the inline
duplication added noise without adding information. The CodeSnippet
now uses the trailing-dot-stripped form so the value pastes cleanly
into DNS provider UIs.

Result: the report tab shows a 'Ran <time>' timestamp followed by
clean per-check rows, with each fail's exact DNS records in their
own copy-friendly snippet.
commits.author: yasen-posthog
