commits.message:
feat(proxy): expose proxy diagnose to PostHog AI as MaxTool

Wires the diagnose pipeline into Max chat as a contextual tool, so a user
on the reverse proxy settings page can ask Max "why is e.foo.com erroring?"
and get back the structured report directly in chat — no MCP install
required.

The DiagnoseProxyTool calls diagnose() in-process (no HTTP round-trip),
filters records by the user's organization in _get_record (the actual
security boundary), and returns both a markdown summary the LLM relays
and a structured artifact that future Max UI can render natively.

The tool is contextual — surfaced only while ManagedReverseProxy is on
screen — and ships with a context prompt template that injects the
visible records so Max can resolve "diagnose <domain>" to a record id.
A suggestion is wired in for any erroring/timed_out record.

Also drops the rstrip(".") on target_cname in the cname check; values
flow through in their stored canonical form, matching what's persisted
on the row.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
refactor(proxy): collocate diagnostics in posthog/ to clear tach boundaries

Tach was failing on cross-module imports between posthog and
products.platform_features in both directions. Reverts the relocation:
diagnostics, cloudflare client, and tests live next to the model and
viewset they serve, so no boundary is crossed.

- products/platform_features/backend/proxy/cloudflare.py back to
  posthog/temporal/proxy_service/cloudflare.py (its original home)
- products/platform_features/backend/proxy/diagnostics.py +
  messages.py merged into posthog/api/proxy_record_diagnostics.py;
  message helpers are now private (_msg_*) since they're not
  referenced outside the module
- Tests collocated under posthog/api/test/ and
  posthog/temporal/proxy_service/test/

The MaxTool stays at products/platform_features/backend/max_tools.py
(MaxTool registry auto-discovers per-product), and tach.toml gains
posthog and ee in platform_features.depends_on so the file's imports
of ProxyRecord, capture_exception, MaxTool, and the diagnose helper
are all valid.

No behavior change; 21 diagnostics tests + 5 cloudflare tests +
the broader proxy regression set all pass locally.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
fix(proxy): harden cert expiry parsing in diagnostics

Addresses Greptile P1+P2: a malformed `notAfter` value in the parsed
certificate (unexpected type or wrong strptime format) could raise
ValueError outside the wrapped except block and bubble up to the API
view as HTTP 500. Replaces the bare `assert isinstance` (which `-O`
strips) with an explicit type guard, and wraps the strptime in
try/except ValueError. Both failure paths now return a graceful warn
CheckResult.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
fix(proxy): patch three security findings in diagnostics

- Block redirects in the live event probe (allow_redirects=False), so a
  controlled-domain admin can't redirect us to internal targets like
  cloud metadata endpoints. Same protection _check_http_challenge
  already had.
- Use the raw socket as a context manager in the cert expiry check so
  the file descriptor closes even when wrap_socket() raises before the
  inner ssl-wrapped context manager takes ownership.
- Add an explicit OrganizationMembership.Level >= ADMIN check at the
  top of DiagnoseProxyTool._arun_impl so non-admin members can't ask
  Max to invoke a diagnostic that the REST endpoint restricts to
  admins. Done by hand because MaxTool's resource-level RBAC doesn't
  recognize membership level (org owners would otherwise fail it).
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
fix(proxy): exempt diagnose_proxy from MaxTool access-control declaration test

CI test_all_tools_have_access_control_or_are_exempt requires every
MaxTool to either implement get_required_resource_access() or be
listed in TOOLS_WITHOUT_ACCESS_CONTROL with a reason. diagnose_proxy
deliberately uses an explicit OrganizationMembership.Level check
inside _arun_impl instead of resource-level RBAC (which doesn't
recognize membership level — owners would otherwise fail), so add it
to the exemption list with that rationale.
commits.author: yasen-posthog

commits.message:
refactor(proxy): apply review feedback batch

- Drop redundant dedent() on DIAGNOSE_PROXY_TOOL_DESCRIPTION; both
  module-level constants now use the same plain triple-quoted form
  (Reece nit on max_tools.py).
- Document that the live event probe sends a hardcoded test api_key
  intentionally — capture endpoint accepts unknown api_keys with 2xx,
  same payload the daily Temporal monitor uses.
- Per-(record, user) cooldown on POST .../diagnose/ (30s) using the
  Django cache, returning 429 on repeat. Bounds the amplification of
  outbound DNS/TLS/HTTP probes against the customer's domain.
- Rename CheckStatus values to past tense: pass→passed, warn→warned,
  fail→failed, skip→skipped (FE + BE). SummaryStatus left alone
  ('healthy', 'warn', 'fail') since it wasn't called out and "warned"
  is awkward as an overall report status.

Note: this commit changes source enum values but doesn't include the
regenerated artifacts (posthog/schema.py, services/mcp/src/generated/
proxy-records/api.ts, frontend schema). Local Postgres wasn't running
so `hogli build:openapi` couldn't be executed; CI's "generated types
in sync" check will catch it. Followup commit will land the regen.

commits.message:
perf(observability): cache positive get_default_event_info per team

The home view (`get_context_for_template`) calls `get_default_event_info`
once per request, which runs `EventDefinition.objects.filter(team=team,
name__in=["$pageview", "$screen"])`. Pganalyze shows this query at 740 ms
average, ~104k calls/day, 7.3% of all read runtime on prod-us writer -
the single biggest fixable target on the home view.

Cache the result for 24 hours, but only when `has_pageview or has_screen`
is true. A negative answer might just mean events have not been ingested
yet, so caching it would block teams from ever flipping to the positive
answer. Once true, the answer is monotonic in practice.

Adds two tests covering the positive/negative cache contract.

commits.message:
fix(observability): invalidate default-event-info cache on definition changes

Codex (P2), paul-reviewer, and qa-team converged on a real correctness gap
in the previous commit: Django-side admin updates and deletes via
EventDefinitionViewSet would leave the home view serving stale
`has_pageview` / `has_screen` for up to 24 hours after a team renamed or
removed `$pageview` / `$screen`.

Add a small `invalidate_default_event_info_cache(team_id)` helper and
wire pre_save/post_save/post_delete signals on `EventDefinition`:

- pre_save snapshots the old name on the instance so renames into or
  out of the default-event set are caught.
- post_save invalidates when either the new or the old name is in
  the default set.
- post_delete invalidates when the deleted definition's name is one
  of the defaults.

Unrelated event-definition changes do not invalidate, so the cache
still earns the win on the hot home-view path.

Tests cover create/delete, rename-out, rename-in, and the
unrelated-event-no-invalidation negative.

Note: rust property-defs ingestion bypasses Django ORM and therefore
these signals - that is by design, since negative results are not
cached, so the first ingested $pageview from a brand-new team will
miss cache and re-query. Only ORM-driven changes need the explicit
invalidation hook.

author: pauldambra

commits.message:
perf(event-definitions): index posthog_eventdefinition on (team_id, name)

The hot home-view query

  SELECT name FROM posthog_eventdefinition
  WHERE name IN ('$pageview', '$screen') AND team_id = X

is the largest single read on prod-us writer (~7.3% of all read time, 740 ms
average over ~104k calls/day per pganalyze). None of the existing indexes
match this filter shape:
- (project_id) does not cover team_id lookups
- the GIN index on name is fuzzy-search optimized
- the partial team_id index requires enforcement_mode='reject'
- the unique expression on (coalesce(project_id, team_id), name) does not
  match a plain team_id = X predicate

Add a regular btree on (team_id, name) so the planner has an exact match
for the common shape. Sister PR #57327 caches the home-view caller of this
query when the answer is positive, so most page loads will skip the query
entirely - this index covers the misses and any other call sites that
filter by team_id + name.

author: webjunkie

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body: Copilot wasn't able to review any files in this pull request. --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: The automated gates denied this PR due to a public_api deny-list match and T2-never classification. The change is a reasonable devex fix to a build script, but it needs a human to override the gate denial and verify the mtime-based detection logic is correct across all CI environments (e.g., filesystem timestamp precision, concurrent writes).

commits.message:
fix(devex): make openapi codegen exit non-zero on silent orval no-ops

orval's `generate()` resolves "fulfilled" even when a per-product slice fails OpenAPI validation (e.g. INVALID_REFERENCE on shared `components.parameters` $refs). The script reported `✓ <product>:fetch` and exited 0 despite no file being written. CI's `git diff --exit-code` gate in `ci-backend.yml` couldn't see this either: orval no-op + stale committed files = no diff to detect, so the gate passed for the wrong reason.

Two layered fixes:

Snapshot expected output mtimes before the orval run, then reclassify any "fulfilled" job whose output file wasn't actually written as `rejected`. Catches both the "no file" and "stale file" cases — anything where mtime didn't move past its pre-run value.

Exit non-zero from the script when any job failed. The existing failed counter was only printed in a summary line; nothing propagated up to the `hogli build:openapi` wrapper, so the diff gate was effectively the only signal.

With both in place a future regression like #56865 (which broke per-product slicing for two days because the slicer was dropping `components.parameters`) would fail `hogli build:openapi` directly, before ever reaching the diff check.

This PR is independent of #57349 (the slicer-parameters fix). #57349 should land first to bring the regen back to green; this PR then ensures the next time the pipeline silently breaks, CI catches it.
commits.author: webjunkie

title: fix(devex): per-product openapi slicer was dropping components.parameters
author: webjunkie

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body: Copilot wasn't able to review any files in this pull request. --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: Gates denied this PR due to migrations and public API changes across multiple team boundaries. This is a cross-team change touching @PostHog/logs and @PostHog/team-data-stack areas, and needs review from those teams before auto-approval.

commits.message:
fix(devex): per-product openapi slicer was dropping components.parameters

#56865 hoisted `project_id` / `environment_id` / `organization_id` from inline path-params into reusable `components.parameters` ($ref'd from each operation). Good cleanup at the unified-spec level.

`frontend/bin/generate-openapi-types.mjs` slices that unified spec into per-product subsets before feeding each one to orval. The slicer was rebuilding `components` with only `schemas`, so every per-product slice lost the parameters bucket. Each operation's `$ref: #/components/parameters/ProjectIdPath` then failed orval validation with INVALID_REFERENCE → orval silently wrote nothing → exit 0.

Fallout that wasn't caught:
- `git diff --exit-code` after `hogli build:openapi` returned clean (orval no-op + stale on-disk files = no diff to detect)
- Every product's `api.schemas.ts` has been frozen at the last successful regen on Apr 30 12:31, picking up serializer changes only when they happened to coincide with a working regen
- 8 products had pending type updates pending in the queue (data_warehouse, integrations, logs, replay, session_summaries, tasks, mcp_analytics, visual_review)

Fix: inline the full top-level `components` bucket (parameters, securitySchemes, anything else) verbatim into each per-product slice, then substitute the filtered schemas. The slice is virtual (lives in a tempdir for the duration of orval's run, then gets deleted), so the duplication has zero runtime or repo footprint.

Including the catch-up regen in this commit so master ends up consistent with what's actually in serializers.

Follow-up worth filing separately: the script should propagate orval's validation failures as a non-zero exit, otherwise the diff-based CI gate in ci-backend.yml will keep passing on broken pipelines like this one did.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(logs): align scope_attribute_filters cast with regenerated schema

A backend tightening (path_drop sampling: explicit shape on `scope_attribute_filters`) had been queued but not flowing into the FE because the orval slicer was silently no-op'ing all per-product regen since #56865. Now that the slicer is unblocked, the regenerated `PatchedLogsSamplingRuleApi` declares `scope_attribute_filters?: { [key: string]: unknown }[]` instead of the old permissive `unknown` — and the existing `as unknown[]` cast no longer satisfies it.

Cast to the structural type the regenerated interface advertises so this assignment stays in sync with whatever the backend serializer says is on the wire.

title: feat(flags): Add bucketing change safeguards for v2 UI
author: gustavohstrassburger

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body:
## Pull request overview Adds safeguards around feature flag bucketing changes in the v2 UI and enforces backend validation to prevent incompatible “device ID bucketing + persist across auth” configurations, including a data migration intended to auto-fix existing invalid flags with an audit trail. **Changes:** - Frontend: adds confirmation dialogs when changing bucketing options, auto-disables “persist across auth” when switching to device bucketing, and hides the persistence toggle for device bucketing. - Backend: adds serializer validation to reject new invalid combinations while allowing existing “grandfathered” ones to be saved. - Data migration: attempts to disable `ensure_experience_continuity` for existing device-bucketing flags and write an ActivityLog entry per fix. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | posthog/migrations/max_migration.txt | Bumps max migration pointer to 1140. | | posthog/migrations/1140_fix_device_bucketing_persist_across_auth.py | Data migration to disable invalid device bucketing + persistence and log activity. | | posthog/api/test/test_feature_flag.py | Adds tests for create-time validation and grandfathered update. | | posthog/api/feature_flag.py | Adds serializer validation for the incompatible combination (including early-return paths). | | frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/FeatureFlagReleaseConditionsCollapsible.tsx | Adds bucketing-change confirmation dialog for existing flags. | | frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/FeatureFlagReleaseConditions.tsx | Adds bucketing-change confirmation dialog + auto-disable persist on device bucketing. | | frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/FeatureFlagForm.tsx | Hides persistence option for device bucketing and auto-disables persist when switching to device bucketing. |
--- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

reviews.author: dmarticus
reviews.body:
A few things from a fresh pass that didn't show up in the existing reviews:

### State overwrite race in `FeatureFlagReleaseConditions.tsx` silently loses the bucketing change

`frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/FeatureFlagReleaseConditions.tsx:675-684`

```tsx
} else if (targetValue === 'device') {
    setAggregationGroupTypeIndex(null)
    setBucketingIdentifier(FeatureFlagBucketingIdentifier.DEVICE_ID)  // 1) writes device_id
    if (featureFlag.ensure_experience_continuity) {
        setFeatureFlag({ ...featureFlag, ensure_experience_continuity: false })  // 2) clobbers (1)
    }
}
```

The `setFeatureFlag` reducer in `featureFlagLogic.ts:698-700` replaces the entire `featureFlag` state with the action payload, and the closure-captured `featureFlag` here still has the OLD `bucketing_identifier`. So step 2 wipes out the `device_id` write from step 1.

Net effect for an existing flag with `distinct_id` + persist=on: user clicks Device, confirms the dialog, and the flag ends up with `bucketing_identifier=distinct_id` (unchanged) + `ensure_experience_continuity=false`. The radio just appears to silently revert.

Compare to `FeatureFlagForm.tsx:1062-1074`, where the order is reversed (`setFeatureFlag` first, then `setBucketingIdentifier`) and it works correctly. Cleanest fix is a single combined `setFeatureFlag` call so it stays atomic.

### PR description vs. implementation mismatch on Group/Mixed

The description says "auto-disable persist across auth when switching from User to Device/Group/Mixed bucketing", but the code only auto-disables on Device. The Group/Mixed branches in `FeatureFlagForm.tsx` and `FeatureFlagReleaseConditionsCollapsible.tsx` never touch `ensure_experience_continuity`. Either the description or the coverage is wrong.

### Survey + other early-return paths bypass the new validation

`posthog/api/feature_flag.py:777-791` — `validate()` returns early when `request` is missing, when `creation_context == \"surveys\"`, or when `get_team` is missing. None of those branches call `_validate_device_bucketing_with_persist_auth`, so a survey-created flag (or any path missing one of those bits of context) can still slip through with `device_id + ensure_experience_continuity=True`.

Cleaner shape: call `_validate_device_bucketing_with_persist_auth(attrs)` once at the top of `validate()` right after `super().validate(attrs)`, and drop the three duplicate calls. The `# MOVED VALIDATION HERE - before early return` comments are "what changed" notes that belong in the PR body, not the code.

### Migration doesn't invalidate the flags cache

`posthog/models/feature_flag/flags_cache.py:845-846` and `posthog/models/feature_flag/local_evaluation.py:856-857` register `post_save`/`post_delete` receivers against `sender=FeatureFlag` (the runtime class). Inside a Django migration, `apps.get_model(\"posthog\", \"FeatureFlag\")` returns the historical model — a different class — so those receivers don't fire when the migration calls `flag.save()`. Affected flags will keep serving cached evaluations with `ensure_experience_continuity=True` until cache TTL expires or another flag write triggers invalidation. Worth either invalidating explicitly inside the migration or documenting the staleness window.

### Missing test case

The three new tests cover create-blocked, create-allowed, and grandfathered-update-allowed. They don't cover the obvious negative case for updates: an existing flag with `device_id` + `ensure_experience_continuity=False` being PATCHed to set `ensure_experience_continuity=True`. That should be blocked, and right now nothing in the suite asserts it.

---

<details>
<summary>📋 Paste-into-agent prompt to fix all of this</summary>

\`\`\`
Address review feedback on PR #57338 (gustavo/flags-ui-change-bucketing-warning).

1. Fix the state-overwrite bug in frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/FeatureFlagReleaseConditions.tsx
   around lines 675-684. The 'device' branch currently calls setBucketingIdentifier(DEVICE_ID)
   followed by setFeatureFlag({...featureFlag, ensure_experience_continuity: false}). The
   second call replaces the entire featureFlag state with the closure-captured value, which
   still has the OLD bucketing_identifier — so the device_id write is silently reverted.
   Replace those two calls with a single setFeatureFlag({...featureFlag, bucketing_identifier:
   FeatureFlagBucketingIdentifier.DEVICE_ID, ensure_experience_continuity: false }) so the
   update is atomic. Verify the behavior of setFeatureFlag against the reducer in
   frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/featureFlagLogic.ts (around line 698) before you change it.

2. Resolve the PR description vs implementation mismatch. The description claims auto-disable
   on switching to Device/Group/Mixed, but only Device is wired up. Decide the intended
   behavior, then either (a) extend FeatureFlagForm.tsx and FeatureFlagReleaseConditionsCollapsible.tsx
   to also clear ensure_experience_continuity for Group and Mixed, or (b) update the PR
   description and any user-facing copy to say Device only.

3. In posthog/api/feature_flag.py validate(), move the call to
   _validate_device_bucketing_with_persist_auth(attrs) to the very top of validate() (right
   after super().validate(attrs)) so it runs on every code path, including the
   creation_context == 'surveys' early return and the missing-request / missing-get_team
   paths. Remove the three existing call sites and the '# MOVED VALIDATION HERE' comments.

4. In posthog/migrations/1140_fix_device_bucketing_persist_across_auth.py:
   - Change select_related('team') to select_related('team__organization') to avoid an N+1
     when reading flag.team.organization for each ActivityLog row.
   - Drop the unused 'count' variable and the trailing comment about it.
   - Add explicit cache invalidation for affected flags. Look at how
     posthog/models/feature_flag/flags_cache.py and local_evaluation.py invalidate caches in
     their post_save receivers, then call the equivalent helpers (or bust the relevant Redis
     keys) for each updated flag — apps.get_model() returns the historical class, so the
     existing post_save receivers won't fire automatically.

5. Add a test in posthog/api/test/test_feature_flag.py covering the missing case: an existing
   flag with bucketing_identifier='device_id' and ensure_experience_continuity=False that gets
   PATCHed to set ensure_experience_continuity=True should return 400 with the validation
   error. While you're there, collapse the three new validation tests into a single
   parameterized test using the parameterized library, since they share most of the setup.

After each change run the relevant tests:
- hogli test posthog/api/test/test_feature_flag.py -k 'device_bucketing or grandfathered'
- pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend typescript:check
\`\`\`

Comments suppressed due to low confidence (1) **products/visual_review/backend/tests/test_baselines.py:100** * This comment still references “sparkline window tests”, but the sparkline has been removed. Updating it to reflect the current reason for backdating `created_at` (e.g. ordering/windowing for overview/drift tests) would reduce confusion. ``` if created_offset: # Force created_at backwards for sparkline window tests. target = timezone.now() - created_offset RunSnapshot.objects.filter(id=snap.id).update(created_at=target) # Also push the parent run's created_at — sparkline filters on run.created_at. ```

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: Gates denied due to size (503 lines, just over the 500-line ceiling). The change is coherent and the author owns the area, but the size gate requires a human reviewer to sign off. Request a review from a teammate on @PostHog/team-devex before re-requesting auto-approval.

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): drop overview sparkline, swap in cheap stability signals

The 30-day daily-bucket sparkline computed per identifier × per day OOM-killed the web pod once the universe fix landed and started returning ~3000 identifiers instead of 3 (a single in-flight pending master run was hiding the real universe). Even with SQL pre-aggregation it took 5-7s on prod because the WindowAgg sort ran over ~2.85M RunSnapshot rows on every request — irreducible without a materialized rollup, and the user explicitly didn't want one.

Replace the sparkline with two cheap aggregates that drive the same product use cases (frequency vs severity sort axes):

`baseline_change_count` (lifetime): COUNT(*) WHERE result IN (CHANGED, REMOVED) on default-branch completed runs. Real baseline flips on master leave a CHANGED/REMOVED row in the run that introduced them; subsequent runs see UNCHANGED against the new YAML baseline. The `snapshot_run_result` index on (run_id, result) bitmap-scans straight to the rare event rows. ~12ms on prod's busiest test repo.

`recent_drift_avg`: AVG(diff_percentage) over the last 10 default-branch completed runs (BASELINE_DRIFT_RECENT_RUN_COUNT). Bounded by run count, not time window, so a busy CI doesn't drag in proportionally more rows. Two-stage query (resolve run IDs first, then aggregate via PK-indexed run_id__in) keeps Postgres from inlining a CTE that scans the full RunSnapshot table. ~27ms on prod.

Total endpoint time on the 2978-identifier test repo: ~350ms cold (was 5-7s + OOM). Universe hydrate (151ms, fetching 2978 rows with thumbnail joins) is now the dominant cost — separate optimisation later.

Frontend updates:
- Drop the 30-day per-day sparkline chart from cards. Replace with a "↻ N" badge tooltipped "Baseline updated N times since inception".
- Sort axis "drift severity" now keys on recent_drift_avg, then baseline_change_count, then tolerate_count_30d as a tiebreak. Adds the change count as a meaningful secondary axis.
- Move the "X of Y snapshots" indicator from the search-toolbar to directly above the grid where it's visually associated with the cards. The user wasn't noticing it before.

Drive-by infra fix in `frontend/bin/generate-openapi-types.mjs`: the per-product schema slicer was rebuilding `components` with only `schemas`, dropping `parameters`. That meant the per-product paths' `#/components/parameters/ProjectIdPath` refs failed validation, orval silently wrote nothing, and every product's api.schemas.ts has been stuck on Apr 30 since the issue started. Inline the full `components.parameters` (and any other top-level component buckets we don't slice) verbatim per product.

API surface change: BaselineSparklineDay and BASELINE_SPARKLINE_DAYS removed from contracts; BaselineEntry loses `sparkline` and `recent_diff_avg`, gains `baseline_change_count` and `recent_drift_avg`. Generated TS regenerated; serializer simplified. Old test for daily buckets replaced with two tests covering the new fields plus a no-signal case.

fix(visual-review): drop raw SQL, scope change_count to universe

Replace Run.objects.raw() window-function query with K cheap per-run_type
LIMIT queries. Postgres can't filter on a window function and the ORM
doesn't auto-wrap the annotation in a subquery, so a small loop over the
distinct run_types (typically ~4) is the cleanest pure-ORM 1:1.

Also scope the change_count_by_key aggregate to identifier__in=
universe_identifiers so we don't aggregate CHANGED/REMOVED rows for
identifiers we'll throw away in Python anyway.

Clears semgrep avoid-raw-sql block and the hardcoded-table-name nit.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): keep raw window query, suppress semgrep

Reverts the per-run_type ORM loop and the universe_identifiers filter on
change_count_by_key — both regressed under benchmark on prod
(repo with 30k runs, 2154 distinct run_types):

  raw window query:       4ms
  ORM loop equivalent:    5600ms (1 distinct + 2154 LIMIT queries)

  change_count without identifier filter:  14ms (523 rows)
  change_count with identifier__in[3004]:  34ms (523 rows, no rows skipped)

The window function is the right tool — Postgres can't filter on a
window result, the ORM doesn't auto-wrap it, and a per-run_type loop
explodes when each Storybook story shows up as its own run_type.
The aggregate already returns only universe rows, so adding identifier__in
pure overhead with no benefit.

Switch the literal table name to Run._meta.db_table and add nosemgrep
markers with justification: query is parameterized via %s binding, no
string concatenation of user input, table name comes from model meta.

author: pauldambra

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: Gates denied this PR because it contains a Django migration, which requires human review per policy. Migration changes need a team member to verify safety (e.g., non-blocking index creation, rollback implications).

commits.message:
perf(insights): index InsightViewed on (insight_id, last_viewed_at DESC)

The insights list endpoint runs a correlated subquery per row to fetch
the most recent insightviewed.last_viewed_at. Without a supporting index,
each subquery does an index scan on the FK (insight_id) and then sorts
by last_viewed_at to pick the max - slow for popular insights with many
view rows.

Add a composite index on (insight_id, -last_viewed_at) so the subquery
becomes a single-row index lookup with no sort.

title: refactor(hogli): lazy-load Click commands via manifest
author: rnegron

reviews.author: webjunkie
reviews.body: Quick glance: Looks like a worthwile refactor 👍🏻

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: The PR is too large for automated review (30 files, 1295 lines). It's a developer tooling refactor by the owning team author with one positive human review, but the size gate requires human sign-off. Get a second review from a team-devex teammate before merging.

reviews.author: webjunkie
reviews.body:
> _Agent-based review — drove `hogli` from a fresh `/tmp` project (uv editable install, hand-written manifest + 3 click commands, exercised happy + error paths)._

The lazy mechanism itself is solid — `--help` listed all my commands without firing the `[import] ...` markers I planted, each invocation imported only the matching module, and the four error branches in `resolve_click_command` (bad import, bad attr, name drift, unknown command) all produced clean `Error: hogli: command 'X' ...` messages. Two-phase `format_commands` (eager `self.commands` pass, then manifest pass for lazy entries reading `description:` from YAML) is the right shape — it keeps the lazy path clean without forking the help formatter.

A handful of things I'd flag, rough priority — none blocking:

**1. Help-text drift between manifest and click docstring (medium)**
Top-level `hogli --help` reads `config.description` from YAML (`cli.py:126`). Per-command `hogli <cmd> --help` reads the click docstring. Nothing keeps them in sync — guaranteed source of \"why does the listing say X but the help say Y\" tickets. Either lint it (cheap, doesn't import — just check non-empty) or document the convention in `tools/hogli/README.md`.

**2. Empty `description:` is silently allowed (minor)**
`config.get(\"description\", \"\")` on `cli.py:126` — a lazy command without `description:` renders a blank short-help line. With non-lazy commands click would surface the docstring. Either require `description:` for `click:` entries or fall back to \"(see `hogli <cmd> --help`)\".

**3. Lazy validation was dropped — what's the new safety net? (medium, deliberate)**
`ab87f26` removed pre-flight checks; `meta:check` (`validate.py:48`) now only covers `bin_script` entries. A typo in `click: foo.bar:baz` is invisible until someone runs the command. Probably fine if test coverage hits every command, but worth confirming what replaces that guard — could be a CI-only `meta:check-lazy` that imports each `click:` once and reports failures.

**4. `cli.py:177` skips auto-update on a non-existent subcommand**
```python
if ctx.invoked_subcommand not in {\"meta:check\", \"help\"} and not in_git_hook:
```
There's no `help` subcommand — `--help` is a click flag and `invoked_subcommand` is `None` at that point. Either dead code or the intended \"don't mutate the manifest while showing help\" guard isn't actually firing. Easy fix or easy delete.

**5. Boot modules erode the lazy win silently (minor)**
`_load_boot_modules` (`cli.py:299`) runs at CLI module-import time on every invocation. The whole point of lazy commands is paying for what you use — if `boot_modules:` grows heavy, the win is gone with no warning. Worth a schema-doc note and maybe a `HOGLI_DEBUG_TIMING=1` knob that prints per-boot-module import time.

**6. `name:` on the click decorator is mandatory but easy to forget (docs)**
`resolve_click_command` enforces `command.name == command_name` (`lazy_commands.py:88`). For commands with colons (`hello:loud`), forgetting `name=\"hello:loud\"` produces a clear-once-you've-seen-it error. Worth a paragraph in `tools/hogli/README.md` under the `click:` section so first-timers don't trip on it.

**7. Path bootstrap overlaps in the common case (cosmetic)**
`add_repo_root_to_path` + `add_commands_dir_to_path` both add the repo root when `commands_dir:` lives there (the typical setup). Dedup guard in place, so harmless — but suggests the two helpers could collapse to one when the resolved path is the same.

**What I liked**
- `name-drift` detection in `resolve_click_command` — that's a real footgun blocker. Catches the case where someone drops `name=\"...\"` from the decorator and the manifest key silently stops matching.
- `HOGLI_MANIFEST` env var made the scratch test trivial — very useful for one-off scripts and isolated reproduction.
- Error messages from `resolve_click_command` all share the `hogli: command 'X' could not ...` prefix — consistent and surfacable.

Net: core change is good — approving. Most flags are docs / lint coverage / the deleted validation, not the lazy machinery itself.

reviews.body: Clean perf fix replacing MAX aggregate + GROUP BY with a correlated subquery. The one real concern (duplicate rows in search when multiple tags match) was caught and fully addressed: `.distinct()` added to the search branch, regression test included. All other filter branches are either already `.distinct()` or use subquery-style filters that don't produce duplicates.

commits.message:
perf(insights): drop GROUP BY by replacing Max(insightviewed) with Subquery

the insights list endpoint annotates last_viewed_at via
Max(insightviewed.last_viewed_at), which forces a GROUP BY across
dashboarditem.id, team.id, user.id. Postgres has to compute the
aggregate for every one of the team's insights before LIMIT can take
30, defeating the (team_id, last_modified_at DESC) partial index
short-circuit.

a recent trace on team 2's basic+saved=true page-load showed the
main SELECT still at 1.2 seconds even after the EXISTS fix in
#57275 — the Max annotation was the remaining culprit.

replace with a correlated Subquery that fetches the latest
last_viewed_at per insight without aggregation. Postgres can now
walk the partial index in last_modified_at order, evaluate the
saved/exists predicate per row, stop at 30 matches, and only run
the per-row subquery for those 30. expect ~1.2s -> <100ms on team 2.

commits.message:
feat(query-performance-ai): local-only autoresearch coordinator

Refactor of #56536 that drops the Django proxy + auth surface and instead
runs everything from a host-side coordinator. The coordinator sources
slow queries from Metabase, opens an HTTP port, and fans sandboxes out
that are network-isolated to that single port. Per-CLI flag, the
coordinator routes candidate SQL either to the test cluster (via
Metabase) or to a local ClickHouse (via sync_execute) — the sandbox
never knows which.

In test-cluster mode the coordinator's prompt addendum tells the agent
to rewrite team_id predicates to team_id = 1 before capturing a baseline.

fix(query-performance-ai): drop ipv6, allow dns, add curl diag in lockdown

Pi-coding-agent kept hitting "Connection error." despite the IPv4

commits.message:
fix(query-performance-ai): pin DNS allow rule to /etc/resolv.conf nameservers

The previous `iptables -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT` allowed UDP/53 to any
destination, which lets a sandboxed process DNS-tunnel data to an attacker-
controlled resolver by encoding it as subdomain queries. With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
in the sandbox env, that's a viable exfil path even after lockdown.

Pin the DNS rule to the resolvers in /etc/resolv.conf at lockdown time
(typically Docker's embedded 127.0.0.11), with a fallback to 127.0.0.11 if
the file is missing or empty so the lockdown doesn't drop all DNS on a
misconfigured container.

commits.message:
feat(query-performance-ai): get CH-side metrics from system.query_log on the metabase path

Previously MetabaseBackend reported `running_time` from Metabase's
response — that's Metabase's wall-clock for the full request, baking
in JDBC overhead and JSON serialisation, and gives no rows_read /
bytes_read / query_id. A faster-but-larger-result candidate could read
as slower because Metabase spends more time materialising rows.

Now we tag each candidate with a per-run `autoresearch_run_id` (16 hex
chars) inside the log_comment JSON, then poll
`clusterAllReplicas(posthog, system, query_log)` for the matching
QueryFinish row. CH-side `query_duration_ms`, `read_rows`,
`read_bytes`, `query_id` flow through to ExecutionResult.

The poll budget is 6 attempts × 1.5s (≈ 9s wall-clock max) to cover
ClickHouse's 7.5s default `flush_interval_milliseconds`. If the row
hasn't flushed inside that budget we fall back to `running_time` and
leave rows_read / bytes_read / query_id at None — same shape as
before.

commits.message:
feat(query-performance-ai): get CH-side metrics on the local backend too

Same shape as the metabase path: tag the candidate with an
autoresearch_run_id in log_comment, then look the row up in
system.query_log to get authoritative query_duration_ms / read_rows /
read_bytes / query_id. Without this LocalClickhouseBackend was
reporting wall-clock round-trip (TLS handshake + driver overhead
included) and None for everything else.

Local CH is single-node so we can `SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS` synchronously
on the same connection as the candidate query — no polling needed,
no extra TLS handshake. If FLUSH LOGS errors (permission / unsupported)
we still try the lookup; it'll either find the row that flushed
automatically or return None and the caller falls back to round-trip.

Refactored the lookup SQL builder + result-row parser into a small
`_query_log` helper module so both backends share the shape. Run-id
is 16 hex chars (regex-validated before SQL interpolation) so it can't
escape the string literal.

commits.message:
feat(insights): add TrendsBarChart hog-charts adapter for ActionsBar

Adds a hog-charts BarChart adapter for vertical stacked time-series
bars (ActionsBar display type). Behind the PRODUCT_ANALYTICS_HOG_CHARTS
flag, ActionsBar now routes to the d3-based TrendsBarChart instead of
the Chart.js ActionsLineGraph fallback. Lifecycle and stickiness still
fall through to the legacy renderer.

Mirrors the trends-line-chart adapter shape: pure transforms in
trendsBarChartTransforms.ts (buildTrendsBarTimeSeries +
buildTrendsBarChartConfig), an injectable click handler that resolves
the clicked series + day index back to the actors-by-day query, and a
kea adapter that wires trendsDataLogic into hog-charts BarChart. Reuses
TrendsTooltip for hover, supports breakdown colors, hidden-series
toggling, and the percent-stack view.

ActionsBarValue (horizontal aggregated bars) is intentionally not
included here — that variant has a sparse-stacking layout and a
different click resolution and lands as a follow-up PR.

Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | products/data_warehouse/backend/api/external_data_source.py | Calls the new `webhook_inputs_updated` hook after webhook inputs are persisted. | | posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/common/base.py | Introduces the `WebhookSource.webhook_inputs_updated` extension point (no-op by default). | | posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/customer_io/api_client.py | Creates webhooks disabled by default and adds an `enable_webhook` API helper. | | posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/customer_io/source.py | Implements `webhook_inputs_updated` to enable the webhook when `signing_secret` is supplied. | | posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/customer_io/tests/test_api_client.py | Updates webhook creation expectations and adds coverage for `enable_webhook`. | | posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/customer_io/tests/test_customer_io_source.py | Adds tests for Customer.io’s `webhook_inputs_updated` behavior. | | products/data_warehouse/backend/api/test/test_external_data_source.py | Extends API tests to assert the source hook is called (and not called on validation failures). |

commits.message:
feat(data-warehouse): auto-enable Customer.io webhook on signing secret

Customer.io reporting webhooks 404 deliveries until the verifier on the
PostHog side has the signing secret. We now create the webhook in a

webhook_inputs_updated previously discarded the (success, error) result

title: perf(insights): use EXISTS instead of Count+HAVING for saved=true
author: pauldambra

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Clean perf optimization replacing COUNT+annotation+HAVING with EXISTS subquery; semantically equivalent, well-tested, no risk to production correctness.

commits.message:
perf(insights): use EXISTS instead of Count+HAVING for saved=true filter

the saved=true filter on the insights list endpoint compiles to GROUP
BY + HAVING(saved OR count(dashboard) >= 1). on team 2 (large org)
this forces postgres to compute visible_dashboards_count for every
insight before LIMIT can short-circuit, taking ~3 seconds.

EXISTS preserves the same semantics (saved insights, plus
unsaved-but-on-a-non-unlisted-dashboard insights) but lets the
planner walk the (team_id, last_modified_at) partial index in order
and stop after `limit` matches.

new parametrised test locks in the OR semantic across the four cases
(saved no-dashboard, unsaved+default, unsaved+template, unsaved+unlisted,
unsaved no-dashboard) so a future rewrite can't accidentally drop
the unsaved-on-dashboard rows.

reviews.body: Scoping `save()` to explicitly mutated fields is the correct Django idiom to prevent clobbering concurrent F-expression updates on `rows_synced`. The fix is minimal, the regression test is solid, and the only inline review comment was a minor style nit that's already resolved.

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): scope job-status save to avoid clobbering rows_synced

In V3 the consumer-side _mark_job_completed can race a still-pending
update_job_row_count F-update from the activity. update_external_job_status
loads the job, mutates status fields, then save()s the entire model — which
rewinds rows_synced to whatever was read at the top of the function. The
downstream emit_data_import_app_metrics then reports a stale (or zero)
rows_synced count.

Pin the save to the fields we actually mutate (status, latest_error,
finished_at, updated_at) so concurrent F-updates on rows_synced survive.

commits.message:
feat(mcp): add feedback-submit tool for agent feedback

Add a new MCP tool that lets agents submit structured feedback about
their experience using the PostHog MCP server. Feedback is captured as
a `mcp feedback submitted` event in PostHog and surfaces tool-level
issues (unclear descriptions, missing capabilities, confusing schemas)
that we can otherwise only learn about through manual inspection of
sessions.

The tool's input schema asks targeted questions designed for an LLM to
answer post-task: a one-sentence summary, sentiment, a single category
covering the dominant theme (tool_correctness, tool_description,
tool_input_schema, tool_output_format, missing_tool, instructions_clarity,
performance, error_message, other), whether the user's task was
completed, the tools that were called, friction points, the most
impactful suggested improvement, an anonymised paraphrase of the user
request, and freeform details.

Both v1 and v2 instruction templates now ask the agent to call
`feedback-submit` after finishing the user's task, with explicit
guidance on when to be especially proactive (unclear descriptions,
missing capabilities, unhelpful errors, etc.) and a reminder not to
include user PII or sensitive query content.

title: feat(insights): add sessionPropertyPreAggregation modifier
author: sampennington

commits.message:
feat(insights): add sessionPropertyPreAggregation modifier

Pre-filter the raw_sessions GROUP BY hash table by `session_id_v7 IN
(cheap pre-aggregation that only materializes the columns referenced
by the outer-WHERE session predicate)`. Useful when the breakdown/SELECT
pulls in many session columns (e.g. `\$channel_type`, ~7 argMinMerge
states per session) but the filter only references one (e.g.
`\$entry_current_url`) — without this, the aggregation hash table is
sized by every session in the date range and OOMs on large teams over
multi-month ranges.

Off by default; opt-in via `sessionPropertyPreAggregation=true`. The
helper short-circuits when the lifted predicate references the same
field set as the outer SELECT (no shrink, just doubled work) or when
no session-only predicate can be safely lifted.

Wired into both v2 and v3 sessions lazy joins. v3's
`select_from_sessions_table_v3` gains an `extra_where` parameter
mirroring v2.

fix(flags): surface full error chain from AWS SDK errors

AWS SDK errors have terse Display impls (e.g. "service error", "dispatch failure").
Actionable details (HTTP status, error codes, auth failures) only live in the error
source chain. Extract a helper to walk the chain and join with ": " so OperationFailed

title: fix(oauth-proxy): use client mapping for refresh_token when region KV expires
author: VojtechBartos

reviews.author: MattBro
reviews.body: Nice fix - root cause is right and the sequencing is safe. Two test gaps worth tightening before merge.

commits.message:
fix(oauth-proxy): use client mapping for refresh_token when region KV expires

The region selection KV entry has a 1-hour TTL, but the client mapping
(proxy client_id → regional client_ids) is permanent. When a refresh_token
request arrives after the region TTL expires, the proxy was falling through
to tryBothRegions which sends the raw proxy (US) client_id to both regions.
EU rejects it because it only knows its own EU client_id, and US rejects
the refresh token because it was issued by EU.

Now the proxy checks for a client mapping before the raw tryBothRegions
fallback, trying each region with the correctly rewritten client_id and
secret. On success it re-stores the region in KV so subsequent refreshes
take the fast path.
commits.author: VojtechBartos

resolveMappingRewrite helper in kv.ts, used by both proxyWithMapping

Add tests for: US-first success, both-regions-fail, authorization_code
with mapping (should still error), and JSON content type.

title: feat(provisioning): allow partners to override the provisioned PAT label
author: MattBro

commits.message:
feat(provisioning): allow partners to override the provisioned PAT label

Partners calling the agentic provisioning API previously got every PAT
labelled "Stripe Projects - {team_name}", regardless of which partner
provisioned it. Adds an optional `label_prefix` field on the request body
for /resources and /rotate_credentials so partners can pass their own
product name; falls back to the existing default when omitted.

Validation: rejects non-string, control characters, and prefixes longer
than 40 chars (matching the PersonalAPIKey.label CharField max_length).
Empty or whitespace-only values fall back to the default rather than
clobbering the label, so partners can't accidentally produce a PAT
labelled just " - {team_name}".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: MattBro

commits.message:
fix(provisioning): reject bidi/format chars, parametrize label_prefix tests

Pre-PR review tightening on the label_prefix validator:

- Reject Unicode Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp categories instead of only ASCII control
  chars + DEL. Cf includes bidi overrides (U+202A-U+202E) and isolates
  (U+2066-U+2069), which a partner could use to re-order surrounding text
  in the user's settings page (Trojan Source class).
- Collapse PROVISIONED_PAT_LABEL_MAX_LENGTH and the now-redundant
  PROVISIONED_PAT_LABEL_PREFIX_MAX_LENGTH into one constant. Both were 40
  and tracked the same DB column max_length; one is enough. Comment
  notes the link to PersonalAPIKey.label.
- Parametrize the label_prefix accepted/rejected and resolution tests
  per the team convention. Added bidi-override and zero-width-space
  cases while restructuring.
commits.author: MattBro

commits.message:
fix(provisioning): cap label_prefix at 25 chars to leave room for team name

Per greptile review feedback. The previous limit (40 chars) matched the
total label cap, which meant a 37+ char prefix consumed the whole label
after concatenation and the team name disappeared from the truncated
result. Cap the prefix at 25 chars instead, leaving 12+ chars for the
team name after " - ".

Also simplify the prefix-default fallback in _create_provisioned_pat:
_extract_label_prefix already normalises empty/whitespace to None, so
the inner .strip() was redundant and forced two places to track the
"empty -> default" rule.
commits.author: MattBro

commits.message:
fix(provisioning): capture invalid_label_prefix event on rotate path

Rotate endpoint now mirrors create endpoint and emits a credential_rotation
error event when label_prefix validation fails, so the failure shows up in
provisioning telemetry instead of silently 4xxing.

Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. Codex can also answer questions or update the PR. Try commenting "@codex address that feedback".

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: The bot reviewer raised a valid, unresolved React 18 concurrent-mode concern: `callbackRef.current = callback` is assigned during the render phase rather than in a `useLayoutEffect`, meaning an interrupted concurrent render could expose an uncommitted callback to the already-registered `visibilitychange` listener. This is a real pattern issue that needs a human to evaluate the tradeoff before auto-approving.

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Clean, well-tested React stable-ref fix. The concurrent-mode concern raised in review comments was addressed in the current diff (ref update moved into `useLayoutEffect`), and both inline comments are resolved. No production risk, no data model or API changes.

commits.message:
fix(perf): stabilise usePageVisibilityCb against parent re-renders

The previous fix re-fired the callback on every parent re-render whenever
a non-memoized inline function was passed (the effect's [callback] dep
changes identity each render). Consumers like ExperimentReloadAction and
PurePlayer pass inline lambdas, so each unrelated state update would
re-dispatch their visibility-change side effects (pause/resume, refetch,
etc.) — visibly more harmful than the original "no initial fire" bug.

Pivot to a ref-backed callback so:
- The mount-time invocation still fires once (the original goal).
- The visibilitychange listener stays registered for the component
  lifetime — no churn on re-renders.
- The latest callback identity is read lazily on each fire.

Added regression tests covering both the no-extra-fire case and the
"latest callback wins on the next event" case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: pauldambra

commits.message:
fix: address qa-swarm + codex review on render-phase ref mutation

Move the callbackRef.current = callback assignment from the render body
into a useLayoutEffect so it runs in the commit phase. An aborted /
restarted concurrent render can otherwise mutate the shared ref without
that render ever committing, briefly exposing an uncommitted callback
to the already-registered visibilitychange listener if an event fires
in that window.

Both chatgpt-codex (P2) and qa-team flagged this — convergent finding,
LOW probability in practice but free to fix.

reviews.body: ## Pull request overview Fixes two production issues in the Visual Review backend by changing how the baselines “universe” is selected and how snapshot history is deduped, to avoid pending-run collapse and to key history on baseline state rather than captured-artifact jitter. **Changes:** - Baselines overview universe: select the latest **COMPLETED** run per (repo, branch, run_type) instead of anchoring on `superseded_by IS NULL`. - Snapshot history: dedupe via `LAG(baseline_artifact_id)` (no `result` filter) to surface true baseline transitions and suppress tolerated-drift/pixel-jitter noise. - Tests: update history seeding to set `baseline_artifact`, rewrite assertions around baseline transitions, and add a regression test for pending-run universe collapse. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | products/visual_review/backend/logic.py | Updates snapshot-history dedupe SQL to use `baseline_artifact_id`; updates baselines-overview run selection to latest completed run via DISTINCT ON. | | products/visual_review/backend/tests/test_presentation.py | Updates snapshot-history integration test to seed baseline artifacts and assert baseline-transition behavior. | | products/visual_review/backend/tests/test_baselines.py | Adds regression test ensuring a pending run doesn’t replace the baselines-overview universe. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): anchor universe on completed runs and key history on baseline_artifact

The baselines overview universe was anchored on `superseded_by IS NULL`,
which collapses to whatever the latest run holds — including a freshly
started PENDING/PROCESSING master run that has 0 RunSnapshots ingested
yet. Prod showed exactly this: a single in-flight storybook run on
master with no snapshots yet, dragging the visible universe from ~2976
identifiers down to 3. Anchor on `status=COMPLETED` with `DISTINCT ON
(repo_id, branch, run_type)` instead, so the universe falls through to
the most recent fully-ingested run.

Snapshot history was using LAG on `current_artifact_id` plus a
`result IN (changed, new, removed)` filter to suppress pixel-jitter
noise. That kept hiding genuine first-appearance rows whose result
classifies as `unchanged` against an existing YAML baseline (every
master run after a snapshot lands), and on tolerated-drift stories the
artifact_id alternates between near-identical hashes the matcher keeps
absorbing — yielding hundreds of fake history events. LAG on
`baseline_artifact_id` solves both: pixel jitter and tolerated drift
leave the YAML baseline untouched, so they collapse naturally; real
baseline-update PRs move it, so transitions surface; first-appearance
rows are kept because the oldest row's LAG is NULL. No `result` filter
needed.

Verified on prod across 2 problem identifiers — counts match
expectation (1 false event → 2 real transitions on the original
99-no-op story; 1 single change → 3 lifecycle events on the
4-hours-ago story).

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): surface real Stripe credential errors

Two related UX bugs caused customers with valid Stripe permissions to see
misleading error messages when connecting Stripe as a data source:

1. validate_credentials() lumped every per-resource exception into
   StripePermissionError. An invalid/expired API key (401) thus surfaced
   as "lacks permissions for ALL 13 resources" — pushing users to grant
   permissions they already had. Now distinguishes 401 (raises new
   StripeAuthenticationError, short-circuits the loop) from 403
   (still per-resource permission gap).

2. OAuth token-exchange failures raised a bare Exception, which DRF
   turned into a 500 with no `detail` field — the frontend toast then
   fell back to a generic "Something went wrong". Now raises
   ValidationError with the provider's `error_description` extracted
   from the response body, and tolerates non-JSON error bodies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): include Invoice items perm + show Stripe error per resource

Following up on the previous Stripe credentials fix:

1. The pre-filled API key creation link and the in-app permissions doc
   omitted Invoice items. Stripe treats `rak_invoice_item_read` as a
   distinct scope from `rak_invoice_read`, so following our docs
   verbatim still produced a 403 on /v1/invoiceitems. Added the scope
   to the prefill list and to the help caption.

2. The per-resource permission failure now includes the underlying
   Stripe error message, not just the resource name. A customer hitting
   a missing scope now sees the literal Stripe response (e.g. "this
   account is not currently set up for Connect"), which makes the gap
   actionable instead of guesswork.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): trim Stripe permission error to resource list

When all failing resources are clean stripe.PermissionError (403), the
resource name alone tells the customer which scope to enable on Stripe.
Including Stripe's full error string (request id, status, headers, body)
just bloats the toast — a customer missing one scope was getting a
multi-line dump for a problem with a one-word answer.

Now: clean 403s render as a plain resource list. Only fall back to the
verbose underlying error when a resource failed with a non-permission
exception (network, rate limit, schema mismatch) where the cause isn't
obvious from the resource name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): split Stripe permission errors from unknown errors

A permission denial (403) and an unknown failure (network, schema drift,
rate limit) are different problems with different fixes, but both were
being raised as StripePermissionError — which forced the user-facing
message to either dump every Stripe error verbatim or hide the cause of
non-permission failures behind a misleading "missing permissions" toast.

Now: validate_credentials tracks the two classes in separate dicts and
raises a distinct exception for each. StripePermissionError carries
clean 403s and renders as a plain resource list. New StripeValidationError
carries unknown errors and surfaces the underlying Stripe message,
folding any collected 403s into the same toast for one-shot reporting.

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): validate nested Stripe resources via parent endpoint

CustomerBalanceTransaction and CustomerPaymentMethod are nested under
/v1/customers/:id, so they cannot be listed without a parent customer
ID and weren't part of validate_credentials's resources_to_check list.
Filtering by table name produced an empty list and fell through to the
"<resource> does not exist" branch — which the source layer renders as
"Stripe credentials lack permissions for CustomerPaymentMethod" every
time the user toggles the sync method on one of these tables.

Map the two nested resources to the Customer endpoint for validation.
That covers the parent scope they all share and avoids the fake
permission-error toast at setup. The nested resources may still need
additional scopes at sync time (rak_payment_method_read for example),
but those will surface with a real 403 from the actual sync run rather
than a misleading message before the run even starts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
refactor: hoist Stripe NESTED_RESOURCE_TO_PARENT to constants

Move the nested→parent map alongside the existing resource-name maps
in constants.py instead of redeclaring it inside validate_credentials.
Single source of truth for the relationship — get_rows already encodes
it live via StripeNestedResource.parent, but validate_credentials
needs it before instantiating the StripeClient, so a module-level
constant is the right shape.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
refactor: derive Stripe nested→parent linkage from shared resource map

Drop the standalone NESTED_RESOURCE_TO_PARENT constant in favour of
deriving the linkage from the StripeNestedResource.parent reference
that already exists in the resources dict — same source of truth used
by get_rows. Both call sites now go through a new _build_resources
factory; validate_credentials walks parent.method via an identity
reverse-index to recover the parent's name.

commits.message:
fix: drop nested-resource fallback that resurrected misleading toast

Previous fallback `flat_method_to_name.get(id(entry.parent.method), name)`
silently used the nested resource name when the reverse-index missed —
which would have reproduced the very "lacks permissions for
CustomerPaymentMethod" toast this whole code path was added to avoid.

Replace with a direct dict access (KeyError on miss) and add a CI test
that asserts every StripeNestedResource's parent.method is registered
as a top-level StripeResource. The misconfiguration is a programming
error and should fail in CI rather than at runtime.

Also format the nested resource error as `Nested (Parent)` (e.g.
"CustomerPaymentMethod (Customer)") so the customer sees both the
table they toggled and the actionable scope they need to grant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message: Merge branch 'master' into claude/stripe-nested-resource-validation
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix: drop method-identity reverse lookup that broke at runtime

Stripe's SDK exposes endpoints via property descriptors that return a
fresh bound method on every attribute access — so
`id(client.customers.list) == id(client.customers.list)` is False at
runtime. The previous reverse index built `{id(r.method): name}` and
then KeyError'd when validating a nested resource because the method
identity at lookup time never matched the one captured at registration
time. Tests passed because MagicMock caches child attribute access and
makes identity equality look True, masking the bug.

Carry the parent linkage explicitly on the StripeNestedResource via a
new `parent_name: str` field. validate_credentials now does a direct
dict lookup on the name. The CI invariant test no longer compares
method identity; it asserts each nested resource's parent_name is a
registered top-level StripeResource — which is the actual property
the runtime depends on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): surface actionable Stripe permission error to user

Stripe's PermissionError carries the exact missing scope ("Having the
'rak_payment_method_read' permission would allow this request to
continue"), which is far more actionable than the generic "check your
configuration and permissions in Stripe" toast we used to show. The raw
message also contains an ~80-char redacted run from the restricted key
that bloats the toast — collapse it before surfacing.

- Add `_clean_stripe_error_message` to collapse 5+ consecutive `*` chars
  (the redacted middle of a restricted key) to `***`. The visible prefix
  and suffix Stripe leaves are preserved for support escalations.
- Add `_call_stripe` wrapper around all SDK list/iteration calls in
  get_rows so any StripeError raised during sync is re-raised with a
  cleaned message under the same exception class — keeps the framework's
  non-retryable substring matching working.
- Apply the cleaner in validate_credentials's per-resource error
  capture as well, so setup-time toasts are also tight.
- Change get_non_retryable_errors's "PermissionError" mapping from a
  static generic message to None, so the now-cleaned underlying Stripe
  message flows through to the user.

Drop a redundant comment on StripeNestedResource.parent_name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
chore: drop runtime parent-type assert in validate_credentials

The CI test test_validate_credentials_nested_resources_have_registered_parents
already enforces that every StripeNestedResource.parent_name resolves to a
registered top-level StripeResource. Running the same check on every
validate_credentials call is wasted work — strengthen the test to cover the
type invariant too and let the validator do a plain dict access with a cast.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): mention Payment methods in Stripe perms caption

The PERMISSIONS list already includes `rak_payment_method_read` (so the

restricted key manually — by following the visible instructions instead

commits.message:
feat(hog-charts): add bar scales and bar-layout module

Pure helpers for the BarChart that's coming next. No consumer in this
PR — the new exports aren't called from anywhere yet.

`scales.ts`:
- `BarScaleSet` — `{ band, value, valueAxes, group }`
- `createBarScales` — builds the scale set for a given orientation
  (`vertical`/`horizontal`) and layout (`stacked`/`grouped`/`percent`).

  value domain through zero so bar baselines align with the plot edge

`bar-layout.ts` (new module, sibling to `scales.ts`):
- `cornersFor(isHorizontal, isPositive, shouldRoundCap)` — picks the
  corner mask for a bar's cap end
- `computeSeriesBars(series, labels, scales, layout, isHorizontal,
  stackedBand, isTopOfStack)` — produces one `BarRect | null` per
  data index (null when the bar isn't drawable). Lives next to scales
  rather than in `charts/BarChart.tsx` so the geometry can be unit
  tested independent of React

`types.ts`:
- `BarChartConfig extends ChartConfig` — `barLayout`, `bandPadding`,
  `groupPadding`, `barCornerRadius`

Tests:
- `bar-scales.test.ts` covers band layout, value-domain construction,
  group-only sub-band, percent domain, horizontal orientation, the
  stacked-series override
- `bar-layout.test.ts` covers grouped + stacked positioning in both

commits.message:
fix(hog-charts): convert computeSeriesBars to options bag

Three /r findings rolled into one commit since they all touch
bar-layout.ts:

1. computeSeriesBars had a 7-positional-arg signature with two
   adjacent booleans (`isHorizontal`, `isTopOfStack`) — call sites
   like `computeSeriesBars(s, labels, scales, 'grouped', false,
   undefined, false)` were error-prone on reorder. Switch to a single
   options-bag parameter.

2. The stacked branch hardcoded the corner mask
   (`shouldRoundCap ? { topRight, bottomRight } : {}`) instead of
   calling cornersFor. computeStackData clamps to Math.max(0, …) so
   the always-positive assumption is correct, but routing both
   branches through cornersFor keeps the corner logic in one place.

title: ci(hogli): publish to pypi via trusted publishing
author: rnegron

reviews.author: webjunkie
reviews.body:
Review — agent-assisted, checked against our existing best practices in posthog-pixelmatch's wheel publishing workflow.

**No tests on the built package before publish**
pixelmatch runs pytest on the built wheel before publishing. This workflow builds, validates metadata with twine, then publishes straight to PyPI without ever testing the artifact. Worth adding a quick smoke test — something like `uv run --with hogli --find-links dist -- hogli --version` or running the actual test suite against the built wheel. A broken build currently goes straight to production.

**`workflow_dispatch` removed instead of guarded**
The first commit had `workflow_dispatch`; bots flagged the version-check bypass; it was removed entirely. The better fix is to keep `workflow_dispatch` and either (a) make the `pypi-hogli` environment require tag refs (not "optionally"), or (b) gate the step to reject non-tag dispatch. Without it, re-triggering a failed publish requires the fragile delete-and-recreate-tag dance documented in the README. pixelmatch keeps `workflow_dispatch` and gates publish behind `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')` on the release job.

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: Gates denied this PR as it touches CI/CD infrastructure (new GitHub Actions publishing workflow). Additionally, there's an unresolved security comment about `actions/checkout@v6` — a tag that doesn't exist for that action — being used in a job with `id-token: write` permissions, which is a concrete security risk in a PyPI publishing workflow.

The only review is on an older commit and predates the current implementation; a team member needs to confirm the final approach.

commits.message:
fix(notebooks): tolerate raw-JSON attrs in custom node parseHTML

Pasting a notebook selection that contains both text and an embedded
custom node (e.g. a SQL query insight) failed: the pasted content
flashed for a frame and then vanished, leaving users to paste the text
and drag the node separately.

The custom-attribute parseHTML in createPostHogWidgetNode hard-coded
JSON.parse(atob(value)), but only the explicit copyToClipboard action
base64-encodes attributes. The default Cmd+C path goes through
renderHTML, which serializes object attributes as raw JSON. atob then
threw on the leading `{`, the node was rejected, and ProseMirror rolled
back the whole paste.

Replace the parser with a tolerant helper that tries base64+JSON first
and falls back to raw JSON / raw string, so both copy paths round-trip.

reviews.body: No showstoppers. This is a focused frontend performance fix (cancel running animations on unmount to prevent detached-tree memory leaks) with correct implementation — `ref.current` is captured at effect setup time, each repeated skeleton item gets its own ref, and the scene-root wrapper key correctly incorporates `activeSceneId`. All bot review comments were addressed in follow-up commits and marked resolved.

commits.message:
fix(perf): cancel running animations on unmount to release detached scene trees

Chromium's DocumentTimeline holds a strong reference to every running animation
and the animation holds its target element via KeyframeEffect. When a component
unmounts while an `animation: ... infinite` declaration is still running, the
detached subtree gets pinned by the timeline -> animation -> element chain.
Across many SPA navigations this accumulates into multi-GB tab memory and OOM
crashes that real users hit.

Added a small `useCancelAnimationsOnUnmount` hook that calls
`element.getAnimations({ subtree: true }).forEach(a => a.cancel())` during
React unmount cleanup, severing the timeline back-reference so the browser can
GC the detached tree normally.

Two layers of defence:
- Leaf hooks on `Spinner`, `LemonTableLoader`, `LemonSkeleton`,
  `WrappingLoadingSkeleton` — catch the loading indicators that appear and
  disappear during a single scene's lifetime (the "loading -> done" churn that
  scene-level cleanup misses). LemonSkeleton's inner div was extracted to
  `LemonSkeletonItem` so each repeated instance gets its own ref + hook.
- `SceneAnimationRoot` wrapper at the top of every scene render in App.tsx,
  keyed on scene id + tab id so it actually unmounts on each scene change. Acts
  as a safety net for any animated component under the scene tree we haven't
  hooked individually.

30 min real-usage simulation (~250 SPA navigations across 10 scenes) measured
via CDP forced GC + Memory.getDOMCounters / Performance.getMetrics:

before:
- heap delta: +231 MB
- DOM nodes delta: +1,078,286
- JS event listeners delta: +62,947

after:
- heap delta: +43 MB
- DOM nodes delta: +13,642 (almost entirely the currently-rendered scene's own
  nodes — no cross-navigation accumulation)
- JS event listeners delta: +14,937 (same — current scene baseline)

Apples-to-apples on the same scene mid-run (t=20min, both on /home, after 17
nav cycles): +83 nodes / +146 listeners — within noise. Original at t=20min
was +732k nodes / +43k listeners and climbing.
commits.author: pauldambra

commits.message:
fix: address bot + qa-swarm review feedback

- Capture `ref.current` inside the effect setup, not in the cleanup, so the
  cancel runs against the actual DOM node even if React nulls the ref before
  the passive cleanup is flushed (flagged convergently by chatgpt-codex and
  greptile bots — strictly safer regardless of the exact commit ordering)
- Add a code comment explaining why `LemonSkeletonItem` is extracted (a
  future inlining would silently disable the leak fix for the repeat case)
- Add a code comment explaining why `className="contents"` on
  `SceneAnimationRoot` is load-bearing (we need a DOM node for the ref +
  layout-neutrality)

reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR reworks the `tools/infra-scripts/clitools/toolbox.py` pod-claiming workflow to support multiple Kubernetes “pools” (including `flags-cache-jumphost`), and updates `bin/rust-jumphost` to delegate to that shared claim-from-pool machinery instead of `kubectl exec`-ing into a long-lived deployment pod. **Changes:** - Add a pool registry (`POOLS`), `--pool`, `--auto-delete`, and `KUBE_CONTEXT`/`KUBE_NAMESPACE` support to the toolbox wrapper, with retries for atomic claims. - Introduce `kubectl_cmd(..., context=...)` and rework context selection to avoid mutating the user’s kubeconfig via `kubectl config use-context`. - Improve operational ergonomics: robust cleanup on broken stdout / terminal close, exec exit-code propagation, and richer Rust warm-cache error formatting. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 6 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | tools/infra-scripts/clitools/toolbox/user.py | Parameterize “claimed label key” and thread kubectl context into `kubectl auth whoami`. | | tools/infra-scripts/clitools/toolbox/pod.py | Generalize pod selection/claiming to pool+namespace+context; add claim-race handling and more robust delete/exec behavior. | | tools/infra-scripts/clitools/toolbox/kubernetes.py | Add `kubectl_cmd` and make `select_context()` return a name without switching kubeconfig; add `validate_context()`. | | tools/infra-scripts/clitools/toolbox.py | Implement pool dispatch, auto-delete + signal/atexit cleanup, claim race retries, and exit-code propagation. | | tools/infra-scripts/clitools/test_toolbox.py | Expand unit tests to cover context threading, pool dispatch, atomic claim races, cleanup ordering, and broken-tty robustness. | | rust/feature-flags/src/bin/warm-flags-cache.rs | Switch per-team error formatting from Display to Debug to preserve SDK error details. | | bin/rust-jumphost | Replace direct `kubectl exec` with a thin shim invoking `toolbox.py --pool flags-cache-jumphost --auto-delete`. |

commits.message:
chore(infra): rewrite rust-jumphost as claim-from-pool shim over toolbox.py

Generalizes toolbox helpers to support multiple pools with pool-specific
claim labels, configurable namespaces, and KUBE_CONTEXT. The rust-jumphost
wrapper now delegates to toolbox.py --pool flags-cache-jumphost --auto-delete.

Safety fixes applied after QA review and live testing:
- Atomic claim: get_toolbox_pod returns resourceVersion; claim_pod attaches
  --resource-version on the first mutation and raises ClaimRaceError on 409,
  with up to 3 retries against fresh pods.
- KUBE_CONTEXT no longer calls kubectl config use-context; --context is
  threaded through every kubectl invocation via kubectl_cmd().
- atexit cleanup and SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers are armed before claim_pod(),
  and only when this invocation is actually claiming (not on pure reattach).
- connect_to_pod returns the kubectl exec exit code; main() propagates via
  sys.exit(rc).
- delete_pod survives a hung-up controlling terminal: progress prints are
  best-effort (BrokenPipeError swallowed) and kubectl's stdout/stderr are
  captured, so the actual delete still runs after a SIGHUP cleanup. Without
  this, the very first print would raise on the dead PTY before kubectl was
  reached, leaking the claimed pod.

62 unit tests covering all of the above; ruff clean.
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
chore(flags): debug-format SDK errors in warm-flags-cache

The ops binary previously stringified its boxed error chain with Display
(``e.to_string()``), which collapses aws-sdk-s3 errors to a generic
"service error" and hides the actual error code (e.g. AccessDenied,
NoSuchBucket, request id). Switch to Debug formatting so the SDK's nested
service error variant is rendered with its code, message, and request id —
making IRSA / IAM / bucket-policy regressions diagnosable from a single
``warn_flags_cache`` log line without needing CloudTrail.
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
chore(infra): harden toolbox auto-delete against deleting unclaimed pods

- delete_pod gains optional expected_label_key/value; when set (atexit path)
  it verifies the pod still carries our claim label before deleting, so a
  claim_pod() failure before any label was written cannot shrink the pool.
- Retry-exhaustion branch now atexit.unregister(delete_pod) before sys.exit,
  so the last lost-race candidate (never claimed) is not deleted on exit.
- KeyboardInterrupt now exits 128+SIGINT (130) instead of 0, matching the
  SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers and POSIX convention.
commits.author: haacked
