commits.message:
feat(flags): implement out-of-band billing counter with dual-write and shadow aggregator

Add an in-process BillingAggregator that collects billing increments in memory
and flushes batched HINCRBYs to a shadow Redis keyspace (posthog:...:shadow)
for offline reconciliation against the authoritative production path.

The authoritative write remains the synchronous increment_request_count to the
production keyspace (posthog:decide_requests:*). The aggregator is optional and
gated by FLAGS_BILLING_AGGREGATOR_ENABLED (default: false) for safe phased rollout.

Extract record_billing_increment() helper to deduplicate dual-write logic across
/flags and /flags/definitions endpoints. Add FLAG_REQUEST_REDIS_ERROR metric
constant and extend test coverage to verify the dual-write contract.

All 1196+ lib tests and 7 billing integration tests pass.
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(flags): address code review feedback on billing aggregator

- Suppress `redis_error` metric under BestEffort flush to avoid
  double-counting with `flush_dropped_on_error` on the shutdown path
- Gate shadow aggregator.record() on sync write success so reconciliation
  remains a strict equality: divergence means an aggregator bug, not
  sync-path Redis noise
- Use bounded `error_type` label on FLAG_REQUEST_REDIS_ERROR via the
  shared classify_redis_error helper (was unbounded e.to_string())
- Parameterize cap and aggregation unit tests with #[rstest]
- Fix misleading "5s" timeout comment in test_shutdown_flush test
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(flags): refactor bucket calculation and fix capture timing for billing counter

Use common current_bucket() helper instead of duplicating SystemTime math.
Move bucket capture before HTTP requests to avoid 2-minute boundary races.
Extract aggregator conditional for consistency with production wiring.
Trim verbose comments to single-line explanations.
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(flags): clarify billing aggregator test harness behavior

Replace misleading comment that claimed tests drive `flush_pending()` (which
doesn't exist) with an accurate explanation: `for_tests()` intentionally skips
the background flusher and doesn't expose a handle, so counts populate the
in-memory pending map but never reach mock Redis. The construction earns its
keep by exercising the synchronous `record()` side of the dual-write, keeping
that codepath honest under mock Redis. End-to-end flush coverage lives in the
real-Redis tests (`test_dual_write_*`, `test_shutdown_flush_*`).
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(flags): make execute_pipeline atomic via MULTI/EXEC

Wraps the redis-rs pipeline in MULTI/EXEC so a connection drop,
server hangup, or read timeout cannot leave a partial commit:
either every command in the chunk takes effect server-side or none
do. Without this, non-idempotent retries (HINCRBY in the billing
aggregator) would double-count commands that committed on the
original attempt before the connection dropped.

All current callers benefit:
- billing aggregator flush: HINCRBYs, retried on Err
- synchronous billing path (flag_analytics): HINCRBYs
- hypercache set_with_etag: SETEX×2; doc-comment already claims
  atomic write of data + ETag, this matches the contract
commits.author: haacked

commits.message:
fix(flags): close shutdown-drop double-count race in flush_once

Swap `in_flight_uncredited` to 0 *before* crediting
`flush_dropped_on_error`, so a concurrent `record_shutdown_drops`
cannot read both: a non-zero residual *and* the about-to-happen
FlushDroppedOnError credit. Previously a shutdown deadline firing
between the credit and the zero would re-credit the residual as
`shutdown_drop`, double-counting it in
`flags_billing_unflushed_requests_total`.

After the swap, exactly one path sees the residual:
  - this thread credits FlushDroppedOnError(residual), or
  - record_shutdown_drops reads in_flight=0 and credits only
    remaining_pending under ShutdownDrop.

The window was nanosecond-scale and only relevant on a stuck-
shutdown-timeout path, but the fix is small and removes the
footgun for future ordering changes.

Also drops the now-redundant local `dropped_counts` accumulator and
its parameter from `flush_chunk`. The post-loop value of
`in_flight_uncredited` equals it by construction (in BestEffort it
is `total - flushed` = dropped, in BailOnError everything is
either flushed or requeued so the residual is 0).
commits.author: haacked

calls `posthoganalytics.feature_enabled(...)`, which performs a network
round-trip per call. For sources that return many schemas (large Slack
workspaces hit ~3000 channels) the per-iteration call inflated response
construction past the 120s gateway timeout, surfacing as a 504 on the
data-warehouse new-source wizard.

The team doesn't change mid-loop, so the result is constant for the
request — call it once and reuse the boolean. Locally `DEBUG=True`
short-circuits the helper, which is why this never reproduced in dev
loops and only bit larger production workspaces.

title: feat(query-tagging): add fallback maps for scene/kind/source -> product
author: robbie-c

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: T1d-complex PR with zero reviews that reclassifies core scenes (Dashboard, Insight, Notebook, DebugQuery) from explicit product mappings to "container" scenes deferring to kind fallback — a behavioral change to shared query attribution infrastructure that needs at least one human reviewer to confirm the intent.

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: The web analytics snapshot file shows two test snapshots apparently swapped (test_bounce_rate_one_user.1 and test_entry_bounce_rate.1 trade SQL bodies), which could mask real query regressions in a product area the author doesn't own. Get a sign-off from @PostHog/team-web-analytics before merging.

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: This PR makes behavioral changes to shared query attribution infrastructure — reclassifying container scenes (Dashboard, Insight, Notebook, DebugQuery) from explicit product mappings to kind-based fallback, moving MCP tagging from middleware to sync_execute, and adding a new exhaustive kind→product dispatch that will raise at runtime if any NodeKind is unhandled. All three top-level reviews are from bots; there are no human reviews. The author has no ownership match, which combined with behavioral changes to shared, cross-product infrastructure requires a human sign-off before merging.

reviews.author: arthurdedeus
reviews.body: Nice! Looks way better centralized like this

commits.message:
feat(query-tagging): scene/kind/source fallback for ClickHouse query tags

Add `add_fallback_query_tags(tags)` in `posthog/clickhouse/query_tagging.py`,
called once at the end of `sync_execute` after every other tagging hook.
Order: `tags.scene` → `tags.query_type` → `source == "mcp"`. Never
overrides values that are already set, so a runner-level explicit tag
always wins.

* `SCENE_TO_TAGS` (str → FallbackTags | None) maps frontend scenes to
  product+feature. `None` rows are container scenes (Dashboard,
  Notebook, Insight, Max, etc.) — they host arbitrary query kinds, so
  the kind fallback decides product. Scene keys come from frontend
  `activeSceneId` (manifest-registered, e.g. `EndpointScene`). The map
  is intentionally non-exhaustive because pulling Scene into the
  generated schema would churn it every time a scene is added.

* `kind_fallback_tags(kind: NodeKind)` covers every NodeKind via a
  match statement with `assert_never(kind)`, so pyright/mypy fails the
  build when a new kind is added without a paired case arm.

* MCP source fallback: when nothing earlier sets a product and the
  request came in via `X-Posthog-Client: mcp` (or matches the existing
  user-agent path), tag `product=Product.MCP`.

* No `feature` default — `Feature.QUERY` is "customer-facing queries
  only", which is wrong for plenty of inferred kinds (Max AI vector
  search, taxonomy lookups). Untagged kind/source paths surface as
  `UntaggedQueryError` in DEBUG, which is the signal to add explicit
  tagging at the call site.

Removes `_infer_query_tags` and `_SCENE_TO_TAGS` from `posthog/api/query.py`
in favor of the layered fallback. Reverts the `mcp_defaults` block from
`UntaggedQueryError` and locking out kind-based attribution for MCP
traffic. Adds `Product.MCP`, `Product.MARKETING_ANALYTICS`,
`Product.COHORTS`, and `Product.REVENUE_ANALYTICS`. `get_event_source`
now also recognises `X-PostHog-Client: mcp`.

`UntaggedQueryError` keeps a comment warning future readers away from
adding catch-all tags to silence the error.

title: perf(insights): drop redundant `dashboards` M2M serialisation on basic list
author: pauldambra

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: The PR introduces an N+1 regression on the full (non-basic) InsightSerializer list path. `TeamScopedDashboardsField` (which reads from pre-fetched tiles) was added for this purpose but never wired into `InsightSerializer.dashboards` — it still declares `TeamScopedPrimaryKeyRelatedField`. With both the `dashboards` prefetch and the tile-fallback `else` branch removed, DRF now calls `instance.dashboards.all()` per insight without a cache on non-basic list requests.

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: The bot's concern about `InsightSerializer.dashboards` not being wired to `TeamScopedDashboardsField` was valid on the older commit it reviewed, but the current diff includes that exact change. Both the basic and full serializer paths now derive the `dashboards` list from the prefetched `dashboard_tiles`, the redundant `dashboards` M2M prefetch is removed, and new parameterized tests confirm no per-insight M2M queries on either path.

commits.message:
perf(insights): drop redundant `dashboards` M2M serialisation on basic list

the basic insights list already prefetches `dashboard_tiles`, and the
client-visible `dashboards` payload is just the list of `dashboard_id`s
on those tiles — yet `InsightBasicSerializer` was also declaring
`dashboards` in `Meta.fields` without an explicit serialiser, so DRF
fell back to `PrimaryKeyRelatedField(many=True)` which traverses
`instance.dashboards.all()`. that traversal goes through the
`DashboardTileManager`'s `exclude(deleted=True)` filter, so its sql
shape doesn't always match the `Prefetch("dashboards", queryset=...)`
cache and can fall back to per-instance lookups under the right prod
state (the `WHERE dashboardtile.insight_id = %s` form seen in jaeger).

replace the implicit field with an explicit `SerializerMethodField` that
reads from the prefetched `dashboard_tiles`, drop the now-unused
`Prefetch("dashboards", ...)` from the basic queryset path, and remove
the redundant `representation["dashboards"]` overwrite in
`to_representation` (the method now populates it directly).

add a regression test that asserts no per-instance M2M dashboards
lookup fires across multiple insights with several dashboards each.
the existing `test_listing_insights_does_not_nplus1` query count drops
from 14 to 13, snapshot updated to match.

perf(insights): drop redundant `dashboards` M2M serialisation on full list too

the full `InsightSerializer` had the same redundancy as the basic
serializer: `dashboards` was a `TeamScopedPrimaryKeyRelatedField` that
triggered a per-instance M2M traversal during serialisation, then the
result was overwritten in `to_representation` by the dashboard_tile

genuine N+1 (487 lookups in one production trace, ~544ms total).

* preload `dashboard_tiles` into `UserPermissions` before serialising
  the page, so `effective_restriction_level` /
  `effective_privilege_level` stop firing two queries per insight.

the N+1 regression test is now parametrised over basic and full paths.
it reproduces the bug on master (assertion fails) and passes after
this commit.

fix(retention): keep first-ever cohort intact when applying a breakdown

With retention type "first ever" + a breakdown, adding breakdown_value to
GROUP BY split each user into one partition per breakdown value they ever had.
The per-partition first-ever check then silently became "first ever with this
value", letting one user populate multiple buckets and inflating bucket sums
above the unbroken total.

Switch to argMinIf to read the breakdown property off the user's earliest
start-event row, leaving GROUP BY untouched. Recurring and first-matching
modes are unchanged.

commits.message:
feat(dashboards): server-side fuzzy full-text search via API

Adds a `?search=` query param to the dashboards list endpoint that combines
Postgres weighted full-text search (`name` weight A, `description` weight C,
prefix-as-you-type via `to_tsquery`) with trigram similarity on `name`. Results
are ordered by combined score so the exact name match wins, with typos and
transpositions still matching via `pg_trgm`.

The frontend dashboards scene now delegates search to the API instead of
filtering the in-memory list with Fuse.js, and suppresses the persisted
alphabetical column sort while a search term is active so the server's
relevance order is preserved.

The MCP `dashboards-get-all` tool already advertised search support but the
endpoint never implemented it; this closes that gap so MCP clients can find a
specific dashboard by name without paging through every result.

commits.message:
feat(dashboards): drop FTS, use trigram word similarity on name and description

The original implementation combined Postgres weighted full-text search with
trigram similarity, but `to_tsvector(name||description)` had no functional GIN
index backing it (every search seq-scanned + recomputed the vector per row),
and the `TrigramSimilarity > 0.2` predicate didn't translate to the `%`
operator that `gin_trgm_ops` accelerates — so the new `idx_dashboard_name_trgm`
index wasn't actually used.

Replace both with `TrigramWordSimilarity` (uses the index via `<%`) on `name`
and `description`, with regular `TrigramSimilarity` on `name` as a tiebreak so
an exact name match outranks rows that merely contain the search word. Drop
the magic 0.05/0.2 thresholds in favour of a single named
`MIN_TRIGRAM_SIMILARITY` module-level constant. Wrap the search in an
OpenTelemetry span so we can track perf in production.

Parameterise the relevance/typo/prefix tests, add explicit case-insensitivity
coverage that the previous `it.each(['Nova', 'nova', 'NOVA'])` provided
before being dropped, and replace the tautological `isinstance(..., list)`
assertion on the unsafe-chars path with a real contract that pathological
inputs return an empty result set rather than raising.

commits.message:
fix(dashboards): coalesce nullable trigram scores so unnamed dashboards rank correctly

`Dashboard.name` is nullable. Without coalescing the trigram annotations to 0.0
a row whose `name` is NULL but whose `description` matched would end up with
a NULL `_search_score`, and Postgres orders `NULLS FIRST` in `DESC` — so
unnamed rows would wrongly outrank named ones in the results.

Wrap each `Trigram*Similarity` annotation in `Coalesce(..., Value(0.0))` and
add a regression test pinning the contract that named matches outrank unnamed
description-only matches. Found by ChatGPT Codex review.

commits.message:
fix(dashboards): address qa-swarm v2 LOW findings on _apply_search

Four mechanical fixes from the second qa-swarm pass:

- Strip NUL bytes from `?search=` before any DB call. Postgres rejects NUL in
  text params with a 500; the URL layer often filters them before our code runs
  but defense-in-depth is cheap (one `replace('\x00', '')`).
- Split the threshold into `MIN_NAME_TRIGRAM_SIMILARITY = 0.3` and
  `MIN_DESCRIPTION_TRIGRAM_SIMILARITY = 0.4`. Descriptions are freeform prose
  where short queries (3-5 chars) trivially clear a 0.3 threshold against any
  long passage — a separate higher threshold tightens recall.
- Extract `_name_match_score` (word + full similarity on name) and
  `_description_match_score` so the relevance formula reads as
  `name_match + 0.5 * description_match` rather than three magic terms.
- Add `dashboard.search.result_count` and `dashboard.search.empty` attributes
  on the request span (via a `list()` override) so we can tune the thresholds
  from prod telemetry — catches both "too tight, returns nothing" and "too
  loose, returns hundreds" by the same signal.

commits.message:
perf(dashboards): drop unused trigram GIN index migration

Local `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` against a populated team confirms the
qa-team finding: Postgres' planner picks a Seq Scan over the team-narrowed
rows in every realistic configuration of this query, so the GIN trigram
index on `name` is never used.

Verified at:
- 1000 dashboards, 53% match selectivity — Seq Scan, ~32 ms
- 10000 dashboards, ~1% selectivity (threshold 0.7) — Seq Scan, ~18 ms
- Both the production `annotate + __gt` shape and the indexable
  `__trigram_word_similar` lookup shape — same plan in each case

The team_id filter narrows fast enough that the index lookup overhead loses
to a sequential scan in every realistic case. Adding the index would only
pay write amplification on every dashboard insert/update without ever
firing on read.

Dropping migration 0002, removing the GinIndex from `Dashboard.Meta.indexes`,
and resetting `max_migration.txt` to the existing 0001. The trigram
functions themselves (`word_similarity`, `similarity`) still work without an
index — they just run as expression evaluations against the seq-scanned
rows, which is what's already happening.

title: fix(signals): Reduce inbox report failures via retries and relay fix
author: Twixes

commits.message:
fix(signals): reduce inbox report failures via retries and relay fix

~70% of signal report research runs have been failing because Modal
sandbox agents crash before producing output. Three things compound:

1. The SSE relay in relay_sandbox_events.py didn't catch
   httpx.HTTPStatusError (404s from dead sandboxes), so it crashed
   immediately instead of marking the stream as errored. This left the
   workflow with no heartbeats and a silent 5-minute countdown to
   inactivity timeout.

2. Both select_repository_activity and run_agentic_report_activity used
   maximum_attempts=1, meaning any transient sandbox crash permanently
   killed the report with no retry.

3. When _drain_final_log raised its RuntimeError, the message said only
   "no agent message" with no hint of the actual cause (e.g. inactivity
   timeout, follow-up delivery failure), making debugging harder.
commits.author: Twixes

title: feat(experiments): gate precomputation by 12h minimum runtime
author: andehen

reviews.author: jurajmajerik
reviews.body: Makes sense, thanks 🙏

commits.message:
feat(experiments): gate precomputation by 12h minimum runtime

Skip lazy-computed exposures and metric events for experiments that
have been running for less than 12 hours. The today-window TTL caches
results for 15 min, which can mask freshly arrived exposures while
most data is still in today's window — the gate scopes that trade-off
to experiments where most data is already in past (frozen) windows.
Explicit PrecomputationMode.PRECOMPUTED / DIRECT query overrides still
win over the gate.
commits.author: andehen

commits.message:
chore(experiments): backdate test fixtures instead of patching gate

Replace the monkey-patch of MIN_PRECOMPUTATION_DURATION_SECONDS in
_save_experiment_with_precomputation with a backdate of the test
experiment's start_date. Backdating to exactly the threshold keeps
the daily window in the same UTC day as the original start_date, so
the SQL filter shifts only by hours within the day, not across days.

Snapshots regenerated for the parameterized "precomputed" tests
(time component shifts from frozen-now to frozen-now − 12h). Existing
master snapshot drift in the same files (email property reading from
person.pmat_email materialized column) is bundled into the regen
since both code paths produce the same SQL.
commits.author: andehen

commits.message:
chore(experiments): pass explicit start_date in precomputed tests

Replace the post-creation start_date mutation in
_save_experiment_with_precomputation with an explicit start_date
argument on each parameterized "precomputed" test. The helper now
just enables the team config and saves; if a test omits start_date
the gate fails and the path falls back to direct.

Each test passes start_date=datetime(<freeze year, month, day>, 0, 0, 0),
which is exactly 12h before the test's frozen now (12:00 UTC) and
matches the existing daily-window UTC date — so SQL filters change
only in the time component (12:00 → 00:00) and no extra job_ids are
introduced.
commits.author: andehen

commits.message:
chore(experiments): address review on precomputation duration gate

Three changes from XP review:

- Move test backdating back into _save_experiment_with_precomputation
  instead of asking every parameterized test to remember a magic
  start_date. Forgetting the start_date silently skipped the
  precomputed branch and the snapshot agreed with the wrong path
  (the worst kind of green test). The helper now owns both halves
  of the precomputation seam: flipping the team flag and ensuring
  the experiment passes the duration gate.

- Note the gate-bypass asymmetry between the two runners.
  ExperimentQueryRunner lets PrecomputationMode.PRECOMPUTED bypass
  the gate; ExperimentExposuresQueryRunner has no equivalent
  override yet (per the existing TODO). Comment makes the gap
  explicit so callers don't expect symmetric behavior.

- Rename experiment_meets_precomputation_duration_gate to
  experiment_has_min_runtime_for_precomputation. Reads more
  naturally — describes the property being asserted instead of
  the mechanism enforcing it.
commits.author: andehen

commits.message:
chore(experiments): document why the precomputation gate is 12h

The existing comment said *why a gate exists*; this adds *why this
threshold*. 12h covers the workday users typically launch and watch a
fresh experiment in (when the 15-min cache lag would be most noticeable
and refreshes are most frequent). Past that, refresh frequency drops and
the cost of scanning live events outweighs the freshness gap, while
keeping the gate short enough that day-two queries still hit the fast
precomputed path.
commits.author: andehen

title: fix(llma): return all spans for a trace, regardless of duration
author: richardsolomou

commits.message:
fix(llma): return all spans for a trace, regardless of duration

The trace detail page (/llm-analytics/traces/<id>) used a tight ~30 minute
time window around the URL `timestamp` parameter, while the same trace
expanded from the sessions view used a 7 day default. Long-running agent
traces or late-arriving spans showed up in one view and not the other,
which read to customers as cache staleness even though the data was
fresh.

Replace the single-stage windowed query with a two-stage lookup: stage
one finds the trace's exact min/max timestamps, stage two fetches all
events using those bounds. This mirrors the pattern already used by
TracesQueryRunner and removes the guesswork around how wide to make the
forward window.

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Additive observability-only change to Server-Timing headers. The greptile concern about using `dur=` for count metrics is correctly addressed with `desc=`. The CH count fields will always be 0 (execute.py not updated), but this is a diagnostic-only feature with no production risk — no crashes, data loss, or API contract changes.

commits.message:
feat(observability): add per-request pg/ch query count and max to Server-Timing

the Server-Timing header already exposes `pg=<ms>` for total cursor.execute()
wall-clock time on a request, but a single number can't tell you whether 4s
of postgres time is one slow query, an N+1 chain, or pgbouncer pool wait.

add four extra entries each for postgres and clickhouse:

- `pg_count` / `ch_count` — number of query executions on the request.
- `pg_max` / `ch_max` — wall-clock of the slowest single execution (ms).
- `pg_slow` / `ch_slow` — number of executions over 50ms.

opening DevTools network panel on a slow request now distinguishes
`pg=4000 pg_count=47 pg_max=180 pg_slow=2` (N+1) from
`pg=4000 pg_count=8 pg_max=3500 pg_slow=1` (one fat query) from
`pg=4000 pg_count=12 pg_max=80 pg_slow=0` (pool/network wait).

QueryCounter is also used by the clickhouse counter, so the same fields
are emitted for clickhouse for free.

fix(observability): emit count/slow as desc, not dur

Server-Timing `dur` is reserved for milliseconds. emitting
`pg_count;dur=47` made DevTools render the query count as '47 ms',
which defeats the diagnostic value. switch counts and slow-counts to
`desc="<n>"` so they show as a description string, not a duration.

author: webjunkie

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR switches `pnpm start-vite` from running Tailwind as a separate CLI watcher (which rewrites an imported CSS file and causes double Vite reloads) to running Tailwind inside Vite via `@tailwindcss/vite`, while keeping the existing production esbuild + standalone Tailwind CLI path intact. **Changes:** - Add `@tailwindcss/vite` to the frontend and enable it in `frontend/vite.config.ts`. - Add a Vite `resolveId` hook to redirect imports of the precompiled Tailwind CSS to the source Tailwind CSS during Vite runs. - Remove `watch:tailwind` from the `start-vite` concurrently chain and add a TS `.d.ts` shim for the plugin. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Adds/updates dependency graph to include `@tailwindcss/vite@4.2.4` and related Tailwind packages. | | `frontend/vite.config.ts` | Wires in `@tailwindcss/vite` and adds a pre-resolve redirect from dist Tailwind CSS to source Tailwind CSS. | | `frontend/src/@types/tailwindcss-vite.d.ts` | Adds a module declaration shim so TS can resolve `@tailwindcss/vite` with `moduleResolution: "node"`. | | `frontend/package.json` | Updates `start-vite` to drop the Tailwind watcher and adds `@tailwindcss/vite` dependency. |
Files not reviewed (1) * **pnpm-lock.yaml**: Language not supported
--- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

reviews.author: pauldambra
reviews.body: robot comments but...

commits.message:
chore(devex): use @tailwindcss/vite plugin in start-vite

Tailwind was running as a standalone CLI watcher alongside Vite,
rewriting `common/tailwind/dist/tailwind.css` on every source save.
That file is `@import`ed by `global.scss`, so each save fired Vite's
HMR twice — once for the source change, once for the regenerated CSS
— which felt like constant reloads.

Swap to the official `@tailwindcss/vite` plugin so Tailwind runs inside
Vite's pipeline. A small resolveId hook redirects the precompiled CSS
import to the source `tailwind.css`, leaving `global.scss` untouched
so the production esbuild path keeps using the standalone CLI.

Drops the `watch:tailwind` worker from the `start-vite` concurrently
chain.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
chore(devex): scope tailwind vite plugin to dev, narrow version gap

Address review on #57075:
- Wrap `tailwindDevSourcePlugin` and `tailwindcss()` in `isDev` so a
  future `vite build` doesn't silently swap precompiled CSS for source
  or double-compile Tailwind.
- Pin `@tailwindcss/vite` 4.2.4 -> 4.1.11 to shrink the dev/prod
  Tailwind version gap (production CLI stays on 4.0.12). Going all the
  way to 4.0.12 isn't viable: the 4.0.x plugin only peer-supports
  vite ^5/^6, and we're on vite 7.

commits.message:
refactor(replay): tag sweep schedules with config fingerprint + reconcile drift

The reconciler previously only upserted schedules for newly-enabled teams; an
edit to an existing team's SignalSourceConfig (sample_rate, recording_filters,
future per-team overrides) wouldn't propagate to its schedule until the team
was disabled and re-enabled. Same for any payload-format change to
SummarizeTeamSessionsInputs — existing schedules carried the old serialized
payload forever.

Add a per-schedule fingerprint:

- compute_schedule_fingerprint(config) returns sha256(canonical_json(config))[:16].
- a_upsert_team_schedule reads the team's config and stamps the fingerprint on the
  schedule via a new PostHogScheduleFingerprint search attribute (registered as
  a Keyword SA in the common attributes registry).
- list_enabled_teams_activity returns {team_id: current_fingerprint} sourced from
  the DB.
- list_summarization_schedule_team_ids_activity returns {team_id: stored_fingerprint}
  read from list_schedules' typed_search_attributes (no extra describe call).
- The reconciler treats teams whose stored fingerprint differs from the freshly
  computed one — including untagged legacy schedules whose value is None — as
  drift, and adds them to the upsert set alongside newly-enabled teams.

Steady state: the SA travels with list_schedules, so drift detection is free.
Any UI edit to a team's config triggers a rewrite within RECONCILER_INTERVAL.
First post-deploy tick: every legacy schedule (no fingerprint tag) gets
rewritten exactly once.

Operator step before deploy: register the PostHogScheduleFingerprint keyword
search attribute in each Temporal Cloud namespace via the existing
register_temporal_search_attributes management command.
commits.author: TueHaulund

chore(replay): tone down verbose comments and test docstrings

Trim multi-line comments and per-test docstrings across the summarization-sweep,
session-summary, and rasterize-recording modules. Removes restated context that
was redundant with the surrounding code.

fix(replay): scope existing-asset reuse to summary-owned exports

Restrict the prep_session_video_asset_activity lookup to assets created by the
summary flow itself (`is_system=True`). Without this, a user-triggered video/mp4
export of the same recording could match and have its export_context overwritten
in place by `_refresh_asset_input_params_locked`, replacing the rendered output
with the AI 8x/3fps render.

Adds a unit test that captures the filter kwargs and asserts `is_system=True`.

title: fix(error-tracking): respect OR/AND operator in issues list filters
author: cat-ph

commits.message:
fix(error-tracking): respect OR/AND operator in issues list filters

The issues list always AND'd user-supplied filters even when an assignment-
rule preview link (or any URL) carried `filterGroup.values[0].type = OR`.
`mergedFilterGroup` rebuilt the group with a hardcoded `And`, and the v3
query runner extracted only `.values` (dropping the operator) before passing
through `HogQLFilters.properties`, which always AND's via `property_to_expr`.

Frontend now preserves the inner operator. When quick filters are selected
alongside an OR omnisearch group, the omnisearch group is nested as a
PropertyGroupFilterValue so its OR is preserved while AND'ing with the quick
filters. The v3 builder reads `filterGroup.values[0].type` and constructs a
single AST node combining issue-level and HogQL property filters with the
chosen operator. User properties no longer flow through the `{filters}`
placeholder; it stays for `filterTestAccounts` only.

title: fix(replay): seekbar preview mousemove listener never removed
author: pauldambra

reviews.author: pauldambra
reviews.body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 Automated comment by **QA Swarm** — not written by a human

Multi-perspective review (qa-team specialists + paul-reviewer + xp-reviewer). See the inline comment for the convergent finding; out-of-hunk findings are below.

## Verdict: 💬 APPROVE WITH NITS

Surgical fix is correct and minimal. One convergent MEDIUM follow-up suggestion about effect-dep churn that's now visible (but not introduced) by this change. Out-of-hunk LOW/NIT items below for context.

### Out-of-hunk findings (cannot be inline-commented, in surrounding code)

**[convergent: paul + xp]** ⚪ NIT — `frontend/src/scenes/session-recordings/player/controller/PlayerSeekbarPreview.tsx:110`

Minor consistency: the listener now lives on `seekBar` (parent) via the snapshot pattern, but `handleMouseMove` still reads geometry from `ref` (the inner wrapper). Two different refs in the same closure with `seekBar`/`ref` names. A rename like `previewRef`/`seekBarRef` would make it obvious which is which.

**[xp]** 🟢 LOW — `PlayerSeekbarPreview.tsx:118`

`if (newPercentage !== percentage) setPercentage(newPercentage)` re-implements React's own setState bail-out — `setPercentage` with an equal primitive doesn't re-render. Dropping the guard removes the only reason `percentage` needs to be in the dep array, which folds into the convergent finding at line 126.

**[xp]** 🟢 LOW — `PlayerSeekbarPreview.tsx` general

No test pinning the listener add/remove symmetry — the bug being fixed (listener added to A, removed from B) is exactly the kind of thing that drifts back without a test. A lightweight RTL test that mounts, fires `mousemove` on the seek bar, unmounts, and asserts no further state updates would lock the contract down.

**[paul]** 🟢 LOW — `PlayerSeekbarPreview.tsx:124`

The deleted comment (`fixes react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warning about stale ref elements`) was pointing at a real lint thing — confirm the warning doesn't come back now that we've gone to the snapshot pattern? lazily asking, the snapshot pattern is the textbook fix so probably fine.

**[paul]** 🟢 LOW — `PlayerSeekbarPreview.tsx` general

When this leaks again in six months we'll be doing the heap-walk dance from scratch. Worth a `data-attr` on the seekbar preview wrapper so we can find it in memlab/leak hunting without grepping? not blocking, just thinking about future-us.

### Convergence

- **`percentage` in dep array causes detach+reattach churn** — flagged by all 3 reviewers (qa-team NIT, paul MEDIUM, xp MEDIUM). Strongest signal; non-blocking follow-up.
- **`ref` vs `seekBar` naming inconsistency** — flagged by paul + xp (both NIT).

### Reviewer summaries

| Reviewer | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| 🔍 qa-team | Fix is correct and minimal. Listener churn from `percentage` deps is now bounded; converting to a ref is a worthwhile but non-blocking follow-up. Ship it. |
| 👤 paul | nice surgical fix — snapshot pattern is the right shape and the heap-walk receipt is convincing. ship it. follow up on the percentage-as-ref shape and a data-attr for future leak hunts. |
| 📐 xp | Diff is a correct, minimal fix for a real bug. The deleted comment was a tell that lint was being silenced rather than understood; the bigger smell (`percentage` in deps) is worth a follow-up plus a test that locks add/remove symmetry. |

---
*Automated by QA Swarm — not a human review*

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Trivial bug fix that removes a stale event listener leak by dropping `percentage` from the effect dep array and properly capturing the ref in a local variable for cleanup. The QA comment was addressed and resolved.

commits.message:
fix(replay): remove seekbar preview mousemove listener from the right node

PlayerSeekbarPreview added the mousemove handler to seekBarRef.current
but its cleanup ran current?.removeEventListener(...) against ref.current
(the inner wrapper), so the listener was never removed. Each recording
switch — and each percentage update via [seekBarRef, percentage] deps —
appended a new listener to the outer seekbar; the captured closure
pinned the previous wrapper div in detached state.

Empirical effect on /replay/home (15 recording switches + forced GC):
- before: 43 detached, PlayerSeekbarPreview2:16, PlayerFrame:8, BindLogic:4
- after: 11 detached, no React components in the detached fingerprint

Snapshot the listen target and remove from the same node.
commits.author: pauldambra

commits.message:
fix(replay): attach seekbar preview mousemove listener once per mount

`percentage` was in the effect's dep array AND set by the listener on
every mousemove, so the effect detached + reattached on every cursor
move. With the listener now actually being removed (previous commit),
that's bounded churn but still wasted work on a hot path.

Drop the manual equality guard — `setPercentage(equal-primitive)` is a
no-op in React already — and drop `percentage` from the deps. Listener
attached once when seekBarRef binds, removed once on unmount.
commits.author: pauldambra

stable. This mirrors the existing resolveValue ref pattern in the same

author: orian

reviews.body: lgtm!

commits.message:
chore(clickhouse): tighten migration ON CLUSTER guard

The existing guard silently skipped operations without _sql metadata
and never re-evaluated cloud-gated  lists, so migrations
emitting ON CLUSTER under a non-default CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT could ship
unchecked.

- Reload each migration module under CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT in {<unset>, US,
  EU, DEV} and re-run the ON CLUSTER + missing-_sql checks
- Hard-fail on operations missing _sql instead of skipping them
- Add an AST-based static backstop that flags ON CLUSTER in any
  migration source string literal
- Add  management command and a CI step that
  renders changed migrations' SQL per cloud environment so reviewers

title: refactor(duckling): share backfill duckgres conn per asset and tighten exception handling
author: fuziontech

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body: ## Pull request overview This PR refactors the Duckling backfill DAG’s duckgres usage to reuse a single pgwire connection per asset run (reducing TLS/connection churn) and tightens exception handling so transient connection failures aren’t silently swallowed as “missing table” cases. It also promotes the duckgres conninfo helper to a public function to avoid cross-module imports of a private API. **Changes:** - Reuse one duckgres connection per asset run and thread `conn` through helper functions instead of opening/closing per helper call. - Narrow missing-table exception handling to specific SQLSTATE errors so operational failures propagate correctly. - Promote `_make_duckgres_conninfo` → `make_duckgres_conninfo` and update call sites; add tests covering missing-table vs operational-error behavior. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 8 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `posthog/ducklake/client.py` | Renames and reuses the duckgres conninfo helper for query/table execution. | | `posthog/dags/events_backfill_to_duckling.py` | Refactors connection ownership to the asset body, updates delete/register helpers, and tightens exception handling. | | `posthog/dags/test_events_backfill_to_duckling.py` | Adds unit tests asserting the missing-table vs operational-error contract for delete helpers. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

commits.message: chore(duckling): log duckgres host instead of catalog db_host in backfill logs
commits.author: fuziontech

commits.message:
refactor(duckling): share duckgres connection per asset run and fix exception handling

Pull the duckgres connection out of every helper and let each asset open
one connection that's threaded through ensure_*, validate_*, delete_*,
and register_* for the duration of the run. Cuts per-partition TLS
handshakes and lets the asset own connection lifecycle.

Fixes a latent bug where psycopg.DatabaseError in the except tuples for
table_exists and delete_*_partition_data swallowed psycopg.OperationalError
(its subclass), so transient pgwire failures looked like "table doesn't
exist" and bypassed the retry decorator. Narrowed those catches to
UndefinedTable + InvalidSchemaName only.

Also: align delete_events_partition_data and delete_persons_partition_data
signatures (both now require conn), drop the @_retry_duckgres_connection
decorator from helpers that no longer own their connection, rename
_make_duckgres_conninfo → make_duckgres_conninfo, replace the conninfo
string-append with psycopg.connect kwargs, inline the rarely-used
delete_*_table helpers into the asset bodies, and add unit-test coverage
for the missing-table-vs-operational-error contract on both event and
person delete paths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: fuziontech

commits.message:
fix(duckling): address review feedback

- DROP TABLE → DROP TABLE IF EXISTS in both backfill assets so a first-run
  with delete_tables=True doesn't abort on a missing table
- Restore structured logger.exception in register_*_file_with_duckling so
  team_id/s3_path metadata still hits structlog on registration failures
- Drop @_retry_duckgres_connection from helpers that take a caller-owned
  conn (ensure_*, validate_*, register_*) — retrying with the same dead
  connection was a no-op; remove the now-unused decorator definition
- Open the duckgres connection only when not (dry_run or
  skip_ducklake_registration) so dry runs don't depend on duckgres
  availability or burn a TLS handshake; gate every conn-using callsite on
  conn is not None
- Parameterize the four delete error-handling tests across (events,
  persons_daily, persons_full) × (missing-table, operational-error) and
  fix the stale "_retry_duckgres_connection" reference in the docstring

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: fuziontech

commits.message:
chore(duckling): restore structured logging on inlined DROP TABLE

Wrap the inlined DROP TABLE IF EXISTS in both backfill assets with a
narrow try/except so unexpected failures (e.g., duckgres mid-DROP crash)
still emit context.log.exception + structlog with team_id/bucket before
re-raising. Mirrors the pattern in register_*_file_with_duckling.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS is fail-safe for the missing-table case; this only
restores observability for the remaining unexpected failure modes that

title: chore(quill): scope postcss config to quill workspace
author: webjunkie

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body: ## Pull request overview Scopes PostCSS configuration to the Quill workspace to prevent Vite from resolving the repo-root `postcss.config.js` (and its root-only plugin deps) during filtered installs/builds (e.g., Cloudflare Pages). **Changes:** - Add a workspace-local `packages/quill/postcss.config.cjs` exporting an empty PostCSS plugin list to stop upward config discovery. --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

commits.message:
chore(quill): scope postcss config to quill workspace

Vite/postcss walks up the directory tree looking for a postcss config. Without one inside packages/quill it would land on the repo-root config, which targets webpack/Storybook v7 and pulls in autoprefixer/cssnano. That's a problem for CF Pages where we install only the quill workspace subset — those root-only deps aren't present and the build crashes with "Cannot find module 'autoprefixer'".

Quill uses Tailwind v4 via @tailwindcss/vite and doesn't need any postcss plugins, so an empty config is enough to halt the upward search.

title: fix(sql-editor): null codeEditorLogic on Monaco models before dispose
author: pauldambra

reviews.author: pauldambra
reviews.body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 Automated comment by **QA Swarm** — not written by a human

QA Swarm review complete — see inline comments. tl;dr: ✅ approve with nits. One convergent suggestion across reviewers (extract a `clearLogicReference` helper next to `initModel`).

reviews.author: stamphog
reviews.body: The fix itself looks correct and well-tested, but the author is not on @PostHog/team-data-stack (which owns both modified production files) and there are no real human reviews — all four reviews are bot-generated comments posted by the author's own account. A behavioral change to core data-warehouse editor logic without an owning-team sign-off needs a human review.

commits.message:
fix(sql-editor): null codeEditorLogic on Monaco models before dispose

Disposed Monaco models stay alive in the JS heap until GC reclaims them.
As long as `(model as any).codeEditorLogic` is set, the captured
codeEditorLogic BuiltLogic — and through its `props.onError` closure,
the entire `sqlEditorLogic` connection graph — stays reachable per
cycle.

`CodeEditor.tsx#disposeTrackedModels` (PR #56743) only clears the
back-reference on models that aren't already disposed. But
`sqlEditorLogic.beforeUnmount` disposes its own per-tab models first,
so by the time `disposeTrackedModels` iterates them they all hit the
`model.isDisposed()` skip and the back-reference is never cleared.
Result: every per-tab model leaks a full sqlEditorLogic graph each
unmount.

Null the back-reference before `m.dispose()` so the Monaco-side GC
actually releases the kea graph it pinned.

Validation on a 5-cycle /home <-> /sql SPA workload, vanilla kea:

| metric                       | before | after |
| ---------------------------- | ------ | ----- |
| detached elements (post-GC)  | 1418   |   599 |
| total BuiltLogic instances   |  177   |   135 |
| sqlEditorLogic instances     |    5   |     2 |

Matches the headline reduction the reverted #56758 plugin achieved
(1369 -> 549 detached, 5 -> 2 instances per logic), without touching
kea or risking the listSelectionLogic stale-subscription crash that
motivated the revert.
commits.author: pauldambra

commits.message:
refactor(monaco): extract clearLogicReference helper alongside initModel

Address qa-swarm review:

- Convergent finding (paul + xp): the back-reference set/clear pair was
  asymmetric — `initModel(model, logic)` had a name; the inverse was an
  inline `(m as any).codeEditorLogic = undefined` cast at two call sites
  (sqlEditorLogic.beforeUnmount and CodeEditor.disposeTrackedModels).
  Hoist a `clearLogicReference(model)` helper next to `initModel`,
  hiding the `as any` cast in one place and giving the operation a
  name that pairs with `initModel`.

- The 9-line explanatory comment in `sqlEditorLogic` collapses to its
  load-bearing point now that the helper carries the intent.

- Add a symmetric note to `disposeTrackedModels` pointing out that
  owners of their own models must call `clearLogicReference` before
  disposing, since `disposeTrackedModels` skips already-disposed
  models — making the contract greppable from either side.

No behaviour change.
commits.author: pauldambra

commits.message:
chore(monaco): trim comments, lock down clearLogicReference behaviour with tests

Replace the prose explaining why callers must clearLogicReference before
dispose with a unit test that fails if model.dispose() ever stops being
non-clearing.
commits.author: pauldambra

commits.message:
chore(sql-editor): replace unit test with integration lock-down on beforeUnmount

The unit test on the helpers passed even if the actual fix was reverted —
it never exercised sqlEditorLogic.beforeUnmount. Swap it for a logic-level
test that mounts the logic, injects fake tracked models, unmounts, and
asserts the back-reference was cleared and dispose was called.
commits.author: pauldambra

commits.message:
docs(hogli): correct Chrome cookie flush behavior in metabase:login

Earlier docs and the in-CLI status hint claimed "close the Metabase tab to
force Chrome to flush cookies." Verified against Chromium source — that's
wrong. Per `sqlite_persistent_cookie_store.cc`, Chrome's `kCommitInterval`
is 30s and is flushed only by that timer (or after 512 batched ops).

shutdown.

The honest UX is: wait. The CLI already polls every second up to a
3-minute timeout, so cookies appear automatically within 30s of SSO.
Update the in-CLI status note and the skill to reflect this and explicitly
say closing the tab does NOT help.

Pull the duplicated `Stage` wrapper and the inline `buildTheme()` calls
out of the four existing hog-charts story files into a shared

title: fix(ci): rebuild canary on synchronize when handle_comment is skipped
author: haacked

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body: ## Pull request overview Fixes the canary-flags enable workflow so that pushing new commits to a PR with an active canary (`pull_request: synchronize`) correctly triggers the heavy `build_and_enable` job, even when `handle_comment` is skipped. **Changes:** - Updates `build_and_enable` job gating to opt out of the implicit transitive `success()`/skipped chain via `!cancelled()`. - Re-asserts direct dependency success via `needs.preflight.result == 'success'` while still gating on `needs.preflight.outputs.should_proceed == 'true'`. --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

commits.message:
fix(ci): allow build_and_enable on synchronize when handle_comment is skipped

A plain `if:` on `needs.preflight.outputs.should_proceed == 'true'` does not
override GitHub Actions' implicit `success()` chain check. On
`pull_request: synchronize`, `handle_comment` is skipped (gated to
`issue_comment`), `preflight` runs and succeeds via its own `!cancelled()`
clause, but `build_and_enable` inherits the chain-skipped status and is
silently skipped before `should_proceed` is ever evaluated. Result: pushing
to a PR with an active canary did not rebuild and redeploy.

Add `!cancelled()` to disable the implicit chain check, plus an explicit
`needs.preflight.result == 'success'` so we still require a green direct
dependency.

quarantine state, and a 30-day stability sparkline.

Backend
  - GET .../repos/<id>/baselines returns the full universe (capped at 5000
    most recently active) plus aggregate totals over the universe so stats
    and unfiltered facets stay correct under truncation.
  - One grouped query each for tolerate counts (30d/90d), active quarantines,
    and the per-day result buckets that feed the sparkline.
  - 12 tests covering universe resolution, truncation, count windows,
    quarantine expiry, sparkline buckets, totals, browser metadata.

Frontend
  - One scene fetch on mount; all filtering / faceting / search done
    client-side via kea selectors. URL hash carries the filter state so the
    view is shareable.
  - Card grid is virtualized (react-window v2 already in deps) so 5000-card
    payloads stay smooth.
  - Inline-SVG sparkline (~30 lines) — Chart.js per card was a non-starter
    even virtualized.
  - Stat tiles double as filter presets via LemonSegmentedButton.
  - Faceted sidebar (TYPE / AREA / STABILITY) recomputes counts dynamically
    over the filtered set (except for the dimension being faceted, so picking
    a TYPE doesn't zero out other TYPE rows).
  - parseIdentifier helpers map Storybook story IDs onto PostHog product
    areas (Insights, Dashboards, Components, ...).

Stacks on feat/visual-review-history-detail (PR #56868) — PR for this
targets that branch and rebases onto master once it merges.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): polish snapshots overview after design review

- Theme picker is Light|Dark only — no neutral state. Picking a side dedups
  paired light/dark variants; identifiers without a theme suffix always show.
- Stat tiles repositioned as a clean bordered grid (the LemonSegmentedButton
  warped multi-line content). Three slices now: All / Tolerated drift /
  Currently quarantined. The frequently-tolerated count surfaces as a small
  inline "X frequent" chip on the Tolerated tile instead of its own slice.
- Both Tolerated and Quarantined sort by recent_diff_avg desc. Added the
  field to BaselineEntry — computed alongside the sparkline aggregation, so
  zero extra queries.
- Sort label visible at the toolbar right ("Sorted by drift avg (high → low)").
- Card borders fixed: Tailwind's `border` was inheriting Link's
  currentColor (orange), painting every card with a primary-colored frame.
  Now `border border-border`.
- Thumbnails: dropped the checkered placeholder and aspect-ratio frame.
  Pixelhog caps thumbnails at 200×140, so a fixed-height top-aligned box is
  enough — content shows at its natural pixel ratio.
- Facet hover used `bg-fill-tertiary` which is too close to the page bg to
  read; switched to `bg-primary-highlight`.
- Area parser dropped the curated AREA_TOKENS table. Now: skip
  `scenes-app` / `components` wrappers, take the next token, glue the next
  one when it's a known multi-word head (`error`, `data`, `feature`, …).
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): close right-edge dead band on snapshots grid

The grid was leaving roughly (cols-1) × CARD_GAP of empty space on the
right edge — I was subtracting the gap budget twice. The card-cell wrapper
already pads its right side internally (paddingRight: CARD_GAP), so the
column width should consume the full container. Drop the gap subtraction
from the columnWidth calc.

Same pass:
  - Sidebar reorder: Stability first (the actionable facet for this view),
    then Type, then Area.
  - Toolbar: Clear all + sort label group on the right together — was sat
    awkwardly between the theme picker and the sort indicator.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
feat(visual-review): repo-scoped URL structure with Runs / Snapshots tabs

Following the DataWarehouse-Source pattern: every working URL lives inside
a repo workspace, and an index scene picks the repo at the entry.

Routes:
  /visual_review                                   → VisualReviewIndexScene
  /visual_review/repos/:repoId/runs                → Runs tab (was /visual_review)
  /visual_review/repos/:repoId/snapshots           → Snapshots tab (was already there)
  /visual_review/runs/:runId                       → run detail (unchanged)
  /visual_review/repos/:repoId/:runType/snapshots/:identifier → history detail

The index scene loads the team's repos and replace()s into the only
repo's Runs page when there's exactly one (the >99% case). Multi-repo
teams see a small picker. Zero-repo teams see a CTA pointing at Settings.

Tab strip (Runs / Snapshots) is shared and rendered inside both the Runs
and Snapshots scenes, scoped to the active repo. Settings stays a gear
button in the header — keeping the strip strictly per-repo and avoiding
mixed-scope tabs.

Backend:
  - list_runs gains an optional repo_id filter so the per-repo Runs tab
    shows only that repo's runs.

Notable details:
  - urls.visualReviewRuns() still returns /visual_review (the entry) so
    sidebar/nav callers don't change. New urls.visualReviewRepoRuns(id)
    points at the repo-scoped page.
  - Breadcrumb chain on the per-repo scenes: Visual review → repo full
    name → tab name.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): smooth out snapshots overview header + grid

Tabs vanished and reloaded on every navigation because each scene owned its own loadRepo. A new keyed visualReviewRepoLogic holds the repo (and the sibling list) so both scenes connect to the same instance — no flicker, one fetch.

The repo switcher moves into the scene title actions as a plain LemonMenu dropdown; only renders when the team has more than one repo. /visual_review now always replace-redirects to the first repo's runs (no picker page in the normal flow), and the picker UI is reduced to the empty state.

Snapshots overview drops react-window in favor of a plain CSS grid. The internal scroll plus page scroll caused two scrollbars and a tall empty band below the grid; with lazy-loaded thumbnails the cost of rendering up to the 5000-cap is fine. The tag legend at the bottom (which users had to scroll through 250 cards to find) is removed.

Smaller bits: Refresh moves down next to the segmented review-state buttons; action buttons use size="small" to match the switcher; breadcrumbs collapse to a single scene crumb so the back arrow doesn't appear pointing at a no-op redirect.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): move legends + count to top of snapshots overview

The colour legend and "sparkline shows last 30 days" hint sat below the grid, so users had to scroll past hundreds of cards to find them. Both move into a slim row above the grid. The result count joins the sort label in the toolbar instead of duplicating below.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message: chore: update OpenAPI generated types
commits.author: tests-posthog[bot]

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): polish snapshot grid + history navigation

- SnapshotCard: pull both corner badges through a shared base style
  (`BADGE_BASE`). Quarantine and tolerate badges were a circle vs a
  capsule before, which read as broken alignment when both were present.
  Now: same height, same min-width, same padding, same font weight.
- Snapshot history breadcrumbs: insert a `Snapshots` row pointing at the
  repo's grid. The chain was `Visual review > {identifier}`, which sent
  the back nav up to `/visual_review` — that auto-redirects to the runs
  tab, not the grid. Now: `Visual review > Snapshots > {identifier}`.
- Render `VisualReviewTabs` on the snapshot history scene with
  `Snapshots` active, so the repo-level Runs/Snapshots tab strip is
  visible inside identifier detail. Without it there's no in-page route
  back to the grid once you click into an identifier.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): refresh away from filter, tabs at depth

- VisualReviewRunsScene: push the Refresh button to the right of the
  segmented filter via `ml-auto`. It was sitting flush next to the
  active-tab handle and read like another filter option.
- VisualReviewRunScene: render `VisualReviewTabs` so the repo workspace
  nav stays visible inside run detail. Going from the runs list into a
  run otherwise stranded users with no in-page route back to the grid
  (or the runs list itself) — same fix the snapshot history scene just
  got. `activeKey="runs"` since the run is reached via that tab.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): scope review-state counts to the active repo

The Runs tab pill showed `Needs review (1)` while the table sat empty.
Counts were team-wide, the list was repo-scoped — so any other repo on
the team that had a matching run would inflate the badge for every repo
it didn't belong to.

Plumb `repo_id` through `get_review_state_counts` and the `counts`
viewset action; frontend now passes `props.repoId` on the loadCounts
call. Counts and list now scope to the same set.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): keep title above the tab strip on detail scenes

Putting `VisualReviewTabs` ahead of `SceneTitleSection` swallowed the
title in the rendered scene shell. The runs/snapshots overview scenes
already render title-first; matching that order on run detail and
snapshot history brings the title back.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): drop unchanged rows before deduping baseline history

`result=unchanged` rows were inflating the timeline. Each capture gets
its own Artifact row even when the diff says it matches baseline —
pixel jitter changes the bytes, blake3 of the bytes is the
content_hash, content_hash keys the Artifact. So consecutive unchanged
runs have *different* current_artifact_ids and slip past the
LAG-on-current_artifact_id dedup, each painted as a fake baseline
event.

Observed on prod for `scenes-app-data-management-comments--comments`
on the PostHog repo: 895 unchanged + 2 changed rows on master, 6
distinct current_artifact_ids but only 2 distinct baselines. Timeline
showed 99 entries, all "No-op", and the dark variant pairing fell
apart because the unchanged rows on either side didn't line up by
run_id.

Filter changes from `result <> 'new'` to
`result IN (changed, removed, new)`. Same as `<> 'unchanged'`
semantically, written explicitly so the next reader doesn't have to
re-derive the rule. Including `new` again so first-capture identifiers
get an initial entry in their timeline (the original belt+braces
exclusion was redundant with `status=completed`).

Same identifier post-fix: 1 entry per theme, both on the same
commit/run — pairing now lines up cleanly.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
test(visual-review): align history seed with the new unchanged-row filter

Two seeded master rows used the default `result=UNCHANGED` and relied
on the dedup-on-artifact path to collapse. Under the new filter those
rows are dropped before they reach LAG, so the test asserted entries
that no longer exist. Flip the seed to `CHANGED` so the same scenario
(two runs sharing an artifact) actually exercises the dedup, and add
an explicit `UNCHANGED` row to lock in that those don't survive the
filter — that's the prod bug this fix targets.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): unbreak sparkline result match for mypy

mypy treats the values_list `result` field as `str` and the
`SnapshotResult` enum members in the tuple as the enum type, so the
`elif result in (SnapshotResult.CHANGED, ...)` branch never narrowed —
flagged as unreachable. StrEnum compares equal at runtime, but the
type-system view is what mypy enforces. Compare against `.value`
(plain strings) so the branch types match.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): address PR review feedback on overview

UUID parsing
  Bare `UUID(repo_id_param)` raises `ValueError` on bad input, surfacing
  as a 500. Wrap it in `_parse_optional_uuid` that raises DRF's
  `ValidationError` so the framework returns a 400 with a clean payload.
  Applied at both `runs.list` and `runs.counts` query-param sites.

Truncation totals
  `universe_identifiers` was built from the truncated slice and reused
  for the universe-scope aggregates — `recently_tolerated`,
  `frequently_tolerated`, `currently_quarantined`, `by_run_type` could
  all undercount silently once a repo crossed 5000 identifiers. Now
  we keep the per-entry aggregates scoped to the loaded slice (we only
  need them for entries we'll return) and pull a separate
  `full_universe_identifiers` distinct query for the totals. Same trick
  on `quarantined_id_count` (re-query under truncation) and
  `by_run_type` (aggregate query under truncation).

Sparkline cross-run-type bleed
  Sparkline + drift dicts keyed only on `identifier`, but the universe
  is one row per `(run_type, identifier)` — same identifier across
  storybook + playwright would merge their stability data and reuse it
  on every entry. Re-keyed both dicts by `(run_type, identifier)` and
  updated the facade to look up by the composite. Public `BaselineEntry`
  contract unchanged.

Sparkline cutoff off-by-one
  `now - DAYS days` pulls rows from a 31st earlier date that has no
  matching `day_key`; those rows would disappear into a never-read
  bucket but their `diff_percentage` still skewed `recent_diff_avg`.
  `DAYS - 1` aligns with `_build_sparkline_day_keys`.

`_SparkBuckets` boundary
  The facade reached into `logic._SparkBuckets` for a zero-default —
  technically allowed, but a smell. Renamed to `SparkBuckets` (public)
  with a docstring saying "this is the one symbol the facade is meant
  to import." `import-linter` doesn't enforce facade → logic-internals
  today (only presentation → facade), so this is style not safety.

Frontend filter dedup
  `filterExcept` in `facetGroups` re-implemented the same six-clause
  filter chain that lived in `filteredEntries`. Extracted
  `applyFilters(entries, filters, exclude?)` shared helper; a new
  filter dimension only needs to be added in one place now.

Accessibility
  `aria-pressed` on `SnapshotFacetSidebar` rows and `SnapshotStatRow`
  tiles. Both behave like single/multi-select toggles but the on-state
  was visual-only.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
refactor(visual-review): nest run list + counts under repos

Move the two list-shaped run endpoints under the repos router so the
filter is path-positional instead of a query param:

  GET /repos/{repo_id}/runs/             # was /runs/?repo_id=
  GET /repos/{repo_id}/runs/counts/      # was /runs/counts/?repo_id=

Run-by-id actions stay flat (`/runs/{id}/...`) — direct links by run id
keep working without forcing repo_id into the path. Same split we used
for the snapshot history rework.

Drops the `_parse_optional_uuid` helper since `repo_id` now comes from
the URL kwarg, which Django parses (the bare `UUID()` 500 path is gone).
Frontend swaps to the regenerated `visualReviewReposRunsList` /
`visualReviewReposRunsCountsRetrieve` clients. CI clients are
unaffected (they hit `POST /runs/` and `/runs/{id}/...`, both flat).
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): unbreak CI on overview branch

Two follow-ups from the last batch:

- mypy still flagged `result in (SnapshotResult.X.value, ...)` as
  unreachable. mypy treats the StrEnum members as a different type
  than the `str` it sees from `values_list("result")`, even via
  `.value`. Use plain string literals — equivalent at runtime, simple
  for the type system.
- `DecoratedEntry` was a local type but the kea-typegen output for the
  overview scene logic re-imports it. Export it so the generated
  `*LogicType.ts` resolves.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): rewrite sparkline result check to dodge mypy

mypy keeps flagging `result in {literal, ...}` as unreachable on this
branch — same complaint with `.value`, with `frozenset`, with plain
literals. Likely django-stubs is narrowing `result` to a specific
Literal further upstream than I can spot. Invert the test to
`!= "unchanged"` so mypy only has to compare a `str` to a string
literal — unambiguous and equivalent (the four `SnapshotResult` values
are all that can land here, and `unchanged` is the only clean one).
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): suppress mypy unreachable on baseline-event arm

Whatever django-stubs is doing, mypy narrows `result` to
`Literal["unchanged"]` after `.values_list("result", ...)` — both
`result in {...}` and `result != "unchanged"` were flagged unreachable.
Restructure so the `unchanged` branch is the explicit elif and the
baseline-moving arm is the (mypy-confused) `else`, with a localised
`# type: ignore[unreachable]` and a comment explaining what's going on.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): coerce sparkline result through str() for mypy

mypy's narrowing on the `result` element of `values_list("result", ...)`
swings between Literal subsets in either direction depending on the
elif structure — both `result == "unchanged"` and `result != "unchanged"`
got flagged unreachable in turn. `str(result)` is opaque to the type
narrower and lets the four-way classify branch as written.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(visual-review): widen tolerated_hash_match_id for sparkline classify

The actual root cause of the unreachable error: `values_list("tolerated
_hash_match_id", ...)` returns a FK id which django-stubs types as a
plain `UUID` rather than `UUID | None`, even though the underlying
field is nullable. mypy then thinks `tol_match_id is not None` always
succeeds, which makes everything after it unreachable.

Annotate the unpacked value as `UUID | None` to widen back to reality
and drop the previous `str(result)` workaround that was treating the
wrong column. Verified with `dmypy run` locally.
commits.author: webjunkie

title: perf(hog-charts): move crosshair from DOM overlay to canvas
author: sampennington

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Low-risk frontend perf optimization — moves crosshair rendering from a DOM overlay to the canvas draw pass. Logic is equivalent and well-guarded; no data, API, or security concerns.

commits.message:
perf(hog-charts): move crosshair from DOM overlay to canvas

The crosshair was rendered as a React-managed absolute-positioned div
that subscribed to ChartHoverContext and re-rendered on every mousemove.
At higher data sizes the per-event style/layout invalidation it forced
became a measurable contributor to hover frame time (~60% of the
hog-vs-chartjs frame-wait gap in the chart-bench harness at 100K points).

Move the crosshair into the existing hover-overlay canvas pass so hover
indication stays entirely on canvas — the same architecture used by
Chart.js, ECharts, and other high-performance charting libraries.
DefaultTooltip, AxisLabels, and ReferenceLines remain in the DOM as
they need rich content or focusable UI.

the right onboarding nudge: install PostHog Code at posthog.com/code

author: vdekrijger

reviews.author: github-actions
reviews.body: Well-targeted bug fix: replaces `update_or_create` in the layout-only code path with a safe `filter().first()` + skip pattern, eliminating the 500 caused by a failed INSERT against the CHECK constraint. Both bot concerns (race condition and test parameterization) were addressed in the diff. Security scoping is correct — filter requires both `dashboard=instance` and `dashboard__team_id=instance.team_id`.

commits.message:
fix(dashboards): skip unknown tile ids in layout PATCH instead of 500

The display-only branch of `_update_tiles` (handling `layouts`, `color`,
`deleted`, etc.) used `update_or_create`, which silently fell through to
INSERT when the tile id+dashboard pair did not match an existing row. The
INSERT carried no insight/text/button_tile FK, so it tripped the partial
`dash_tile_exactly_one_related_object` CHECK constraint and raised an
unhandled IntegrityError, returning a generic 500.

Switch this branch to a `find-then-update` pattern that never inserts a row.
Unknown tile ids (cross-dashboard kea contamination, hard-deleted tiles,
races with concurrent edits) are now silently skipped with a structured
warning, so the rest of the layout payload still saves.

author: TueHaulund

reviews.author: fasyy612
reviews.body: Couldn't see anything glaring, LGTM!

commits.message:
feat(signals): replace per-tick cap with cityHash64 sample rate

The summarization sweep no longer caps dispatch at 10 sessions per tick.
A `sample_rate` in `[0, 1]` on `SignalSourceConfig.config` is now the
per-team throttle. Sampling is pushed into the recordings query's HAVING
clause via cityHash64 so the decision is stable across ticks and the
sweep is one ClickHouse round trip.

The stuck-rasterize visibility query is inverted to scope by team and a
2h CloseTime window — without the cap, the previous candidate-ID IN
clause could blow past Temporal's query string length limit.
commits.author: TueHaulund

commits.message:
feat(signals): default sample_rate=0.1 for new session-analysis configs

Newly created `SignalSourceConfig` rows for session_replay /
session_analysis_cluster get `sample_rate=0.1` injected by the serializer
unless the caller provided one. Stops the runtime fallback in
`coerce_sample_rate` (1.0) from being load-bearing for new teams.
commits.author: TueHaulund

commits.message:
fix(signals): bound per-tick child fan-out and tighten sample_rate guards

Three small refinements from code review:

- Cap concurrent `start_child_workflow` calls per tick at
  `CHILD_DISPATCH_BATCH_SIZE = 100`. The single `asyncio.gather` over
  every sampled candidate could put the 5-minute workflow execution
  timeout at risk for teams running at high sample rates over a large
  candidate set.
- Reject `bool` in `coerce_sample_rate`. The serializer already does
  this, but `isinstance(True, int)` would let `float(True) == 1.0` slip
  through any non-API write path.
- Freeze time and assert the resolved `CloseTime` cutoff substring in
  the stuck-rasterize visibility-query test, so a regression that
  produces a malformed cutoff would actually fail.
commits.author: TueHaulund

commits.message:
fix(signals): align runtime sample_rate default with serializer default

`coerce_sample_rate` returns this when the config is missing `sample_rate`
(legacy row, raw ORM, future migration). Aligning it to 0.1 matches the
serializer's create-time default so write/read paths agree.

fix(llma): memoize dashboardLogic in reload action to avoid stale store path

LLMAnalyticsReloadAction called dashboardLogic({id: selectedDashboardId || 0})
unmemoized on every render. When selectedDashboardId changes (tab switch,
dashboard deletion), the previous dashboardLogic.<id> path is unmounted, but

the old store path and Kea throws "Can not find path".

dashboardLogic instance per selectedDashboardId, with a stable fallback
instance for id=0, so useValues/useActions bind to a stable reference and
the unmount happens cleanly.

reviews.body:
## Pull request overview Adds a configurable fallback for resuming cloud runs without relying on Modal filesystem snapshots (needed for EU), by resuming from the last git checkpoint and ensuring the backend can surface prior-run artifacts/logs needed for resume. **Changes:** - Introduce `TASKS_USE_MODAL_RESUME_SNAPSHOTS` (default off in EU) and gate snapshot creation/usage accordingly. - Add resume-chain walking in the Tasks API for artifact downloads and log retrieval (concatenated oldest→newest). - Add unit tests covering resume-chain walking (artifacts + logs) and snapshot gating behavior. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 8 out of 8 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | products/tasks/backend/api.py | Walk resume chain for artifact lookup and concatenate logs across resume ancestors. | | products/tasks/backend/models.py | Strip stale snapshot ids during cloud handoff when snapshots are disabled; add instrumentation logs. | | products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/workflow.py | Add inactivity timeout override and gate resume-snapshot creation behind the new flag. | | products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/provision_sandbox.py | Ignore `snapshot_external_id` when flag is off; add resume decision logging. | | products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/create_resume_snapshot.py | Add start log for snapshot creation activity. | | posthog/settings/temporal.py | Define `TASKS_USE_MODAL_RESUME_SNAPSHOTS` (EU default off) and `TASKS_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. | | products/tasks/backend/tests/test_api.py | Add tests for resume-chain artifact download and logs concatenation behavior. | | products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/tests/test_workflow.py | Add tests for snapshot gating in finally block and for respecting the modal-resume flag during provisioning. |

title: fix(llma): skip judge evaluation when source trace errored
author: richardsolomou

commits.message:
fix(llma): skip judge evaluation when source trace errored

When an `$ai_generation` event has `$ai_is_error=true`, there is no
meaningful output for the LLM judge to score. Previously the judge ran
against an empty Output and tended to return spurious verdicts (often
`true`) — for example a "Relevance" eval would mark a failed 401 trace
as relevant.

Short-circuit `execute_llm_judge_activity` when the source trace
errored: return `verdict=False` (or `verdict=null, applicable=false`
when N/A is allowed) with explanatory reasoning, and mark the result
`skipped` so the workflow does not charge the team's trial quota for
an evaluation that never made an API call.

commits.message:
fix(llma): use pytest.mark.parametrize and drop error counter

`parameterized.expand` does not pass pytest fixtures through to async
test functions, so the new errored-trace tests failed in CI with
`missing 1 required positional argument: 'setup_data'`. Switch to
`pytest.mark.parametrize`, which integrates with fixtures correctly.

Also drop the `increment_errors("trace_errored_skipped")` call: skipped
evaluations are not failures, and counting them under `llma_eval_errors`
inflates error-rate dashboards. Workflow-level SKIPPED status emitted
by the metrics interceptor already provides the necessary visibility.

- Drop `model` and `provider` empty strings from the skipped result so

fix(llma): accept snake_case Gemini usage metadata

The bug-reporter's traces come through posthog-python, which forwards
Gemini usage metadata via .to_dict() / vars(). Both convert protobuf
field names to snake_case, so production events arrive with
prompt_tokens_details / candidates_tokens_details / cache_tokens_details
and { modality, token_count } entries — not the camelCase form the
Vercel AI SDK uses on Node.js.

Our extractor only looked at camelCase keys, so the entire Gemini
extraction silently no-op'd for Python users. The transcription
customer's audio tokens never made it into $ai_audio_input_tokens, the
billing pipeline saw no modality data, and the audio rate never
applied.

Add tolerant key lookup (camelCase OR snake_case) for every Gemini
metadata key the extractor walks: promptTokensDetails /
prompt_tokens_details, candidatesTokensDetails /
candidates_tokens_details, cacheTokensDetails / cache_tokens_details,
and the modality entry's tokenCount / token_count. OpenAI's shape is
already snake_case via Pydantic model_dump(), unchanged.

Tests: snake_case input modality, snake_case output modality, snake_case
cache modality, full-shape Gemini event with all three; integration test
in process-ai-event.test.ts now uses snake_case to mirror the actual
production payload from posthog-python.

reviews.body: ## Pull request overview Updates the canary-enablement workflow to use a GitHub App installation token (instead of the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`) for org team membership checks so `/pr-canary`, manual label authorization, and `workflow_dispatch` actor validation can correctly verify membership in org-private teams. **Changes:** - Add `actions/create-github-app-token` steps using `GH_APP_POSTHOG_ASSIGN_REVIEWERS` credentials. - Route team membership checks in `actions/github-script` steps through the app token. - Update failure messaging to reference the GitHub App’s org permissions rather than `GITHUB_TOKEN`. --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. commits.message:
fix(ci): use github app token for canary team membership checks

The /pr-canary command and other canary-flags workflow team membership
checks were calling github.rest.teams.getMembershipForUserInOrg with
the default GITHUB_TOKEN, which only has repo-scoped permissions and
cannot read org-private team memberships. The API returns 404 in that
case (rather than 403), and the catch block treats 404 as 'not a
member' — so legitimate members of team-feature-flags or
team-flags-platform got 'Not a member of an authorized team'.

Use actions/create-github-app-token with the GH_APP_POSTHOG_ASSIGN_REVIEWERS
app credentials (already used by auto-assign-reviewers.yml for org-team
operations) and pass the resulting token to each github-script step
that performs a team membership check. Also update the misleading
error messages so future failures point at the app's permissions
rather than GITHUB_TOKEN.
