commits.message:
fix(visual-review): make snapshot history return real baseline events

Snapshot-history queries on prod returned 1093 rows for one identifier on
master where the actual baseline content only changed 5 times. The page was
both capped at 15 (so users saw 1.4% of the noise wall) and full of duplicates
when uncapped. Three concrete causes:

- pre-classification rows leaked through. `result` defaults to NEW on upload
  and is only finalised when the run completes; runs stuck in pending/processing
  left ~21% of the rows pointing at NULL artifact ids
- steady-state spam — every master commit on an unchanged identifier created
  another `result=unchanged` row pointing at the same `current_artifact_id`.
  one artifact accounted for 553 rows in the test case
- the 15-cap from `[:limit]` happened *before* DRF pagination, so the
  client-side `limit=100` was a no-op

Now `get_snapshot_history`:

- filters `run__status=COMPLETED` and excludes `result=NEW`
- collapses adjacent rows sharing `current_artifact_id` so the timeline
  reflects baseline-content changes, not raw run rows
- drops the DB-side slice; views' `paginate_queryset` actually paginates

Master/main is still hardcoded as the default-branch fallback. Repos use one
or the other in practice; when `trunk`/`develop` shows up this becomes a `Repo`
field. Real EXPLAIN against the 37M-row snapshot table is 7 ms via the existing
`run_branch_type_current` + `unique_snapshot_identifier_per_run` indexes — no
migration needed.

Frontend meta strip: with dedup the `history.length - 1` count is the actual
number of baseline updates, and the tail of the list is genuinely the first
capture (was wrong on truncated pages).

Also: `seed_snapshot_history` now raises `CommandError` on missing repo so the
exit code reflects failure.

commits.message:
refactor(api): extract project_id/environment_id path params into components

drf-spectacular inlines path parameters into every operation that uses them.
``project_id`` alone shows up ~1100 times in the generated spec, with byte-
identical ``schema`` and ``description`` each pass. ``environment_id`` adds
another ~440. Repeating the same blob 1,500+ times bloats the spec and lights
up vacuum's ``description-duplication`` rule for the same reason — we have a
DRY problem the spec format already has a fix for.

This commit hoists the two stable, hardcoded path params into
``components.parameters`` and replaces inline copies with ``$ref``. Equivalent
output for downstream codegen (Orval inlines refs when emitting zod), spec
shrinks from 7.6 MB → 7.1 MB (~6%), and ``description-duplication`` drops
from 7165 → 5568 findings (~1600 of those were these two params alone).

Why only these two: they're already hardcoded in the postprocess hook with
fixed schema and description (see _SHARED_PATH_PARAMS). Other path params
like ``id`` come straight from drf-spectacular's per-resource introspection
(integer vs UUID, varying descriptions per resource), so they aren't safe to
hoist without losing precision. Query params like ``limit``/``offset``/
``search`` sometimes vary per endpoint too. Keep the extraction surgical.

Two consumers of ``frontend/tmp/openapi.json`` needed updates to handle
parameter refs:

1. ``filterSchemaByOperationIds`` (tools/openapi-codegen) didn't preserve
   ``components.parameters`` in the filtered output — it stripped them
   entirely. Operations with ``$ref`` parameters then had unresolved refs,
   and Orval's zod generation hung in an infinite loop trying to resolve
   them. Fix: walk collected refs, copy referenced parameter components
   into the filtered output, and recurse into any schema refs they carry.

2. ``generate-tools.ts`` reads ``parameter.in`` and ``parameter.name``
   directly. After this change those return ``undefined`` for ref entries,
   silently breaking the ``project_id``/``organization_id`` auto-resolved
   omit. Fix: deref parameter refs at load time so the rest of the script
   sees fully resolved parameter objects.

Net generated MCP tool output is byte-identical to before this change.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
refactor(api): also extract organization_id path param into components

Completes the auto-resolved set: project_id + environment_id +
organization_id are all path params resolved by TeamAndOrgViewSetMixin
and generate-tools.ts already groups them together as autoResolvedParams.
Same shape across all 79 inline copies (1 description, 1 schema), so
extraction is safe.

Side benefit: drf-spectacular was emitting organization_id without a
description, generated TS just had ``organization_id: zod.string()``.
Now it carries the canonical description so codegen consumers know the
field's purpose.

Spec size: 7.12 MB → 7.11 MB (small additional win on top of the previous
~480 KB shrink). description-duplication count unchanged because the
prior inline parameters had no ``description`` field — the descriptions
are net new, deduplicated to once in components.parameters.

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): seed source form defaults at runtime

The new-source form's defaults were computed inside `forms()` from
`props.availableSources`, but kea evaluates the builder once at logic
build time — at which point `props({})` still has `availableSources`
undefined. `buildKeaFormDefaultFromSourceDetails` short-circuits to
`{}`, so the form never received defaults like MySQL `using_ssl="true"`,
ClickHouse `secure`/`verify`, or Vitally region. The select dropdown
showed "Yes" as a visual fallback while form state was empty, so the
required-field validator fired "Please select a use ssl?" on submit.

Seed defaults from `selectConnector` listener instead, mirroring the
hog functions pattern (`hogFunctionConfigurationLogic.tsx` resets the
form from `templateToConfiguration(template)` after data loads). Build-
time defaults are now an empty literal; the `=== undefined` guard
preserves user edits, OAuth-restored values, and URL-handler writes.
commits.author: MarconLP

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): also seed defaults from setInitialConnector

Address review feedback on #56863:
- Extract seeding into a `seedConnectorDefaults` module-level helper
  and call it from both `selectConnector` and `setInitialConnector`
  listeners. Preselect flows (NewSourceScene initialSource prop,
  SourcesModal) hit `setInitialConnector`, which previously bypassed
  the seeding.
- Collapse the per-key dispatch loop into a single
  `setSourceConnectionDetailsValues` call (one validator pass instead
  of N).
- Drop redundant `as any` / `as Record<string, any>` casts.
- Add four `seedConnectorDefaults` unit tests covering the empty,
  partially-filled, fully-filled, and null-connector cases.
commits.author: MarconLP

commits.message:
refactor(data-warehouse): align source form defaults with hog functions pattern

Replace the imperative seedConnectorDefaults helper with a selector +
named action, mirroring how hogFunctionConfigurationLogic computes form
defaults from loaded data:

- New selector defaultSourceConnectionDetails — derives form defaults
  from values.selectedConnector via buildKeaFormDefaultFromSourceDetails.
- New action resetSourceForm — single entry point that fills the form.
  selectConnector and setInitialConnector listeners both delegate to
  this; any future "connector context changed" path can route through
  the same action without re-discovering the seeding requirement.
- resetSourceForm listener uses kea-forms resetSourceConnectionDetails
  (REPLACE) layered with OAuth-restored values and the URL-set
  access_method, instead of the per-key non-clobbering merge loop.
- urlToAction no longer hand-rolls savedValues restoration; it's owned
  by the resetSourceForm listener.
- Drop seedConnectorDefaults helper, getInitialSourceConnectionDetailsValues
  (now unused), and their tests.

Same defaults pattern applied to sourceSettingsLogic — its build-time
defaults call also returned empty payload (props.availableSources is
not populated at logic build time). ConfigurationTab continues to seed
real defaults at runtime via its useEffect; no behavior change.

commits.message:
chore(data-warehouse): trim form-defaults comments

build-time props.availableSources call). Trim to one line each that

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): preserve saved access_method across OAuth redirect

The previous refactor flipped the priority: URL-provided access_method
clobbered the saved one. Since the OAuth callback URL doesn't carry
access_method forward, a user who picked direct mode and OAuth-ed away
would come back in warehouse mode.

Restore the original priority — saved values win — by reordering the
spread in resetSourceForm. Extract the merge into a pure
`mergeRestoredSourceFormValues` helper and reinstate the access_method
priority tests that the previous commit dropped along with the
deleted `getInitialSourceConnectionDetailsValues` function.
commits.author: MarconLP

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): widen form defaults type to fix CI typecheck

The empty `defaults: { prefix: '', description: '', payload: {} }`
literal made TypeScript infer a narrow form value type, which broke
every downstream read of fields like `access_method`, `payload.host`,
`cdc_management_mode`, `auth_method`, etc.

Pre-refactor, defaults came from `buildKeaFormDefaultFromSourceDetails`
which returns `Record<string, any>` — that wide type was load-bearing
for the rest of the codebase. Restore the cast on the empty literal.

Same change in `sourceSettingsLogic.ts` for the parallel form.

commits.author: MarconLP

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): thread access_method through resetSourceForm

The previous fix put `setSourceConnectionDetailsValue('access_method', accessMethod)`
after `selectConnector` in `urlToAction`. Because kea listeners run synchronously
inline, the listener-driven restore of saved form state (including
access_method) ran first, and the subsequent setValue call clobbered the
restored access_method with the URL fallback. On the OAuth callback URL —
which doesn't carry access_method forward — that meant a user who'd picked
direct mode would land back in warehouse mode.

Pass accessMethod through `selectConnector` → `resetSourceForm` as an action
arg so the URL value flows directly into the merge step, with no round-trip
through form state and no implicit ordering between dispatches.

commits.message:
fix(api): emit valid OpenAPI 3.0 for $ref + sibling, lint default vs enum

Two related spec correctness fixes:

1. $ref siblings are illegal in OpenAPI 3.0 (the spec mandates $ref be the
   only key in the object). drf-spectacular's own emission honors this by
   wrapping refs in allOf, but our Pydantic-side fixer in
   _fix_pydantic_schema_for_openapi flattened Optional[$ref] into
   {"$ref": ..., "nullable": true} and let bare-ref-with-description through
   unchanged. Vacuum and other strict OpenAPI 3.0 linters rightly flag this.

   Wrap any $ref that ends up with siblings in allOf so the siblings
   (description, default, nullable, etc.) live legally on the parent.
   Generated TypeScript improves materially — unions that were being flattened
   into merged enum maps now emit as proper TS unions.

2. Add lint_spec_consistency_hook as a postprocessing hook that emits
   drf-spectacular warnings for spec self-inconsistencies:
   - default not a member of enum (catches the funnel_window_interval_type
     "days" vs ["DAY", ...] bug class)
   - required field missing from properties
   - $ref with sibling keys (defense-in-depth alongside the fix above)

   The warnings flow through GENERATOR_STATS so --fail-on-warn (already
   enabled in `hogli build:openapi-schema`) catches them in CI.
commits.author: webjunkie

commits.message:
fix(api): clean up vestigial $ref siblings + redundant allOf wrappers

Vacuum's strict OpenAPI 3.0 lint surfaced two more shape issues left over
after the $ref-sibling fix landed; same fixer, three small additions:

1. Drop ``minimum``/``maximum``/``exclusive*`` siblings from wrappers whose
   only content is ref-only combinators (allOf/oneOf/anyOf full of $refs).
   drf-spectacular emits these on ``IntegerChoices`` fields (carrying the
   integer field's range alongside the enum ref). The ref'd component
   already encodes the allowed values, so the bounds at this level are
   meaningless — vacuum's ``oas-schema-check`` rightly flags them.

2. Collapse ``{"allOf": [{"$ref": "..."}]}`` to just the ref when there's
   nothing else worth wrapping for. Once the vestigial bounds are stripped
   the wrapper becomes pointless — vacuum's ``no-unnecessary-combinator``
   was right.

3. Drop the over-eager allOf wrap on ``anyOf`` entries: a bare ``$ref``
   inside an ``anyOf`` array is legal alone, the sibling-restriction only
   applies to siblings on the same JSON object.

Also extend the postprocess pass to walk parameter and requestBody schemas
in operations — same shape issues surface there but the components-only
walk missed them.

Net vacuum score: ``oas-schema-check`` 24 → 0, ``no-unnecessary-combinator``
284 → 0. Generated TypeScript improves accordingly (math/property unions
emit as proper TS unions instead of merged enum maps).

fix(api): emit root tags array, replace empty additionalProperties with true

Two more vacuum findings cleaned up at the source:

1. ``operation-tag-defined`` (2962 findings → 0): operations declared tags
   like ``experiments`` / ``feature_flags`` etc. but the OpenAPI spec had no
   root-level ``tags`` array declaring them. We already collected ``all_tags``
   for ``x-tagGroups``; now also emit the standard ``tags`` array so the spec
   is self-consistent.

2. ``oas-missing-type`` for empty ``additionalProperties: {}`` (~120 findings
   eliminated): drf-spectacular emits ``{}`` to mean "any type" but vacuum's
   ``oas-missing-type`` rule trips because the inner schema has no ``type``.
   Boolean ``true`` is the spec-blessed equivalent and lints cleanly.

(oas-schema-check 24 → 0, no-unnecessary-combinator 284 → 0,
operation-tag-defined 2962 → 0, oas-missing-type 1197 → 1075).

commits.message:
fix(api): address reviewer feedback on openapi consistency lint

Five fixes from PR review on the consistency lint and the schema fixer:

1. ``type: \"null\"`` is not valid OpenAPI 3.0. The all-null ``anyOf`` branch
   in ``_fix_pydantic_schema_for_openapi`` was emitting it — exactly the
   class of bug this PR fixes everywhere else. Now emits
   ``{\"enum\": [None], \"nullable\": True}`` which is OAS 3.0 valid and
   tells consumers precisely what to expect (null only).

2. The ``default ∈ enum`` lint only checked when ``enum`` was a sibling of
   ``default``. After the ``\$ref+sibling → allOf`` rewrite, enums almost
   always live in the referenced component (not on the same node), so the
   lint was effectively cosmetic. Now follows ``\$ref`` and ``allOf``
   branches to find the referenced enum before checking membership.
   Also suppresses the false positive on nullable-enum patterns
   (``default: null`` is fine when ``nullable: true`` or ``oneOf:
   [..., NullEnum]``).

3. ``\$ref + allOf`` coexistence no longer overwrites. Previously the
   sibling-wrap step replaced any pre-existing ``allOf`` with a
   ref-only list; now it prepends the ref instead. drf-spectacular
   shouldn't produce this combination, but the fixer is defensive
   elsewhere — should be here too.

4. The ``required vs properties`` lint check is now skipped on composed
   schemas (``allOf``/``oneOf``/``anyOf`` present). A flat lookup would
   false-positive when ``required`` is satisfied through a referenced
   branch — exactly what would have blocked legitimate composed-schema
   changes in CI.

5. The operation-level fixer walk now also covers
   ``responses.*.content.*.schema``. Today every response schema is a
   ``\$ref`` (so the components-only walk catches them), but inline
   response schemas added later would silently bypass the fixer —
   the lint hook would fire in CI rather than the fix being applied.

All five raised by automated reviewers (Copilot, Codex, Greptile) on
the parent PR. Zero new lint warnings against the current spec.

author: MattBro

reviews.author: fercgomes
reviews.body: left some nits

commits.message:
fix(integrations): use sandbox developer secret for stripe sandbox installs

Persist is_sandbox on the Integration record at OAuth time so downstream
Stripe API calls (refresh_access_token, write/clear_posthog_secrets,
account-name lookup) authenticate with the correct developer secret. Live
installs use STRIPE_APP_SECRET_KEY, sandbox installs use
STRIPE_APP_SANDBOX_SECRET_KEY. Previously the post-OAuth flow always used
the live secret; for sandbox installs this silently failed (caught by a
broad except that only logged a warning), so Stripe Apps Secret Store
was never populated and the Stripe app frontend showed Not connected
even after a successful OAuth.

- Use strict identity check (`is True`) instead of `bool()` for the
  is_sandbox flag so a malformed string write fails closed to live.
- Reuse `OauthIntegration.oauth_config_for_kind("stripe", is_sandbox=...)`
  inside `_stripe_client` to inherit its missing-secret guard
  (NotImplementedError when STRIPE_APP_SANDBOX_SECRET_KEY is unset)

Per greptile review feedback. The `is_sandbox` strict-identity check
appeared inline in OauthIntegration.refresh_access_token and as the
body of StripeIntegration.is_sandbox. Extracted to a module-level
helper so the rule lives in one place and a future migration to a
dedicated column is a single-line change.

fix(integrations): swallow NotImplementedError in _stripe_client

If sandbox env vars are unset on a sandbox install, oauth_config_for_kind

title: feat(duckling): route backfill through duckgres pgwire
author: fuziontech

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body: ## Pull request overview Routes the duckling backfill DAG through each org’s duckgres (pgwire) service instead of running DuckDB in-process, decoupling the Dagster image’s DuckDB/DuckLake version from customer catalogs and removing client-side attach/credentials/retry complexity. **Changes:** - Introduces a psycopg-based `_connect_duckgres()` connection factory using shared duckgres conninfo generation. - Migrates backfill helpers from `duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection` to `psycopg.Connection`, updating exception handling and parameter binding. - Removes in-process DuckDB connection setup and client-side retry loops/tests, relying on duckgres server-side attach + conflict retries. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | posthog/dags/events_backfill_to_duckling.py | Switches all DuckLake operations from in-process DuckDB to psycopg/pgwire duckgres connections; removes attach/cross-account plumbing and local conflict retries. | | posthog/dags/test_events_backfill_to_duckling.py | Updates/removes unit tests that depended on in-process DuckDB; retains identifier-validation-focused tests with mocks. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

commits.message:
feat(duckling): route DuckLake backfill through duckgres pgwire

Replace in-process duckdb with psycopg connections to each org's duckgres
server. Duckgres auto-attaches the DuckLake catalog on connection and
configures cross-account S3 access server-side via IRSA, so the DAG no
longer needs `attach_catalog`, `configure_cross_account_connection`,
`_connect_duckdb`, or the in-process retry loops for DuckLake transaction
conflicts (duckgres handles those server-side via retryOnConflict).

Removes the duckdb/ducklake version coupling between the Dagster image
and the customer duckling — each duckling owns its duckdb/ducklake pair.

Net -454 LOC; 72 unit tests pass.

title: chore(mcp): generate OAUTH_SCOPES_SUPPORTED from posthog/scopes.py
author: MattBro

reviews.author: joshsny
reviews.body: much better, what about scoped that are added between a django and mcp deployment?

commits.message:
chore(mcp): generate OAUTH_SCOPES_SUPPORTED from posthog/scopes.py

The MCP server's protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728) advertises
`scopes_supported` from a hand-maintained array in
`services/mcp/src/lib/constants.ts`. The authorization server's metadata
is computed dynamically by Django from `posthog.scopes.get_scope_descriptions()`.

Both lists must agree, but they have drifted twice in the past two weeks:

- `llm_skill:read/write` was added to the MCP list ahead of the Django
  deploy, breaking sign-in until the revert in #55300.
- `introspection` lived in the MCP list as a typo (it is the OAuth Token
  Introspection endpoint per RFC 7662, not a grantable scope), causing
  #55307. Removed in #56833.

Spec-compliant clients (e.g. Claude Code) read `scopes_supported` from the
resource metadata and pass every entry to `/oauth/authorize`. If the
resource list contains a scope the AS does not recognize, the AS rejects
with `?error=invalid_scope` and sign-in is unrecoverable from the client.

This change makes `OAUTH_SCOPES_SUPPORTED` derive from the same source the
Django AS uses, eliminating the drift class:

- `bin/build-mcp-oauth-scopes.py` imports `posthog/scopes.py` (via
  importlib, so no Django setup needed) and writes
  `services/mcp/src/lib/oauth-scopes.generated.ts`.
- The generated file is committed so PR diffs show scope changes
  explicitly to reviewers.
- `services/mcp/src/lib/constants.ts` re-exports `OAUTH_SCOPES_SUPPORTED`
  from the generated module; call sites are unchanged.
- The script runs as `build:openapi-mcp-scopes` inside the existing
  `hogli build:openapi` pipeline, with `posthog/scopes.py` registered as
  a trigger so editing scopes auto-prompts regeneration.

After this, adding a scope on the Django side and forgetting the MCP
side is no longer possible. `hogli build:openapi` regenerates both,
and CI will fail on uncommitted regen output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: MattBro

commits.message:
chore(mcp): factor get_oauth_scopes_supported() into posthog/scopes.py

Extract the `OIDC + get_scope_descriptions().keys()` pattern from
`posthog/api/oauth/views.py` into a single helper in `posthog/scopes.py`,
then have both the AS metadata endpoint and the MCP codegen consume it.
Removes the duplicate `oidc_scopes = ["openid", "profile", "email"]`
literal that was sitting in two places.

Generator hardening:
- AST-walk `posthog/scopes.py` before importing it and reject any
  non-stdlib import. The importlib bypass of `posthog/__init__.py`
  silently breaks the moment scopes.py picks up an in-package
  dependency; this fails loudly at codegen time instead.
- Wrap `sys.modules` registration in try/finally so the side-channel
  module name does not leak if the script is ever imported.
- Match the AS metadata's unsorted insertion order rather than
  alphabetising; makes byte-for-byte comparisons during incident
  debugging straightforward.
- Reword the "MUST be a subset" framing in the generated header to
  attribute the requirement to OAuth client behavior, not RFC 9728
  (the RFC permits subset, it does not mandate it).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: MattBro

commits.message:
chore(mcp): hide user_interview_DO_NOT_USE scope from OAuth metadata

The scope is intended for manually issued personal API keys only, but it
was leaking through `get_scope_descriptions()` into the AS
`scopes_supported` and (with this PR) into the MCP protected-resource
metadata. Add `OAUTH_HIDDEN_SCOPE_OBJECTS` for "PAT-allowed but
OAuth-hidden" and filter it from `get_oauth_scopes_supported()`. PAT
validation paths use `get_scope_descriptions()` directly and are
unaffected — humans can still paste the scope into a token.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: MattBro

commits.message:
chore(mcp): allow __future__ in scopes codegen import allowlist

`from __future__ import annotations` is a compile-time directive with no
runtime side effects, so it doesn't conflict with the importlib bypass
of `posthog/__init__.py`. Add to `ALLOWED_IMPORT_ROOTS` so a maintainer
adding it to `posthog/scopes.py` doesn't get a misleading "non-stdlib
import" error from the codegen guard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: MattBro

title: fix(mcp): remove 'introspection' from OAUTH_SCOPES_SUPPORTED
author: MattBro

commits.message:
fix(mcp): remove 'introspection' from OAUTH_SCOPES_SUPPORTED

`introspection` is the OAuth 2.0 Token Introspection endpoint (RFC 7662),
already advertised correctly as `introspection_endpoint` in AS metadata
(RFC 8414). It is not a grantable scope.

Spec-compliant MCP clients read scopes_supported from the protected
resource metadata and pass every entry to /oauth/authorize. The auth
server then rejects with ?error=invalid_scope, breaking sign-in.

Reproduction:

  comm -23 \
    <(curl -s mcp.posthog.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource \
        | jq -r '.scopes_supported[]' | sort) \
    <(curl -sL mcp.posthog.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server \
        | jq -r '.scopes_supported[]' | sort)
  introspection

After this change, the diff is empty and the OAuth handshake completes.

Closes #55307.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: MattBro

Looks solid overall — clean separation between parsing and rendering, and the test matrix is thorough. A couple of small follow-ups:

**Suggestions**

1. `ConversationMessagesDisplay.test.tsx:123` — now that `arguments` includes `| null`, the `null as unknown as Record<string, unknown>` cast (and the comment justifying it) can be replaced with a plain `null`.
2. `ConversationMessagesDisplay.tsx:495` — the `'function' in item` check is redundant alongside `item.function && typeof item.function === 'object'`. Dropping it tightens the guard without changing behavior.

**Questions**

1. For `args.kind === 'empty'`, we render the header with no body and no "no arguments" affordance. Was that an explicit UX call, or worth a subtle hint so it's clear the call truly took no args (vs. a render failure)?

The LLM analytics docs example for $ai_output_choices recommends

chore(admin): address review feedback on schema repartition page

- Type partition format choices via PartitionFormat (typing.get_args), so the
  dropdown picks up new formats automatically.
- Drop the implicit "datetime" fallback when partition_mode is unset. The

  to datetime)". The fallback messaging was misleading.

  without a reset mixes old and new layouts in the same Delta table and
  corrupts the data — operators shouldn't be expected to remember.

  schedule's OnlyOne overlap policy and can race with regular runs; pausing

commits.message:
fix(admin): set reset_pipeline on sync_type_config, not workflow input

Activity retries within a single workflow re-read the original workflow
input on every attempt. Passing `reset_pipeline=True` there made every
retry call `handle_reset_or_full_refresh`, which wipes Delta files and
clears the incremental cursor — so a retry after a worker shutdown or
heartbeat timeout always restarted from 0 rows.

Mirror the pattern used by the existing /resync API: write
`reset_pipeline=True` to `schema.sync_type_config` and pass `None` on
the workflow input. The pipeline pops the flag after the first reset,
so subsequent retries see `reset_pipeline=False` and resume from the
saved cursor.

title: fix(integrations): use sandbox secret for Stripe sandbox installs
author: MattBro

reviews.author: fercgomes
reviews.body: Stamping to unblock, but this feels very hacky, do we have a better way of handling the sandbox?

commits.message:
fix(integrations): use sandbox secret for Stripe sandbox installs

Stripe issues separate client_id AND client_secret pairs for live vs sandbox
installs of the same app. The previous PR (#56614) only added the sandbox
client_id; the token exchange still authenticated with the live secret, which
Stripe rejects with `invalid_grant: Authorization code provided does not
belong to you` whenever the code was minted by the sandbox flow.

Two changes:

1. `oauth_config_for_kind` now returns the sandbox secret when `is_sandbox=True`.
   Adds `STRIPE_APP_SANDBOX_SECRET_KEY` env var; raises `NotImplementedError`
   if sandbox is requested but either the client_id or secret is unset.

2. `integration_from_oauth_response` retries the token exchange with the
   sandbox config when the first attempt returns the "does not belong to you"
   marker error. This handles marketplace-initiated installs (the
   `/integrations/stripe/confirm-install` flow) where there is no `is_sandbox`
   signal in the redirect from Stripe.
commits.author: MattBro

commits.message:
fix(integrations): also guard retry on sandbox client_id

The retry guard in `integration_from_oauth_response` only checked
`STRIPE_APP_SANDBOX_SECRET_KEY`, but `oauth_config_for_kind("stripe",
is_sandbox=True)` requires *both* sandbox client_id and secret. If the
secret was set without the client_id, the retry would raise
`NotImplementedError("Stripe sandbox not configured")` and mask the
original Stripe OAuth error with a 500.

Adds `STRIPE_APP_SANDBOX_CLIENT_ID` to the retry condition and a test
covering the secret-set-but-client-id-missing case.

commits.message:
feat(data-warehouse): connection-string parsers for every released DB source

Add per-source connection-string parsers so MySQL, MSSQL, Snowflake, and
ClickHouse get the same paste-and-go UX that Postgres and Redshift already
have. The frontend now dispatches by source name to a dedicated parser per
source, with each parser owning its own URL schemes, default ports, and
field nesting (Snowflake fills auth_type.password.{user,password},
ClickHouse derives `secure` and the right default port from the URL
scheme, MySQL emits `using_ssl` from `?ssl=...`).

Generated-By: PostHog Code
Task-Id: 20a3de37-2c08-40b9-a360-befcb46eb06f
commits.author: PostHog Code

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): preserve snowflake auth selection when URL has no password

Previously the snowflake connection-string parser unconditionally pushed
`auth_type.selection = 'password'` plus the nested user/password fields,
even when the URL had no password. A user who already had keypair auth
configured and pasted a URL just to grab `account_id`/`warehouse` would
silently lose their keypair selection.

Only emit the `auth_type.*` fields when the URL actually carries a
password — otherwise leave the existing form selection alone.
commits.author: MarconLP

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): use family-aware port when overriding clickhouse secure flag

Pasting `http://...@host/db?secure=true` previously inferred port 9440
(native TLS) regardless of the original scheme family, so a user who
typed an HTTP-family URL ended up on a native port. Track each scheme's
family (http vs native) and pick the same-family canonical port when
the secure flag is flipped:

- http ↔ https → 8123 / 8443
- clickhouse ↔ clickhouses → 9000 / 9440
commits.author: MarconLP

commits.message:
chore(data-warehouse): document mysql ssl=preferred → using_ssl mapping

`ssl=PREFERRED` is a distinct MySQL mode (try SSL, fall back to plaintext)
that doesn't map cleanly onto our binary `using_ssl` flag. Add a comment
explaining why we round it up to `true`: secure-by-default beats a silent
downgrade, and a server that can't speak SSL will fail loudly so the user
can flip the toggle off.
commits.author: MarconLP

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): write Snowflake auth fields at flat form paths

The form Group for `auth_type` is flat: option sub-fields render
directly under it as `auth_type.user` / `auth_type.password`, matching
the `SnowflakeAuthTypeConfig` schema. Writing to
`auth_type.password.user` / `auth_type.password.password` left the
required username unset and clobbered the password slot with an object,
causing credential validation to fail on paste.
commits.author: MarconLP

commits.message:
chore(data-warehouse): tighten ParsedField.value to string

Every parser already returns string values (ports use String(), bools
use 'true' / 'false'). Narrowing the type self-documents the contract
and prevents future parsers from accidentally returning non-strings.
commits.author: MarconLP

commits.message:
feat(data-warehouse): accept JDBC-style Snowflake URLs in parser

Snowflake connection strings show up in two shapes: the canonical
SQLAlchemy/dlt form (`snowflake://user:pw@account/db/schema?warehouse`)
and a JDBC-influenced form that puts credentials, database, and schema
in query params. Fall back to the query-param shape when userinfo and
pathname don't carry them, so paste-to-fill works for either. Userinfo
and pathname still win when both are provided.

  flush interval if waiting stalls

commits.message:
feat(hogli): add metabase:databases and metabase:query commands

Adds discovery and query commands so agents never handle raw session cookies
and never hardcode Metabase database IDs (which drift when the metadata DB
is rebuilt).

- metabase:databases --region <r> — lists id/name/engine from /api/database
  so callers can discover the current ClickHouse or Postgres DB IDs at call
  time rather than trusting hardcoded values in docs/skills.
- metabase:query --region <r> --database-id <n> — reads SQL from stdin or
  --file, hits /api/dataset internally using the cached cookie, emits TSV
  (default) or JSON. --save <path> writes to disk to avoid piping large
  result sets through terminals or agent transcripts. The cookie never
  appears in stdout.
- Skill updated to instruct agents to use metabase:query (never
  metabase:cookie, which leaks the session header into transcripts).
  Hardcoded DB IDs removed from the skill in favor of "always run
  metabase:databases first".
commits.author: andyzzhao

commits.message:
fix(hogli): address review comments on metabase commands

- Cookie and --save output files are now written atomically at mode 0600
  via a shared `_secure_write` helper, closing the TOCTOU window where
  `write_text` + `chmod` briefly left them world-readable (flagged by
  hex-security and greptile as P1).

  `metabase:login`, so callers always pick US or EU explicitly.
- Deduplicate a trivially duplicated status string in

  the poll loop don't break the test with a `StopIteration`.
- Add test coverage for `--save` mode 0600 and the new required

commits.message:
perf(hog-charts): split hover from static layer onto a separate canvas

Hover used to repaint the entire chart on every mousemove because
hoverIndex was a dep of the single useChartDraw effect. At 100k×10
that meant ~1M lineTo calls per hover frame — hover latency scaled
linearly with point count and reached ~1.5s for a 30-move sweep.

Splits the canvas into:
- a static layer (grid, lines, areas, points) — redrawn only when
  scales/series/labels/dimensions/theme change
- an overlay layer (highlight rings) — redrawn only when hoverIndex
  changes

Also caches the (x, index) hit-test table once per (labels, scales)
change instead of rebuilding it on every mousemove.

Measured on the chart-bench scene: raw hog-charts at 10 series ×
100k points dropped from ~1.5s/30-move sweep to ~420ms (close to the
~240ms rAF floor). No measurable change for small datasets where
the static redraw was already cheap.

Internal API: Chart now takes drawStatic + drawHover instead of a
single draw callback. Only LineChart consumes that surface — no
external callers affected. Public LineChart props are unchanged.

title: fix(data-warehouse): surface real Stripe credential errors
author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): surface real Stripe credential errors

Two related UX bugs caused customers with valid Stripe permissions to see
misleading error messages when connecting Stripe as a data source:

1. validate_credentials() lumped every per-resource exception into
   StripePermissionError. An invalid/expired API key (401) thus surfaced
   as "lacks permissions for ALL 13 resources" — pushing users to grant
   permissions they already had. Now distinguishes 401 (raises new
   StripeAuthenticationError, short-circuits the loop) from 403
   (still per-resource permission gap).

2. OAuth token-exchange failures raised a bare Exception, which DRF
   turned into a 500 with no `detail` field — the frontend toast then
   fell back to a generic "Something went wrong". Now raises
   ValidationError with the provider's `error_description` extracted
   from the response body, and tolerates non-JSON error bodies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): include Invoice items perm + show Stripe error per resource

Following up on the previous Stripe credentials fix:

1. The pre-filled API key creation link and the in-app permissions doc
   omitted Invoice items. Stripe treats `rak_invoice_item_read` as a
   distinct scope from `rak_invoice_read`, so following our docs
   verbatim still produced a 403 on /v1/invoiceitems. Added the scope
   to the prefill list and to the help caption.

2. The per-resource permission failure now includes the underlying
   Stripe error message, not just the resource name. A customer hitting
   a missing scope now sees the literal Stripe response (e.g. "this
   account is not currently set up for Connect"), which makes the gap
   actionable instead of guesswork.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): trim Stripe permission error to resource list

When all failing resources are clean stripe.PermissionError (403), the
resource name alone tells the customer which scope to enable on Stripe.
Including Stripe's full error string (request id, status, headers, body)
just bloats the toast — a customer missing one scope was getting a
multi-line dump for a problem with a one-word answer.

Now: clean 403s render as a plain resource list. Only fall back to the
verbose underlying error when a resource failed with a non-permission
exception (network, rate limit, schema mismatch) where the cause isn't
obvious from the resource name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: danielcarletti

commits.message:
fix(data-warehouse): split Stripe permission errors from unknown errors

A permission denial (403) and an unknown failure (network, schema drift,
rate limit) are different problems with different fixes, but both were
being raised as StripePermissionError — which forced the user-facing
message to either dump every Stripe error verbatim or hide the cause of
non-permission failures behind a misleading "missing permissions" toast.

Now: validate_credentials tracks the two classes in separate dicts and
raises a distinct exception for each. StripePermissionError carries
clean 403s and renders as a plain resource list. New StripeValidationError
carries unknown errors and surfaces the underlying Stripe message,
folding any collected 403s into the same toast for one-shot reporting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
